title: Stetson Bennett IV seems to be ready to serve as Matthew Stafford's understudy
summary: Two years ago, with Rams backup quarterback Jimmy Garoppolo due to miss the first two games of the regular season because of a PED suspension, the Rams weren't sure Stetson Bennett IV was ready to serve as the understudy to Matthew Stafford.
full_text: Two years ago, with Rams backup quarterback Jimmy Garoppolo due to miss the first two games of the regular season because of a PED suspension, the Rams weren’t sure Stetson Bennett IV was ready to serve as the understudy to Matthew Stafford. With Garoppolo gone and rookie first-rounder Ty Simpson still learning the ropes, Bennett seems to be ready to be one play away from playing for the Rams. Bennett had a solid outing in the Rams' 34-0 preseason win over the Saints, completing 19 of 31 passes for 181 yards and scoring two rushing touchdowns. "I think he’s getting better and better," Rams coach Sean McVay told reporters after the game. "I think part of it is the overall command. I thought he made some really good decisions. I thought he got through some progressions. Then I love the fact that he used his legs. . . . [H]e did a great job. I thought he got an opportunity to be able to really showcase a lot of his skills. Huge credit to [quarterbacks coach] Dave Ragone too. I think those two guys were really in sync and it was fun to watch.” The only caveat is that, in three prior seasons, Bennett hasn't taken a single snap in a game that counts. He's had to develop exclusively in preseason games. "We talk about it all the time, and you guys have heard me say it, repetition is the mother of learning," McVay said. "[Bennett] has been intentional about applying those reps and you can feel like his teammates, they enjoy him. He's an easy guy to be able to root for. He's just got a nice swag and a nice presence and especially like what we asked earlier, you feel his game really comes to life in game day settings. The gamer thing, he's just got a good feel and it's not too big. He loves competing and it's fun to watch him do it.” The lone caveat came when Bennett held the ball out for the pylon and risked fumbling through the end zone. The ruling on the field that Bennett hadn't scored was reversed to a touchdown. "We'll learn from reaching the ball out on the end zone even though I challenged that and it worked out for us," McVay said. "We want to make sure that we don't leave ourselves susceptible to getting a fumble in those types of situations where it goes to a touchback." It's a small point, one that won't take anything away from the fact that, even though the Rams have no quarterback other than Stafford with regular-season playing experience, Bennett is ready to fulfill the obligation of replacing Stafford, if the need should arise this season.
author: Mike Florio

title: CeeDee Lamb's house was burglarized while the Cowboys were in Oxnard
summary: With the Cowboys spending training camp in Oxnard, some homes of the players were left unattended.
full_text: With the Cowboys spending training camp in Oxnard, some homes of the players were left unattended. One of those homes was robbed. Via the Fort Worth Star-Telegram , citing The Spit Bucket Podcast , one or more thieves absconded with more than $300,000 in property from the home of receiver CeeDee Lamb on July 30. A worker noticed a broken window at the property the next day. The stolen property includes four luxury bags. No suspects have been identified to date. In recent years, crime rings have targeted pro athletes, given that their travel schedules are well known. Usually, that means the day and time for a road trip or a home game. For the Cowboys, it means an annual extended stretch where the entire operation relocates to California for training camp.
author: Mike Florio

title: Patriots rookie QB Behren Morton fills in at punter, then throws game-winning TD
summary: As a rookie seventh-round draft pick, Patriots quarterback Behren Morton is no lock to make the 53-man roster.
full_text: As a rookie seventh-round draft pick, Patriots quarterback Behren Morton is no lock to make the 53-man roster. But he helped his chances in multiple ways in Saturday's preseason game. Morton did his most important job by playing well when running the offense late in the game, throwing the game-winning 37-yard touchdown pass in the final minute. But Morton also showed he can be counted on in a pinch by punting very well after the Patriots' regular punter, Bryce Baringer, left the game because he wasn't feeling well. In Baringer's absence, Morton punted three times for a 44.3-yard average. "Tonight was fun. I wasn't expecting to punt. It's been since high school since I've punted. You've just got to make the most of your opportunity when it comes, so I tried to do that tonight," Morton said. "Coach came up to me and just said, 'If we've got to punt on this drive you're going out there.' I went over to the net, hit a few balls. I asked [long snapper Julian Ashby], 'How far do I need to stand back?' He told me 15 yards, catch the ball and then just put it down there." Morton, who never punted in college but did it in high school, said that on his first punt, he was taken aback by how close it came to getting blocked, but he was able to get it off. "In high school, they didn't rush that fast," Morton said. "So the first rush kind of threw me by surprise." Morton showed good command of the offense late in the game, completing 13 of 17 passes for 129 yards and that game-winning touchdown. If he makes the roster, that's why. But his ability to work as a fill-in punter doesn't hurt.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jayden Daniels makes a three-play cameo for Commanders at Lions
summary: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels made his preseason debut on Saturday.
full_text: Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels made his preseason debut on Saturday. If you blink, you may have missed it. Daniels got the start and handled one drive. It was a three-and-out that netted one yard. In the three plays that Daniels was on the field, he was 0-for-1 passing and suffered a 10-yard sack. Sam Hartman and Athan Kaliakmanis, a seventh-round rookie from Rutgers, played quarterback after Daniels. Backup Marcus Mariota is currently out with a knee injury. He's expected to miss the rest of the preseason with an MCL sprain. The Commanders play the Ravens next weekend before opening the regular season at Philadelphia.
author: Mike Florio

title: Shedeur Sanders didn't appreciate the booing of Deshaun Watson
summary: There was a theory that quarterback Deshaun Watson got his preseason start last week because the game was not being played in Cleveland.
full_text: '' There was a theory that quarterback Deshaun Watson got his preseason start last week because the game was not being played in Cleveland. If that was a reason for the decision, it was a good one. Watson was booed in his first home appearance for the Browns since tearing an Achilles tendon during the 2024 season. After the game, quarterback Shedeur Sanders expressed disagreement with the verbal disapproval of Deshaun. “Yeah, I mean, in general, I don’t appreciate that at all," Sanders said, via the transcript distributed by the team. "Regardless of competition, we’re all human beings. I think we all need to understand that. In this room too, we’re all humans. I don’t do things to humans that I wouldn’t want done to me. I don’t like making people feel uncomfortable in different spaces, and that’s why, even in daily things I do, I try to make sure everybody’s comfortable. Because I know sometimes just being who I am can make people uncomfortable. I’m aware of that. "For all the fans, we appreciate you showing up, and however you feel about the situation with Deshaun and everything, I think it’s more about a bigger purpose and it’s respect. It’s a respect thing that I feel should be there, because we’re all out there trying to do our best and serve the franchise the best way possible. We’re going out there to win games, doing everything we can. So I don’t really appreciate that.” It's a reasonable position, but it may not be very realistic when it comes to professional sports. The anonymity of a crowd makes it easier to boo, and those who pay for tickets feel entitled (and they arguably are) to voice their displeasure. Watson arrived a year after twenty-plus lawsuits were filed against him for alleged misconduct during massage-therapy sessions. The Browns gave up a treasure trove of draft picks to get him, before giving him a five-year, $230 million, fully-guaranteed contract. He served an eleven-game suspension right out of the gates. If he'd performed well, and if the team had won games, it would have been fine. Injuries and unimpressive performances magnified the negatives created by the overall situation. While Deshaun was on the wrong end of the boos, he wasn't the only target. Browns fans are, and should be, upset with everything about the acquisition and compensation of a player who has never delivered on the promise of what arguably has become the single worst transaction of the salary-cap era, if not of all time.
author: Mike Florio

title: Joe Brady: Ed Oliver's absence is related to an injury, not his personal tragedy
summary: The Bills and defensive tackle Ed Oliver had decided not to announce that Oliver's young son had died in late June.
full_text: The Bills and defensive tackle Ed Oliver had decided not to announce that Oliver's young son had died in late June. The news was reported on Friday. It forced the Bills to acknowledge it on Saturday . After Saturday's preseason game, coach Joe Brady addressed the situation. “I'm a parent, right?" Brady told reporters. "And ever since I found out, it's really hard and I can't fathom what he's going through. There’s really not words to describe it. As a coach, as a father, it's my job to be what he needs right now, and that's loving him and giving him the privacy that he deserves. Whatever it looks like, no matter how someone might want to handle it, it's however he wants us to handle it, and go through it." The apparent justification for reporting the development before Oliver or the Bills could announce it arose from the perception that the Bills possibly were attributing his absence from the team to a phantom injury. "[H]e's not here right now because of an injury and he’s dealing with that," Brady said. "This wasn't the reason why he's not here, but it's unfortunate, the way that it came out, but I respect a lot of you guys and you might have known about it, and [the way you] handled it. That’s part of journalism as well, but I appreciate your guys' hearts and understanding the human elements of it. It’s hard. You know, it's hard when I see him and I can't imagine. I haven't had the words since, and I don't really have the words, but all I can do is just be there for him . . . in whatever way that he needs.” In situations like this, everyone has to make a decision as to whether the details of a player's personal tragedy will be reported before the player is ready to share them. The problem is that, even if every other reporter who knew about it decided to give Oliver the time and space to announce it on his own, it only takes one to decide to handle it differently. That's what happened here. Absent evidence that it's anything more than a personal tragedy, it's hard to justify going there. Which perhaps explains the attempt to make the news relevant by suggesting that the Bills weren't being truthful about Oliver's absence. Regardless of whether Oliver actually is injured.
author: Mike Florio

title: Todd Monken closes in on his quarterback decision
summary: Sunday's review of Saturday's game film could lead to a winner.
full_text: '' The clock is ticking, and midnight has nearly arrived for Todd Monken. The Cleveland quarterback decision is coming soon. Perhaps as soon as Sunday. “At some point I’m going to have to decide, right?" Monken told reporters after Saturday's preseason game against the Bills. "I’m saying it kind of jokingly. At some point we’ve got to get that guy the reps, so I’m not going to paint myself into a corner. Optimally, you’d like to give one player all of the reps and you know who the one is, and we’ve done the best we could as a staff trying to work through this. Like at any position." Monken made it clear that he plans to watch the film on Sunday and then talk to the coaching staff. A review of the entire picture is necessary to understand why things didn't go well, on the occasions when they didn't go well. "I was looking at things live, and everybody had a hand in it," Monken said. "I already know, looking at it and watching, we had too many issues with us, that had nothing to do with them. We’re playing some guys who just got with us, but alignment, assignment and communication, Browns hurting Browns, really. You’re not going to have a chance when that happens." The final drive, handled by third-stringer Dillon Gabriel, was a particular disaster. In one three-and-out effort, the Browns had three false starts, pushing them all the way to a third-and-25. "[A]t the end, it was like, really?" Monken said. "That was some shitty football. I don’t care who goes out there. If I could have taken a knee, I probably would have. I mean, what the shit? I don’t know what to tell you." The first-year hea coach told the world plenty in his praise of Sanders's ability to control the game with a strong cadence. "We work on cadence and operation, and we’re going to continue to do it, because you can’t be leading the offense when you’re not leading the cadence," Monken said. "In the first half we did, we had a shot. We got them to jump offside, we wanted to take a shot and we jumped, and we had another time we could’ve tapped. We got them in the neutral zone. That’s one thing Shedeur’s going to continue to get better at. We had a chance on third-and-12 to take a shot, he has to see the flag down, we checked it down but didn’t convert on third-and-eight. We were really good at cadence in the first half, but at the end there, it’s not good enough." As to Watson, Monken's comments made it even more clear that, even though signs recently were pointing to the veteran as the starter, the tide has perhaps started to turn — sharply. "I was disappointed for us collectively that we didn’t play well offensively [under Watson], I’ll just put it that way," Monken said. "We had to get back on track a bunch. It happened in the first game. When you’re behind the chains, it’s hard. It’s just hard. You can’t force the defense into certain looks [when you] put yourself behind the chains. "I’ll have to wait to see the tape, but I’m proud of the way he’s worked to get to where he’s at, and that’s part of it. Right? I know you’ve asked him, 'Hey, how it feels to get booed?' It’s a pretty easy question, it sucks. I don’t want to get booed. It comes with the territory. You don’t want to get booed? Let’s play good football. Let’s play good at quarterback, on offense and as a team, and then you won’t have to worry about all that, because it can turn just like that. Win, play good football, and everybody will be fine." As to the booing Watson, it's more complicated than playing well. The fans were already wired to boo him, for reasons unrelated to his current level of play. The entire circumstances of his arrival and ongoing presence on the roster point to Browns fans being poised to boo him. The boos could be heard when Watson took the field in the third quarter, even though the stands seemed to be largely empty. They booed him after the first drive of the second half. The boos were consistent, and unrelated to his play. Watson said it himself . The boos weren't about his performance. If he's the starter in Week 3, he'll hear it all day long — unless the Browns somehow upset both the Jaguars and Buccaneers on the road to start the season. There will be plenty of subjectivity and discretion when the time comes to pick a starter between Sanders and Watson. If it's close for Monken, the fact that the customers have made their position loud and clear will make Sanders the only right answer.
author: Mike Florio

title: Eagles RB Ja'Quinden Jackson has full movement, CT scan was negative
summary: Ja'Quinden Jackson's agent offered good news on the Eagles running back's health after a scary incident on the opening kickoff Saturday night.
full_text: Ja'Quinden Jackson's agent offered good news on the Eagles running back's health after a scary incident on the opening kickoff Saturday night. Damien Butler of CMV Sports said in a statement that Jackson is "awake, has full movement and use of all four limbs, and his CT scan came back negative." "Tonight, above everything else, we thank God that Ja'Quinden is doing well after what was an incredibly frightening moment," Butler said. "What happened tonight was frightening for everyone who witnessed it, and we are extremely grateful to the Philadelphia Eagles medical staff and all of the first responders who acted quickly and took great care of Ja'Quinden in those critical moments." Jackson dove at the legs of Patriots running back Lan Larison while trying to make a tackle and took a knee to the head. Jackson was knocked out, and both arms went into the fencing position. Medical personnel immediately began work on Jackson before he was placed on a backboard and then a stretcher and placed into an ambulance, which took him to a local hospital for evaluation. Butler did not indicate whether Jackson remains in the hospital and/or whether he will fly home with his teammates.
author: Charean Williams

title: Harrison Butker makes a 69-yard FG on final play of first half
summary: Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker kicked a 69-yard field goal on the final play of the first half Saturday night.
full_text: Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker kicked a 69-yard field goal on the final play of the first half Saturday night. Butker and the Chiefs celebrated as if it was an NFL record . . . and it would have been had it been the regular season. Jaguars kicker Cam Little kicked a 68-yard field during a Nov. 2, 2025, game against the Raiders to set the record. Little had a 70-yard field goal as time expired against the Steelers in the 2025 preseason. Butker's kick cleared the crossbar by a few yards. He also had field goals of 45 and 58 yards in the first half as the Chiefs lead the Bucs 9-0 at halftime.
author: Charean Williams

title: Josh Allen is "very, very sad and angry" with how news of Ed Oliver's son passing emerged
summary: The news came out on Friday before the Bills or the DL announced the death of Oliver's 2-year-old.
full_text: Many were aware that Bills defensive tackle Ed Oliver's young son died earlier this summer. The vast majority of those who knew decided to wait for the Bills or Oliver to announce the development when they were ready to do so. The news came out on Friday before the Bills or Oliver announced it. Bills quarterback Josh Allen isn't happy about that. “How it came out makes me very, very sad and angry at the same time,” Allen told a group of reporters on Saturday after the preseason game at Cleveland, via Matt Parrino of NewYorkUpstate.com. “Obviously, very unfortunate what happened, and as a teammate of him, and as someone in this locker room, all we can do is love on him.” Allen said that many of the team's players knew what had happened. “What we’ve been doing is giving him his space and time, but at the same time being around him, loving up on him,” Allen said. “But not trying to do anything to to reopen that. . . . Just guys being around him and putting their hand on him and not having to say too much, but ‘I got your back.’” Although someone decided it was newsworthy to share the story before the Bills or Oliver could do so, most decided that the nature of the tragedy called for discretion. “It’s very hard to wrap your mind around a teammate going through a situation like that,” Allen said. “Because you have kids, you understand what that could be like and what that could feel like. You never want to put yourself in that situation or those shoes. He’s a strong man.” Every reporter and/or content creator has to make a decision for themselves as to how they'll handle situations like this. For most, the right move is to wait. For some, a different decision is made. And when that decision is made, it opens the person up to scrutiny and criticism by those who believe that the right thing to do was to say nothing until those directly impacted by an unimaginable loss choose to acknowledge it.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bears LB Nephi Sewell carted off with leg injury
summary: Bears linebacker Nephi Sewell was carted off the field during Saturday's preseason game against the Bengals.
full_text: Bears linebacker Nephi Sewell was carted off the field during Saturday's preseason game against the Bengals. Sewell injured his right leg while making a tackle of Bengals running back Tahj Brooks after a 10-yard gain with 36 seconds left until halftime. Sewell's brother, Noah, a linebacker who remains on the active/physically unable to perform list as he works his way back from an Achilles tear, was among those wishing Nephi the best before he departed. Nephi Sewell left last Saturday's game against the Browns with a concussion after taking a hit on a kickoff. He spent his first four seasons with the Saints, appearing in 30 games, before the Saints released him at the end of last season and Bears signed him to the practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Patriots OT Marcus Bryant out with an ankle injury
summary: Patriots offensive tackle Marcus Bryant was injured on the fourth official play from scrimmage in Saturday night's preseason game against the Eagles.
full_text: Patriots offensive tackle Marcus Bryant was injured on the fourth official play from scrimmage in Saturday night's preseason game against the Eagles. Bryant started at right tackle but remained down on the field after a 1-yard run by running back Lan Larison. He needed assistance getting off the field and eventually to the training room. Bryant was heavily favoring his left ankle. The Patriots announced that he is out for the remainder of the game with an ankle injury. The 2025 seventh-round pick is competing with Caleb Lomu for the swing tackle job. His injury is the latest in the offensive line for the Patriots. Last week, New England lost its top two backup interior offensive linemen with Ben Brown now out for the rest of the preseason with a leg injury, and Andrew Rupcich was waived with an injury settlement with a strained MCL.
author: Charean Williams

title: Browns coach Todd Monken on TE Dae'Quan Wright entering the portal: "Man, isn't this shit crazy?"
summary: Browns coach Todd Monken has spent much of his career in the college ranks.
full_text: Browns coach Todd Monken has spent much of his career in the college ranks. Things have changed dramatically since then, however. He currently has a first-year player on the roster who has entered the transfer portal, after winning an injunction this week that has given him another year of college football. “Man, isn’t this shit crazy?" Monken told reporters after Saturday's preseason contest against the Bills, a game in which Wright didn't play. "I don’t even know what to say. As far as I know, he’s had a medical issue that wasn’t allowing him to practice. That’s a medical issue. It has nothing to do with me. He was cleared, so we dressed him just in case we had to have him. . . . "I don’t know what to say. I wondered why Lane Kiffin reached out to me a week ago, now I know. I didn’t call him back; I guess I should have." Kiffin's LSU is indeed one of the programs that has been trying to set the stage to create room for first-year NFL players who could return to college for another season. Because even though the system craves a return to something that seems normal, the coaches want to win now. Those who can take advantage of the current chaos can acquire a legitimate edge in the quest to do so.
author: Mike Florio

title: Eagles RB Ja’Quinden Jackson leaves in an ambulance after opening kickoff
summary: Eagles running back Ja’Quinden Jackson left Gillette Stadium in an ambulance during Saturday night's preseason game.
full_text: '' Eagles running back Ja’Quinden Jackson left Gillette Stadium in an ambulance during Saturday night's preseason game. Jackson was injured on the opening kickoff. He appeared to take a knee to the head from Patriots running back Lan Larison after diving at Larison's legs to make a tackle. Jackson was knocked out, and both arms went into the fencing position. Medical personnel immediately began work on Jackson before he was placed on a backboard and then a stretcher and placed into the ambulance, which came onto the field. The entire Eagles team went onto the field to wish Jackson well before he left. The Eagles released a statement saying, "Jackson has strength and movement in all extremities and is being taken to a local hospital for further evaluation."
author: Charean Williams

title: Anthony Richardson: I'm just looking forward to helping the team
summary: Anthony Richardson's future with the Colts has been debated often since he requested a trade this offseason and assistant General Manager Ed Dodds gave a strong hint about how things are going to play out last week.
full_text: Anthony Richardson's future with the Colts has been debated often since he requested a trade this offseason and assistant General Manager Ed Dodds gave a strong hint about how things are going to play out last week. Dodds said that the Colts want to have three quarterbacks " that can play ," which suggests that both Richardson and Riley Leonard will make the cut as backups to Daniel Jones. After Saturday's preseason game against the Falcons, Richardson weighed in on the prospect of remaining with the team into the regular season. "I'm just looking forward to helping the team ," Richardson said, via the team's website. "They truly believe that I have a chance to be on this squad and I love that. I just want to be able to contribute, put my best foot forward and help the team win." Leonard started Saturday's game and went 7-of-14 for 62 yards while leading the Colts to a pair of field goals. Richardson, who started the first preseason game, was 3-of-9 for 24 yards while running three times for 15 yards and being sacked twice in the 34-6 loss. Neither performance made a compelling argument for the No. 2 job, so the competition will likely continue through the team's final preseason game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Eagles rookie WR Makai Lemon remains out tonight
summary: Rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon is among the Eagles players not suited up for tonight's preseason game against the Patriots, Jeff McLane of the Philadelphia Inquirer reports.
full_text: '' Rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon is among the Eagles players not suited up for tonight's preseason game against the Patriots, Jeff McLane of the Philadelphia Inquirer reports. The Eagles’ first-round pick injured his hamstring on Aug. 3 and missed nine practices before returning to limited work on Thursday. Lemon will have two weeks to catch up before the season opener. Linebacker Jihaad Campbell, running back Tank Bigsby, defensive tackle Byron Young (shoulder), wide receiver Hollywood Brown, wide receiver Elijah Moore (neck), cornerback Jakorian Bennett (knee), tight end Grant Calcaterra (back) and offensive tackle John Ojukwu (pectoral) are among players who played last week who are not playing tonight, per McLane.
author: Charean Williams

title: Dolphins claim CB Jai'Onte' McMillan
summary: The Dolphins went to the waiver wire to add a cornerback on Saturday.
full_text: '' The Dolphins went to the waiver wire to add a cornerback on Saturday. They announced the addition of Jai'Onte' McMillan to their active roster. McMillan was dropped by the Colts when they signed tight end JJ Galbreath on Friday. Miami cleared space for McMillan earlier in the day when they released cornerback Nick McCloud. McMillan was undrafted out of Minnesota this year and he signed with the Colts in June. He played 17 defensive snaps and one special teams snap in the Colts' preseason opener. The waiver claim was announced during the Dolphins' game against the Giants on Saturday afternoon. McMillan will begin practicing with his new team on Monday and could see time in their preseason finale.
author: Josh Alper

title: Deshaun Watson: Boos are a disrespectful thing, has nothing to do with performance
summary: Watson was booed during his appearance in the third quarter of Saturday's home game.
full_text: '' Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson said this week that he didn't care about how fans reacted to him during Saturday's home preseason game, but he appeared to be a bit rankled when asked at a postgame press conference about the boos that greeted his entry to the game in the third quarter. Watson was making his first appearance in a home game since he tore his Achilles in 2024 and he heard those boos before he took his first snap. They continued while he went 5-of-12 for 36 yards and an interception in a 31-7 loss to the Bills. "I didn’t have no reaction ," Watson said. "I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance. It’s a little bit [more] personal than that. I think that’s a disrespectful thing. I’m gonna keep whatever I feel with me and my family internally with how I feel about that and move on." Browns head coach Todd Monken said in his own press conference that "everybody will be fine" if Watson plays good football while helping the Browns win games, but Watson reiterated his disagreement with the idea that the booing is tied to performance when asked if he agreed with that sentiment. "Last time I played on this field I tore my Achilles. That same fan base cheered when I got hurt," Watson said. "What does that have to do with anything about performance? When a person gets hurt, especially for your own city and they cheer?" Watson signed a fully guaranteed five-year, $230 million contract after being traded to the Browns ahead of the 2022 season and he's played poorly in 19 starts since joining the club. It remains to be seen if he will get to No. 20 in Week 1 — Monken declined to name a starter after Saturday's game — but it seems like a safe bet that the reaction won't be a terribly warm one if he takes the field for the Browns' home opener in Week 3.
author: Josh Alper

title: Raiders place CB Chigozie Anusiem on IR
summary: The Raiders placed cornerback Chigozie Anusiem on season-ending injured reserve Saturday, the team announced.
full_text: '' The Raiders placed cornerback Chigozie Anusiem on season-ending injured reserve Saturday, the team announced. Anusiem injured his knee in the third quarter of Thursday night's preseason game against the Texans. He was on the punt team when he was dragged down from behind. He played 54 special teams snaps in three games last season for the Raiders, who signed him to the active roster in Week 15. Anusiem has also had stints with the Browns and Cardinals. He has appeared in four career games, primarily on special teams.
author: Charean Williams

title: J.J. McCarthy: End zone misses are throws I have to make
summary: Vikings quarterback J.J.
full_text: Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy is no longer fighting for the team's starting job, but he is trying to solidify his spot as the backup to Kyler Murray and Saturday's game against the Ravens was a decidedly mixed effort on that front. McCarthy was 5-of-10 for 81 yards, including a 50-yard strike to wide receiver Tai Felton that set the Vikings up in the red zone in the first quarter. McCarthy had a pair of opportunities to turn that field position into a touchdown, but missed Felton in the back of the end zone on second down and overthrew a wide open Myles Price on fourth down from the 1-yard-line. After the game, McCarthy called those "throws I’ve got to make ." "I know I can make those throws," McCarthy said, via Kevin Seifert of ESPN.com. "And it's great to have that experience logged in and that data logged in to be able to make that throw next time." McCarthy was sacked once and hit on other plays in his quarter of work. He was asked if he felt he was sped up on the misfires. "I wouldn't say I felt sped up," McCarthy said. "It's just sometimes you hit them, sometimes you miss. And it's . . . what preseason's all about. You get it out now and log that feeling, like I said, and make sure you hit it the next time." Head coach Kevin O'Connell said McCarthy was " a little hobbled " after the game, but McCarthy said he doesn't anticipate missing any time. Carson Wentz, who would likely be the backup if O'Connell opts to go away from McCarthy, was 9-of-11 for 92 yards during his time in Saturday's game.
author: Josh Alper

title: Report: Steelers will keep both Will Howard, Drew Allar on the 53-player roster
summary: Mason Rudolph is the second-best quarterback on the Steelers' roster.
full_text: '' Mason Rudolph is the second-best quarterback on the Steelers' roster. The team lists him as the backup quarterback to Aaron Rodgers. While Rudolph is the team's only experienced backup, the Steelers are set on keeping young quarterbacks Will Howard and Drew Allar on their 53-player roster, Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reports. It seems unlikely that either would clear waivers to return to the team's practice squad. Dulac's report came after the Steelers were shut out in a preseason game for the first time since a 17-0 loss to the Eagles in 2016. Howard and Allar both had disappointing outings after promising starts to the preseason, but Dulac said the decision to keep both came before the game and didn't change with anything that happened Friday night. In the 17-0 loss to the Jets, Howard was 10-of-15 for 74 yards and two interceptions and Allar went 11-of-23 for 110 yards and three sacks. “Those two turnovers will really make it sour,” said Howard, who started the game and played the entire first half. “There were some good things out there, but if you don’t win the game and turn the ball over, that’s unacceptable.” Rudolph didn't play as the Steelers know what they have in the ninth-year veteran, but do they have room to keep four quarterbacks? Or maybe a better question is: Can they afford to go into the season without a veteran backup behind a 42-year-old starter?

title: Michael Penix cleared for all football activities
summary: Falcons quarterback Michael Penix has been limited in practice all summer, but that is set to change this week.
full_text: Falcons quarterback Michael Penix has been limited in practice all summer, but that is set to change this week. Penix met with his doctors this week and head coach Kevin Stefanski told reporters after Saturday's preseason game that he received clearance for all football activities. Penix has been practicing throughout training camp after recovering from a torn ACL, but has not taken any snaps in 11-on-11 work while waiting for the green light. The Falcons' planned competition between Penix and Tua Tagovailoa for the starting quarterback job was on hold until Penix was cleared for team work, so it can now really get underway. The Falcons play their final preseason game in Miami next Friday and Tagovailoa is expected to play after sitting out Saturday's game against the Colts. Stefanski did not say if Penix will play in that game and that decision will be a point of interest around the team in the coming days.
author: Josh Alper

title: Cleveland fans boo Deshaun Watson as he struggles in return
summary: Watson struggled in front of a hostile home crowd.
full_text: '' Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson said this week that he doesn’t care what kind of reception he gets from the fans in Cleveland. The reception he got in today's preseason game was decidedly negative. The fans in Cleveland loudly booed as Watson took the field and continued booing throughout the third quarter as Watson struggled. Although Huntington Bank Field is mostly empty, the fans who are there are making it known that they don't like Watson quarterbacking their team. Watson played poorly while the fans booed. The Browns' offense went three-and-out on Watson's first two drives, then Watson threw an interception on his third drive and threw a fourth-down incompletion to end his fourth drive. Trading for Watson was a disaster for the Browns, who gave up three first-round picks, a second-round pick, a third-round pick and a fourth-round pick to get Watson, then gave him a five-year, $230 million fully guaranteed contract. For that, Watson has played a total of 19 games in four seasons, and has been one of the worst quarterbacks in the NFL in those 19 games. And the Browns made the move for Watson despite knowing he had been accused of sexually assaulting some two dozen massage therapists, accusations that resulted in Watson being suspended for the first 11 games of his time in Cleveland. Given all that, Watson should expect to be booed in Cleveland if he's the starter in Week Three, when the Browns play their first home game of the regular season. Whether Watson cares or not.

full_text: The Dolphins freed up a spot on their 90-man roster ahead of their preseason game against the Giants on Saturday. They announced that they have released cornerback Nick McCloud. McCloud signed with the team on August 10, so it was a very brief stay in Miami for the veteran. McCloud appeared in 15 games for the Bears last season. He started four games and finished the year with 27 tackles and two passes defensed. McCloud played for the 49ers, Giants and Bengals prior to joining the Bears. summary: With Kyler Murray previously winning the starting quarterback job in Minnesota, J.J.

title: Chiefs' Harrison Butker drills historic 69-yard field goal, but it won't count in the NFL record book
summary: Butker can have bragging rights after his booming kick, but the NFL record stands
full_text:
The biggest highlight of the NFL preseason this year just came from a kicker and it happened on Saturday night when Harrison Butker drilled a 69-yard field goal just before halftime in the Chiefs ' game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers .
And yes, you read that correctly: Butker hit from 69 YARDS.
The NFL record for longest field goal is 68 yards and Butker actually topped that with his kick, but he won't be getting his name etched into the NFL record book, because preseason kicks don't officially count. Due to that rule, Cam Little's 68-yard field goal from last season still stands as the longest kick in NFL history.
Even though it won't go down in the record book, Butker's kick was still wildly impressive and that's mostly because the ball easily cleared the crossbar. Butker absolutely smashed the kick -- the ball hit the net behind the field goal posts -- and his attempt likely would have been good from 75 yards or even further.
You know what, let's stop talking about the kick and just watch it.
69-YARD FIELD GOAL TO END THE HALF 🦵 pic.twitter.com/hMfVCH2A6L
Butker only got the field goal attempt because the Chiefs' defense made a fourth-down stop late in the first half. With under 10 seconds left to play in the second quarter, the Buccaneers were facing a fourth-and-5 from Kansas City's 49-yard line and they decided to go for it. The Bucs ended up failing on the fourth down after Jake Browning threw an incomplete pass and that gave Kansas City the ball with just three seconds left. At that point, Andy Reid decided to sent out Butker.
The 69-yarder was one of three that Butker hit against Tampa Bay to go along with a 58-yarder and 45-yarder, but he also missed a 43-yard kick in the fourth quarter of Kansas City's 16-15 loss.
Although Butker won't be getting his name in the NFL record book, he will certainly have some bragging rights and that's because 69-yarder is tied for the second-longest field goal made in an actual game in the history of football.
The first American football game was played in 1869 and in the 157 years since then, only three kickers have hit a field goal of at least 69 yards in a game:
1. Cam Little hit a 70-yarder for the Jaguars during the 2025 preseason.
CAM LITTLE 70-YARD FIELD GOAL Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/OCIZ1W5M5f
T-2. Harrison Butker hit a 69-yarder on Saturday night (The first clip we showed you at the top was from the Chiefs' broadcast team, so now, let's see what the Buccaneers' broadcast team had to say about the kick)
Whole team was HYPED for this 69-yard FG by Harrison Butker 🗣️ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/O2B9LRknli
T-2. Abilene Christian kicker Ove Johansson hit a 69-yarder in 1976. And in case you're wonder, yes, there is footage of Johansson's kick.
44 years ago today on October 16, 1976 it was homecoming weekend at Abilene Christian University and Ove Johansson made history. With a 17 MPH wind, Johansson kicked the longest field goal ever 69-yards against East Texas State! Here’s the historic kick! pic.twitter.com/1hloys1OIB
College kickers were allowed to use a 1- to 2-inch kicking block until 1989 when they were banned. Before the ban, kickers were essentially kicking off a tee as long as the holder was able to get the ball in the right spot. The five longest field goals in college history, including Johansson's, all came when the kicking block was legal.
With their field goals being kicked off the ground, Little and Butker are in a league of their own.
Now that Butker has a 69-yarder under his belt, we might want to keep an eye on him this year, because he could go off like Little did last season for the Jaguars. Although Little's 70-yard kick in the preseason didn't count in the NFL record book, he ended up breaking the record anyway. The Jaguars kicker drilled a 68-yarder last November to break the record for longest field goal in NFL history. The mark had been held by Justin Tucker , who hit a 66-yarder in 2021. Little also hit a 67-yarder in Week 18 , and thanks to those two kicks, Little now officially has the two longest field goals in NFL history. The 67-yarder also holds the mark for longest OUTDOOR field goal in NFL history (His 68-yarder came indoors in Las Vegas).
Butker's career long in a regular-season game is 62 yards, so he definitely has a big leg and it won't be surprising if he tops that number this season. Maybe he'll even break Little's record, because at the rate things are going, it seems like it will only be a matter of time before an NFL kicker drills a 70-yarder in a regular-season game.
One reason we're seeing more long kicks is thanks to a new K-ball rule that the NFL implemented last season . Under the new rule, each team is given 60 kicking footballs (K-Balls) at the beginning of the season. This allows each team to break the ball in before they use it. Since the ball can be used in practice, that generally softens it up. Teams are also allowed to use a brush to try and rub down the bumps (Every football is covered by thousands of tiny bumps). A football that's broken in tends to fly better and a smoother ball allows the kicker to make better contact, which leads to better kicks.
Under the old rule that existed from 1999 until 2024, teams were given three brand new footballs ON GAME DAY and they had roughly one hour to break them in. The new balls were stiff, which made them more difficult to kick. It was the difference between using a brand new baseball glove and a worn in glove.
Last season, almost every kicker seemed to agree that the new rule was adding five to 10 yards to their kicks. Bengals special teams coordinator Darrin Simmons has been an NFL assistant since 1998, so he's seen everything, and he thinks the new rule could lead to even longer kicks going forward.
"I believe it makes a big difference and I think that's why the distances on some of these long field goals went up and I think it will continue to just skyrocket as long as that rule stays in place the way it is," Simmons told CBS Sports and several other outlets in late July.
Records are made to be broken and thanks to the NFL's new K-ball rule, it won't be surprising at all if the record for longest field goal goes down for the second straight season.
author: John Breech

title: Deshaun Watson fires back at Browns fans after being booed: 'It's a disrespectful thing'
summary: Watson clearly took the booing to heart
full_text:
While his performance against the Bills did not help his cause in his position battle against Shedeur Sanders , Deshaun Watson likely hurt it even more during his postgame press conference while addressing being booed by Browns fans.
Watson, after going 5 of 12 for 36 yards and an interception during Cleveland's 31-7 loss to the Bills , decided to go on the offensive when asked about the boos.
"I think the whole world knows it has nothing to do about the performance," Watson said . "It's a little bit more personal than that. So, I think it's a disrespectful thing."
To make his point, Watson noted that Saturday wasn't the first time that he felt the ire of Browns fans. He added that he gets treated better by opposing fans.
"Last time I played on this field, I tore my Achilles. That same fan base, they cheered when I got hurt," he said. "What does that have to do with anything about performance? When a person gets hurt, especially in your home stadium, and they cheer."
Watson said that his experiences with Browns fans are usually only negative on either social media or during home games. He was hoping that the situation regarding the fans' treatment of him would be better given his involvement in the city and after he worked to get himself back in position to compete to be the Browns' starting quarterback.
"I thought being away for two years and working myself back from two Achilles injuries and putting the time in and being around the facility, being around the city, doing charity work in the city, supporting the Cleveland Browns, hanging out with fans whenever I do see them, being honest, being the type of person that I know I am and the character would help," he said . "And I guess it hasn't. So that's why I say it's personal. So it is what it is. People have their own opinions. There's only so much you can do to change that. So at the end of the day, I just have to continue to just work on it and strive to be better mentally moving forward."
Saturday was a continuation of the downward spiral that has been Watson's career, especially since he arrived in Cleveland in 2022. A three-time Pro Bowler with the Texans , injuries and inconsistent play have plagued Watson throughout his time with the Browns. He is 9-10 as the Browns' starting quarterback with just 19 touchdowns, 12 interceptions and a mediocre 61.2% completion percentage.
Adding to the frustration that has been Watson's story in Cleveland is the amount of capital the Browns spent to get him. They sent Houston six draft picks that included three consecutive first-round picks in addition to signing Watson to a record-setting, five-year, $230 million fully guaranteed contract. It's undeniably one of -- if not the -- worst transactions in the history of sports .
There's also the fact that the Browns traded for Watson despite the fact that he had already been sued by over two dozen female massage therapists for sexual harassment and sexual assault (in 2022, it was announced that 20 of the 24 women who sued Watson had reached confidential settlements). Watson's time in Cleveland began with him serving an 11-game suspension for violating the league's personal conduct policy.
In addition to Watson's plight, the fact that he's competing against the immensely popular Sanders doesn't help his cause. Sanders, who made the Pro Bowl as a rookie, went 9 of 11 for 74 yards with a touchdown and an interception against the Bills. Sanders also shined during his postgame press conference when he was asked about the fans' treatment of Watson.
"I think we all need to understand that we're all human," he said . "I don't really do things to humans I wouldn't want done to me. ... Just for our fans, I appreciate y'all showing up and everything. However y'all feel about the situation, about Deshaun, I think it's more about a bigger purpose than just respect. The respect thing that I feel like should be there. Because we're out trying to do our best and trying to serve the franchise the best way possible. We're going out there every game and doing everything we can do. I don't really appreciate that."
As noted above, Watson didn't do himself any favors both during and after Saturday's game. And while it appears that his time in Cleveland is destined to be remembered as an epic disappointment, Watson remains optimistic that there is light at the end of the tunnel in terms of his playing career.
"I don't regret anything in my life," he said. "I think the Lord puts you in situations for a reason. I don't regret anything at all. I had different thoughts on how it was gonna be, but it is what it is. Sometimes, the tables turn, and I'm patient enough -- because I'm a child of God -- to wait for that change. So, I ain't tripping."

title: Browns quarterback battle: Shedeur Sanders decent in start, Deshaun Watson struggles, both throw interceptions
summary: Browns coach Todd Monken reportedly plans to make a decision in the coming days
full_text:
The Cleveland Browns have kept their quarterback battle going through nearly a month of training camp and preseason action, so what was an hour delay before gathering their final data points? After Cleveland's Week 2 preseason game against the Buffalo Bills was suspended for roughly an hour due to lightning, Shedeur Sanders and Deshaun Watson got their latest -- and perhaps final -- chances to show they deserve to start Week 1 against the Jacksonville Jaguars .
ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported the decision could come as soon as Monday.
Sanders got the start and came out on fire, completing all four of his pass attempts on the opening drive. The final connection was an 8-yard touchdown to Luke Floriea .
the second year connection for the TD! #BUFvsCLE on News 5 pic.twitter.com/BntGdJpIAM
Overall, Sanders hit on his first eight throws and generally looked comfortable in the pocket and getting through his reads; there appeared to be just one play in which Sanders bailed from a relatively clean pocket, and even then, he managed to turn it into a short gain. When he was asked to execute play-action concepts, Sanders looked smooth and took the easy throws.
It helped that the Bills' pass rush was not particularly active, and Todd Monken gave Sanders lots of easy answers. When the situation wasn't as straightforward -- such as a third-and-15 play -- Sanders was calm, cool and collected ... and accurate.
Shedeur + Luke = big-time plays #BUFvsCLE on News 5 and NFL Network pic.twitter.com/fPAPEidymf
Arguably Sanders' best play didn't even show up on the stat sheet. On a third-and-5 -- the play right before the one above, in fact -- Sanders scrambled for 13 yards after getting hit in the helmet. The play came back, though, as Zak Zinter got called for holding, and the contact to the helmet went uncalled.
QUESTIONABLE:  Refs call a questionable holding call on #Browns G Zak Zinter whilst missing Shedeur Sanders getting smacked in the head, negating this scramble play by Shedeur Sanders. pic.twitter.com/NhoI742KSq
Unfortunately for Sanders, his ninth throw was not a good one, either. The former Colorado star threw behind 2025 undrafted tight end Jermaine Terry II , and the ball deflected up in the air and right to Damar Hamlin .
Damar Hamlin comes up with the INT 🙌 BUFvsCLE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SBow1PXq6x
Overall, Sanders was 9-for-11 for 74 yards, a touchdown and an interception. He took one sack (which lost no yardage) and had a 2-yard run.
Sanders got the ball out quickly for the most part and was generally accurate, except for the interception. His passes traveled, on average, 3.2 yards downfield, a very low number, and a couple of completions that went for minimal gains led to drives fizzling out.
Overall, it was a better performance than Week 1, but the interception certainly put a damper on it.
After outperforming Sanders in Week 1, Watson entered in the third quarter and played quite poorly. The embattled, oft-injured quarterback missed both of his throws on the first drive, including an attempt to a well-covered Gage Larvadain that narrowly avoided being intercepted.
On his second drive, Watson got his first completion of the day, but it was an ugly one: a bit high and wide for Davon Booth on a screen that resulted in a 1-yard loss. On third down, Watson did ... whatever this is:
Checking in on Deshaun Watson pic.twitter.com/2kHZtPYmmH
Boos rained down on Watson when he first took the field and when he left the field after both three-and-outs.
His third drive was better ... until it wasn't. He threw low, but complete, to Malachi Corley for 20 yards and had a 9-yard scramble shortly thereafter, but then he threw an interception to Te'Cory Couch .
Te'Cory Couch with the INT! BUFvsCLE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/UQXxepOOG7
This is a throw that shouldn't be made in the first place, because it requires perfect ball location. If it's low, short or behind, it's an interception for the cornerback (in this case, No. 36, Jordan Dunbar ). If it's even slightly high, as it was here, there's a chance it gets picked by Couch, which is what happened. All this while targeting a Larvadain, who is listed at 5-foot-8. Ironically, Watson almost made the perfect throw, and Larvadain almost made what would have been an excellent catch. Instead, it's a pick.
Watson actually got a little bit more action than expected, playing into the fourth quarter, but he overthrew a deep shot to Corley, who had a step on his defender, on a third-and-6 and then threw behind Floriea on fourth-and-6. Boos ensued again.
Overall, Watson finished 5-for-12 for 35 yards and an interception. He ran twice for 13 yards.
Watson was believed to be in the lead for the Week 1 starting job, and Jared Verse even said Friday, "I think I have a vibe of who I think will go out there." If the Browns are truly taking every snap into account, though, there was a clear better player Saturday.
Watson's major struggles when things get even slightly off-kilter -- he gets pressured, his first read isn't open, or even if he just has to move in the pocket -- showed. So did his general inaccuracy. For example, on the 20-yard completion to Corley, he threw the ball low, forcing Corley to go to the ground, rather than catch the ball with a chance for YAC. And that was Watson's best play of the day.
Here are the numbers through two preseason games. GM Andrew Berry said during the broadcast that game performance is just one factor, obviously, but this provides some context.
Again, there is much, much more going into the decision than just the numbers above. Still, Saturday especially was a win for Sanders, and even if it's not deemed enough for him to start Week 1, there's a good chance we see both quarterbacks play significant snaps in 2026.

title: NFL preseason Week 2 winners and losers: Bo Nix shines in return, Deshaun Watson takes shot at Browns fans
summary: Rookie wideout De'Zhaun Stribling continues his historic preseason run for San Francisco, while Geno Smith shines in his return to New York
full_text:
The second week of the NFL preseason is underway, with the regular season drawing ever closer.
Preseason football is like a box of chocolates as Forrest Gump would say, "You never know what you're going to get." That's because some squads have their starters chained to the bench, some play minimal snaps and some could receive as much of a half of work. Observing who could emerge as a real contributor from the chaos that is preseason football is tricky given the varying degrees of skill levels on the field all at the same time, but it's possible to identify who maximized their opportunity and who would like a do-over.
Let's kick identify the winners and losers of Week 2 of the 2026 preseason.
Was Shedeur Sanders perfect in his preseason Week 2 start? Hardly. Was he much, much better than Deshaun Watson ? Absolutely. (Though the bar was basically on the ground).
Sanders came out firing after having to wait out a weather delay of nearly an hour, connecting on all four of his passes on the opening drive. That included a fourth-down conversion to tight end Blake Whiteheart and, later on, an 8-yard touchdown pass to Luke Floriea . Sanders had a few of Cleveland's starters -- namely rookies Spencer Fano and Denzel Boston -- out there with him, but he was mostly working with backups. The Bills rested basically all of their starters, too.
the second year connection for the TD! #BUFvsCLE on News 5 pic.twitter.com/BntGdJpIAM
"There's a lot there to like," coach Todd Monken said. "I mean he plays with a certain amount of confidence. He has gotten a lot better at getting rid of the ball. Certainly he wants to make a play.
"... I thought he did a lot of really good things. I'm really proud of him and where he's come from. From the moment I got here until now, very impressive."
Monken in specific cited the above touchdown pass and a 23-yard completion on third and 15 as two of Sanders' best moments.
Sanders actually hit on his first eight passes in a row before an interception in which he threw slightly behind Jermaine Terry II . Monken said the ball "certainly" could have been caught. It also could have been a better throw.
Damar Hamlin comes up with the INT 🙌 BUFvsCLE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/SBow1PXq6x
Overall, it was a strong day for Sanders -- 9-for-11, 74 yards, one touchdown, one interception, one sack -- and a much better outing than in Week 1.
Preseason scores do not matter at all, but there might not have been a single team needing a good week more than the Falcons . Atlanta got walloped by Denver, 27-7, last week, hours after the news came out that James Pearce Jr . was suspended eight games . Tua Tagovailoa looked awful, the defense looked awful, and the vibes were bad.
Week 2 was much better. With no Tagovailoa or Michael Penix Jr . playing, Cooper Rush and Jack Strand both played well, and three different players had a rushing touchdown in a 34-6 win over the Colts .
The best news, however, came after the game: Kevin Stefanski said Penix has been cleared to return to 11-on-11 work after a lengthy rehabilitation from yet another torn ACL. Maybe Tagovailoa is already the de-facto starter since it's taken Penix a bit, but it's always nice to get positive injury updates.
San Francisco 49ers 2026 second-round pick wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling , the rookie 33rd overall pick out of Ole Miss, is THE breakout star of the preseason this year. After catching four of his five targets for 46 yards receiving on Thursday against the Los Angeles Chargers , Stribling is now up to 11 catches for 109 yards receiving on 13 targets. That makes Stribling the first player since at least 2017 to produce at least 11 catches combined within the first 20 minutes of two consecutive preseason games, per CBS Sports Research. Many preseason All-Stars don't end up contributing much outside of special teams for their respective squads, but it's safe to say Stribling will have a place on head coach Kyle Shanahan's play call sheet early this regular season. That's especially true when factoring in how snake-bitten by injury San Francisco is at the position.
Every De'Zhaun Stribling target from week 2 of the preseason. pic.twitter.com/aDUNARC2WT
No, Will Anderson Jr. , Danielle Hunter , Derek Stingley Jr . and the rest of the starters from the NFL's No. 1 total defense (277.2 total yards per game allowed) in 2025 weren't on the field Thursday night, but the Houston Texans ' ferocious tenacity on defense certainly was.
They bullied Las Vegas Raiders first overall pick rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza in the first half, generating an 80-yard pick six by fourth-round rookie linebacker Wade Woodaz and an 11-yard sack by second-round rookie defensive tackle Kayden McDonald .
OPEN UP A CAN OF WOODAZZZZZZ 🤯 📺: @nflonespn pic.twitter.com/Ke0lrYupPs
Seeing McDonald flash pass rush chops like this should send shivers down the spines of offensive coordinators all around the league. If there was an area Houston needed to shore up on their defense, it was defensive tackle, and they were able to do so by drafting McDonald, the 2026 NFL Draft's top defensive tackle prospect in the eyes of many, including yours truly. McDonald, who is listed at 6-foot-3-inches tall while weighing 326 pounds, was more of a run stuffer than a pass rusher in college at Ohio State, but if he can find his groove early on when tasked to get after the quarterback, Houston's defense could be a much greater problem for the rest of the league.
KMAC WITH THE SACK 😮‍💨 📺: @nflonespn pic.twitter.com/kOks1uMcrW
Tennessee All-SEC cornerback Jermod McCoy profiled as a likely first-round pick in the 2026 NFL Draft until the medicals surrounding his knee scared teams away. McCoy did suffer a torn ACL in January 2025, but fears about inflammation and arthritis in his knee caused him to tumble all the way down to being the 101st overall pick and a fourth-round draft choice.
In the Raiders' 22-20 preseason victory over the Texans on Thursday, McCoy appeared to be moving well and in phase with opposing wide receivers when tasked with dropping back into man coverage. Perhaps he can end up becoming the best value pick of the 2026 rookie draft class if given the opportunity to receive snaps with Las Vegas' starting defense.
Jermod McCoy man coverage snaps. Talent is there. Very fluid and easy COD. Needs to finish at the catch point. Taunting that gives offense a first after forced incompletion is the opposite of finishing. Need to see him against starters. pic.twitter.com/DFBlIRfOfH
Outside of Minnesota Vikings quarterback J.J. McCarthy , perhaps no other quarterback had a more depressing 2025 season than Geno Smith . The two-time Pro Bowler led the NFL in both sacks taken (55) and interceptions thrown (17) last season while attempting to pilot then-offensive coordinator Chip Kelly's scheme with the Las Vegas Raiders. Those statistics made Smith just the sixth quarterback since the 1970 AFL/NFL merger to lead the NFL in both sacks and interceptions in the same season. Kelly had to trudge back down to the college ranks, where he is now Northwestern's offensive coordinator.
Smith, a second-round pick of the New York Jets in the 2013 NFL Draft, returned to New York after the Jets acquired him and a 2026 seventh-round pick from the Raiders in exchange for a 2026 sixth-round pick. He kicked off his second stint with the Jets with a perfect drive while leading the Jets' starting lineup on the opening possession against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Friday before head coach Aaron Glenn decided he'd seen enough from the 35-year-old veteran quarterback to end his night.
Smith completed all seven of his throws on New York's opening drive, including the 13-yard scoring strike to tight end Jelani Woods . He also connected with both of the Jets' top wide receivers, Garrett Wilson (one catch on one target for 10 yards) and Adonai Mitchell (two catches on two targets for 29 yards), to finish the night with 65 yards passing.…
author: Garrett Podell

title: Bengals-Bears joint practice takeaways: Joe Burrow gets into rare scuffle, defense terrorizes Caleb Williams
summary: Dexter Lawrence is already making his presence felt in Cincinnati, and his dominance has rubbed off on his fellow defenders
full_text:
CINCINNATI -- Beating up on your younger brother is always fun, so Zac Taylor was probably thrilled with how things unfolded Thursday during Cincinnati's joint practice with Chicago.
The Bengals head coach has close ties to the Bears because his younger brother, Press Taylor, is Chicago's offensive coordinator. The Bengals completely revamped their defense this offseason, and after the starters played just one series in the first preseason game , the battle against the Bears' offense represented the first big test of Cincinnati's new-look unit, which features four new starters, including Dexter Lawrence .
If the joint practice was any indication, the Bengals need the regular season to start now because the defense looks ready to roll.
Here are five takeaways from the joint practice. Although the Bengals defense had some big moments, we're going to start with Joe Burrow because he got into a fight, and anytime a QB gets into a fight, you have to start there.
If there's been one common theme around the NFL this year, it's that if you hold a joint practice, there's going to be at least one fight, and that was the case here. There weren't any brawls, but there were a few scuffles, including one involving Burrow.
If there's one rule at an NFL practice, it's that you never touch the quarterback, and Dayo Odeyingbo slightly broke that rule. The Bears defensive end got his hands on Burrow and wouldn't let go of his jersey, which caused things to get heated. Burrow wasn't happy with Odeyingbo, and he let the Bears defender know it.
Burrow was asked about the scuffle after practice, and he gave an interesting two-word answer.
"Shit happens," the Bengals QB said . "That's how practice goes sometimes."
Burrow did admit this was the first time since college that he got into a scuffle.
"Fun to go at it a little bit," he said.
Although it was fun for Burrow, the scuffle was quickly broken up before it could turn into a full-fledged fight.
Burrow's teammates were ready to go to battle for him during the scuffle, and that's what Ja'Marr Chase wants to see more of this year.
"I don't care what we do, we just better f---ing protect Joe," Chase said after practice.
The Bengals were in a feisty mood Thursday, and one reason is that everyone on the roster seems to sense the urgency surrounding the 2026 season. And if they don't realize it, they will soon because Burrow is reminding everyone all the time.
"The urgency is very high in the locker room, you can feel it," Burrow said. "It's palpable."
Burrow was asked if this is a "now or never" season for the Bengals, and he didn't disagree with that assessment.
"I'm tired of saying next year, next year, next year," Burrow said. "This is it. Life is too short to keep pushing things down the road."
Burrow threw just one interception against the Bears, and it actually came on the play that started the scuffle. His pass bounced off Mike Gesicki and into the hands of Chicago safety Dillon Thieneman , who came away with the interception.
Burrow got some revenge on the next play when he hit Chase for a big gain after the receiver made an impressive toe-dragging catch along the sideline. Overall, Burrow had a strong practice, and his favorite receiver was Tee Higgins , who caught at least six passes.
"Tee made some plays today," Burrow said. "That was good to see. We know what kind of player Tee is, and he's going to make big plays in big spots, and we're counting on him."
Besides Higgins and Chase, Burrow also made some big throws to Drew Sample and Andrei Iosivas . Although the offense was good, the Bengals have to be thrilled with how their defense played, so let's get to that.
There's a reason the Bengals gave up a first-round pick to get Dexter Lawrence back in April, and that's because the team feels he can be a game-changer. If Thursday's practice was any indication, Lawrence is going to live up to that hype and more.
As a matter of fact, Caleb Williams might have nightmares about the 6-foot-5, 350-pound defensive tackle. There were multiple plays where Lawrence barged his way through the Bears' offensive line to get a hand in Williams' face or "sack" him. Not only did Lawrence wreak havoc on pass plays, but he was also a run-stuffer up the middle.
And then there was his interception, which was definitely the play of the day. Near the end of practice, Lawrence tipped a Williams pass into the air and then picked it off himself.
Video of the Dexter Lawrence interception exists! Sexy Dexy is an absolute game-change for the Bengals. He's going to be a problem for opposing offenses this year. #Bengals #Bears pic.twitter.com/XQtR2Bocao https://t.co/Stckx28oQG
That's an athletic play for a guy who weighs 350 pounds.
Following practice, Williams admitted he was wildly impressed with Lawrence.
"He's an All-Pro guy, one of the best, if not the best D-tackles, up there with Chris Jones ," the Bears QB said. "He's a force to be reckoned with."
Lawrence still hasn't played a regular-season game for Cincinnati, but so far, the Bengals' decision to acquire him is looking brilliant.
Earlier this year, the Bengals decided not to pick up Murphy's fifth-year option, which means the pass rusher is in a contract year. If Thursday's practice was any indication, Murphy might be setting himself up for a huge payday.
The final offensive possession of practice went to the Bears, and they did nothing with the ball because no one could block Murphy. The 2023 first-round pick sacked Williams on two straight plays, including one that ended with a "safety." One ref ruled it a safety, but the officials gave the ball back to the Bears at the 1 so they could run another play because this was a practice. On the next play, Williams threw an interception to Jalen Davis .
Murphy also recorded at least one other sack earlier in the day, so he had at least three against the Bears. During an interview after practice, Murphy got an ovation at his locker from Boye Mafe .
Boye Mafe giving Myles Murphy an ovation as Murphy is being interviewed at his locker pic.twitter.com/0PJbqeHAqJ
The Bengals defense struggled to close out games last year. One of their worst losses came against the Bears, when Williams threw a 58-yard game-winning touchdown pass with just 17 seconds left in a 47-42 Chicago win. This time around, the Bengals closed out the Bears with two sacks and an interception on Chicago's final offensive possession.
"As a defense, that's exactly what we're looking for, to close out games," Murphy said after practice .
The 6-11 Bengals lost five games last year by six points or fewer, and a lot of those happened because the defense couldn't close things out. This year, things feel different.
It certainly felt like the Bengals defense got the best of the Bears offense during practice, but that doesn't mean it was all bad news for Chicago. The Bears offense made several huge plays over the course of the day. I didn't chart all of Williams' throws, but according to WLWT's Charlie Clifford , the Bears quarterback went 16 of 26 with three touchdowns and two interceptions during the 11-on-11 portion of practice.
One of Williams' favorite targets was Colston Loveland , who had no trouble weaving his way through the Bengals defense. He caught a touchdown pass, and it's starting to feel like he could emerge as one of the top tight ends in the NFL this year after catching 58 passes for 713 yards and six scores as a rookie last season.
Although Williams shined at times, he was under constant pressure, which led to an inaccurate day. However, he did a good job spreading the ball around. He hit Kalif Raymond with a deep shot for a touchdown. Raymond is in his first year with the Bears and already seems to be emerging as one of Williams' favorite targets. Although it's his first year in Chicago, Raymond spent four seasons with Ben Johnson in Detroit, so he's familiar with the Bears' offensive concepts.
"He's been in Ben's offense, so it's very similar to him," Williams said…

title: Arizona Cardinals struggle in preseason loss to Dallas Cowboys
summary: Not that it matters in the grand scheme of things, but this was about as good of a display of the issues that have plagued the Arizona Cardinals at camp as we could have asked for.  And I get it, in the spirit of the preseason a 34-13 loss to the Dallas Cowboys is about […]
full_text: GLENDALE, ARIZONA - AUGUST 22: The Arizona Cardinals cheerleaders perform before the preseason NFL game against the Dallas Cowboys at State Farm Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Glendale, Arizona. (Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Not that it matters in the grand scheme of things, but this was about as good of a display of the issues that have plagued the Arizona Cardinals at camp as we could have asked for. And I get it, in the spirit of the preseason a 34-13 loss to the Dallas Cowboys is about as useful as you know what’s on a boar. However the penalty issues, especially the offensive pre snap penalties have been a constant at training camp and the Cardinals have been hampered by these issues for years. So, the hope is that Mike LaFleur and the first team offense can fix this. Yet, he’s been stuck with maybe a really bad defense and the presnap issues remain. Let’s hope this issue was a Gardner Minshew thing, because tonight we didn’t see a mad genius offensive guru, we saw someone who struggled. For one night, all our worst fears, or maybe all the outside expectations came true.

title: Now that Garrett Williams is on the active roster, where will he play?
summary: Last year, the Arizona Cardinals medical tent was pretty busy. At one point in the season, there were 24 guys listed on IR. Even early in the preseason, several players have been lost for the year: OG Chase Bisontis, TEs Kenny Yeboah and Jameson Geers, LB Austin Keys, CBs Jaden Davis and Joey Blount, and […]
full_text: Cardinals cornerback Garrett Williams (21) celebrates an interception against the Commanders during a game at State Farm Stadium in Glendale on Sept. 29, 2024. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co Last year, the Arizona Cardinals medical tent was pretty busy. At one point in the season, there were 24 guys listed on IR. Even early in the preseason, several players have been lost for the year: OG Chase Bisontis, TEs Kenny Yeboah and Jameson Geers, LB Austin Keys, CBs Jaden Davis and Joey Blount, and DT Kaleb Proctor. RELATED: WILLIAMS ACTIVATED FROM PUP LIST The Cardinals have activated CB Garrett Williams off the PUP list. This is actually surprising based on his injury from last year when He tore his Achilles tendon in Week 16 against the Atlanta Falcons. The injury came in late December, which placed the time frame for complete recovery around four to six months for normal folks doing normal activities. Since playing football is not considered an ordinary situation, the projection to return to the field is anywhere from six to 12 months. With this being late August, Williams’ rehab is at eight months. CB Garrett Williams has been activated from the PUP list pic.twitter.com/qLLTM0s59M — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) August 20, 2026 In almost every press conference with head coach Mike LaFleur, he was often asked about Williams, and LaFleur seemed positive at each and every presser. In the August 3 post-practice press conference, he stated when asked about the PUP players: “Yeah, I’d say progress, but no timeline right now. If you ask Tip (Reiman), Tip’s feeling good. Garrett’s (Williams) feeling good. Sweaty’s feeling good. But I don’t have a timeline for you, and truly I mean that.” CB Will Johnson is healthy. So are CB Denzel Burke and CB Max Melton. Those four should become the main actors in the starting cornerback slots in Week 1. But where? How is this going to play out? The development of Williams was considered one of the keys for this defensive backfield. At times, he looked like a gem that was taken in the third round. Then, in other games, he appeared lost and played badly. He is entering his fourth NFL season and is the second-oldest defensive back on the roster behind S Budda Baker. The more quality players that you have in one position room, the better it’s going to be for not only the team, but for that player. Good athletes thrive on competition. For starters, Johnson will be situated at the left outside cornerback position. Burke has already grabbed the right outside cornerback spot. That leaves the slot. Williams has been earmarked for this position, but Melton is going to push him. And hard. So is Sean Murphy-Bunting. Open Your Eyes & You’ll See Whats Real.. #LLA ❤️‍🩹 pic.twitter.com/S3dlj7ozsg — Garrett Williams🎭 (@garrettismynam3) February 26, 2025 When Jonathan Gannon was the head coach, the defense featured Williams inside as well as outside. And even though Nick Rallis was the DC last year, he wants to stick three guys at three positions, and then rotate other players in as needed. If at all. Williams is one of the best cornerbacks on the roster. LaFleur has stated that Williams will compete for the nickel (slot) position and will have to win back the job. More than likely, you won’t see Williams play in the preseason at all. There hasn’t been a timeline for his return, and there isn’t a timeline for his reappearance in the lineup. Plus, Williams just might not be 100% for a return in Week 1, so we will see. The coaching staff may decide to bring him back slowly now that he is off the PUP list, which could hinder the number of snaps he gets in each game. Or, he may not be ready to get back on the field until later. The defense is expecting a big jump from Johnson in his second year in the league. Injuries kept him from completing a full season, but what he learned as a rookie should help him improve his play in 2026. Take the players that are now healthy: Johnson, Burke, Melton, and Williams. Add in the backups Murphy-Bunting, Kei-Trel Clark, and Elijah Jones. Now mix in the safety guys such as Baker, Andrew Wingard, Kitan Crawford, and Dadrion Taylor-Demerson. The NFC West Division may be a pass-happy place to reside, but this year, the Cardinals are going to be ready and make life very difficult for the likes of Matthew Stafford, Brock Purdy, and Sam Darnold. But these guys aren’t the ones this Cardinals defensive backfield is the most concerned with. That job lies with Puka Nacua (Rams), Jaxon Smith-Njigba (Seahawks), and Mike Evans (49ers).
