title: Cardinals scout Ryan Gold’s alleged betting update
summary: On July 17, Arizona Cardinals Director of College Scouting, Ryan Gold, was suspended indefinitely for violating the league’s gambling policy. Apparently, the integrity of any NFL game was not affected, but Gold’s alleged actions was a violation of the NFL’s Gambling Policy. The reason is the Gambling Policy is in place is so that the […]
full_text: Jul 30, 2021; Glendale, AZ, USA; A painter works on the details of the Arizona Cardinals logo on State Farm Stadium during training camp. Mandatory Credit: Joe Camporeale-USA TODAY Sports On July 17, Arizona Cardinals Director of College Scouting, Ryan Gold, was suspended indefinitely for violating the league’s gambling policy. Apparently, the integrity of any NFL game was not affected, but Gold’s alleged actions was a violation of the NFL’s Gambling Policy. The reason is the Gambling Policy is in place is so that the playing field is completely level, and nobody knows the outcome of every league game. This affects legal betting for one, and secondly, the NFL does not wish their league to become rehearsed and game outcomes already set like professional wrestling. RELATED: CARDINALS DIRECTOR OF COLLEGE SCOUTING SUSPENDED FOR GAMBLING The NFL isn’t interested in folks who bet on other sports, just not the one they are employed by. That is a huge no-no. Gambling on the NFL is a fact that has gone on forever. But the image is more important. It matters most that the NFL wants any gambling at any time not to influence the outcome of games whatsoever. It is commonly referred to as “protecting the shield.” The NFL issued this statement: “The Gambling Policy, which is annually reviewed with all NFL personnel, strictly prohibits anyone in the NFL from participating in or facilitating any form of sports gambling, and from providing third parties non-public information. Although there is no reason to believe the integrity of any NFL game was affected, the League takes any violation of the Gambling Policy with the utmost seriousness.” So, Gold was suspended indefinitely. Several days after his suspension, Gold issued a statement that the so-call bets, was instead his own wife who was placing weekly parlays with some of her old high school friends. His next move was to appeal the suspension. Ryan Gold's attorney says, "the gambling activity was Gold's wife making $10 weekly bets with a group of high school friends on parlays and that Gold was not involved." https://t.co/VC4rh7tkvp — David Payne Purdum (@DavidPurdum) July 19, 2026 The initial investigation was opened by the Arizona Department of Gaming in July. Social media had a field day with Gold’s reasoning, whether it is true or a woeful defense. “Sure lol” “Throwing the wife under the bus… bold strategy.” “Would love to see the attorney bill that crafted this bulletproof defense” “My girlfriend and her friends never shut up about busted parlays” “She’s a keeper” —————————————————————————————————————————— The question was then raised if the NFL’s policy included immediate family members who are also not allowed to gamble on the league. Now, a second investigation has been opened related to Gold’s activities. Enter the Massachusetts Gaming Commission (MGC). Despite the Arizona Department of Gaming’s investigation, the MGC has begun another investigation into unusual betting patterns in the state, according to ESPN, that may be tied to Gold’s alleged actions. Gold has deep roots with the State of Massachusetts as a player and coach as well as his advanced education. According to his attorney, Mike Caspino, he issued a statement on behalf of his client: “There is absolutely zero substance to the claims made against Ryan Gold. The NFL’s investigation is so deeply flawed and so wrong. He will be vindicated next month in our appeal.” Gold was not involved in his wife’s weekly parlay bets with friends, Caspino said. The basis of the NFL’s investigation into Gold is this: They are stating that Gold had confidential, nonpublic inside information involving Arizona’s 2026 draft selections before the picks were announced. Apparently, GM Monti Ossenfort had already made the decision to select RB Jeremiyah Love at the start of draft week, with the first round on Thursday night. BetMGM opened Love at 30-1 odds to go #3 overall. Then suddenly, he was 2-1 odds two days ahead of the draft. DraftKings reported before the draft that more bets and more money had been wagered on Love to go #3 than any other player offered. Gold had bet parlays on NFL games. Gold had bet parlays on college games. Gold has been with the Cardinals for 13-years. He was promoted to director of college scouting in June 2025. He previously spent three years as the franchise’s assistant director of college scouting after working for four seasons as a college scouting coordinator from 2018 to 2021. Gold oversaw the Cardinals’ day-to-day college scouting operations. The Cardinals issued this statement: “The NFL’s policies and expectations for all employees are clear, comprehensive, and consistently communicated. We fully support the league’s decision in this matter, which involves a single employee. Our focus remains on preparing for the start of training camp next week and the 2026 season.” The Cardinals fully cooperated with the league and noted that the issue involved a single employee. His suspension hearing has been set for September 23. Both investigations are still open.

title: Michael Penix injury update: Falcons QB cleared for football activities
summary: Michael Penix Jr. has been cleared for 11-on-11 activities, and the Atlanta Falcons QB1 race is still wide open. Early this week, Penix Jr. spoke more in depth about his belief that he is closer than ever and can do anything the coaching staff asks of him; it simply came down to whether or not […]
full_text: Jul 29, 2026; Atlanta, Falcons, USA; Atlanta Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. (9) talks to the media during the first day of training camp at IBM Performance Field. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Michael Penix Jr. has been cleared for 11-on-11 activities, and the Atlanta Falcons QB1 race is still wide open. Early this week, Penix Jr. spoke more in depth about his belief that he is closer than ever and can do anything the coaching staff asks of him; it simply came down to whether or not his doctors believed he was prepared for full contact. After meeting with medical staff on Friday, he’s been cleared to return. The timing couldn’t be better. Tua Tagovailoa has not come close to cementing his status as the starting quarterback for Atlanta. He had a rough outing against the Denver Broncos , and was reportedly volatile against the Indianapolis Colts during joint practice sessions. "Tua pressured on 100% of his dropbacks vs DEN" is a good reminder that pressure can be a QB stat. Contextualize everything pic.twitter.com/m8cerREHD4 — Tre’Shon (@tre3shon) August 18, 2026 Penix Jr. could not ask for a better opportunity to regain his status as the starting quarterback, but what should we expect from the third-year player? In most of these situations, concerns around rust and receiver chemistry are valid, but Penix Jr. hasn’t been on the rehab field all summer; he’s participated in everything outside of team activities — and he’s worked through mental reps in 11-on-11s when he can’t participate. Those reps should pay off and help him get up to speed quickly. Fans are dying to see the young quarterback take reps under center and prove that his alignment was the fault of his former coaching staff, not his own ability. Penix Jr. will also have to prove that he’s improved his accuracy and can handle turning his back to the defense on play-action concepts, which is no small feat with only one preseason game left. This return is welcome because the idea of Tagovailoa winning the job simply based on ability was starting to put a damper on this year’s training camp. The hope is that Penix Jr., at the very least, can make this a real competition.

title: Falcons – Colts preseason instant recap: Atlanta dominates the day
summary: Well, that went better. Atlanta’s backups dominated Indy’s backups in the first half of this one, with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand dicing them up through the air, Tyler Goodson and Nate Carter running them over for a pair of rushing touchdowns, and the defense frequently slowing Riley Leonard and company. Paired with another strong […]
full_text: WESTFIELD, IN - AUGUST 20: Atlanta Falcons helmets sits on the field during the Indianapolis Colts and Atlanta Falcons joint training camp practice on August 20, 2026 at the Grand Park Sports Campus in Westfield, IN. (Photo by Zach Bolinger/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Well, that went better. Atlanta’s backups dominated Indy’s backups in the first half of this one, with Cooper Rush and Jack Strand dicing them up through the air, Tyler Goodson and Nate Carter running them over for a pair of rushing touchdowns, and the defense frequently slowing Riley Leonard and company. Paired with another strong day from special teams, this was actually quite fun to watch from wire-to-wire, with the Falcons utterly destroying Indy’s preseason hopes and dreams. This game also gives the Falcons’ coaches plenty to evaluate, with the need to figure out how much of this success was owing to the Colts’ gameplan and talent and how much of it was owing to what the Falcons did, but plenty of encouraging performances to consider. Jack Strand and Cooper Rush threw the ball well and operated the offense effectively, Tyler Goodson, Nate Carter, and Cash Jones all ran well, Chris Blair, Vinny Anthony, and Jack Velling stood out as pass catchers, the offensive line did better, and the defense completely shut down Indianapolis with strong performances more or less across the board. It was the kind of effort that you definitely want to see from players hoping to make the roster, and if it makes evaluating battles and making decisions a little tougher, that’s fantastic. Here’s a full drive-by-drive recap of the game you just watched. 1st Quarter Nick Folk kicked us off, and Deon Burks slipped free to get across the 50 before the flag brought it back. A quick handoff up the middle for Seth McGowan picked up four yards. Riley Leonard looked for Laquon Treadwell, who was tied up as the pass fell incomplete. The blitz didn’t get home on third down and Leonard ran for a first down, but a holding call on the Colts backed it up to 3rd and 16. McGowan picked up about six yards on third down, but the Colts had to punt. Zachariah Branch brought it back a few yards. Cooper Rush threw a bullet to Branch for 15 yards on first down. Branch then got a handoff that went for maybe a yard, followed by Tyler Goodson picking up three yards. Rush then hit tight end Jack Velling for a first down over the middle. Goodson then evaded a tackle for four yards. Goodson then ran outside to the right, but the blocking wasn’t there and he was limited to a yard. Rush then whipped one into the dirt trying to get Branch, setting up a 51 yarder that Nick Folk easily hit. Falcons 3, Colts 0. Kendal Daniels delivered the nice hit on the return, and the Colts backed up again thanks to a holding call. McGowan picked up five yards on first down. Leonard then found a wide open receiver on the sideline for 39 yards. McGowan evaded one hit but DeMarcco Hellams got him after six yards. Pressure got to Leonard from JD Bertrand and he threw it short to Pharaoh Brown, with a big hit from Hellams for a small loss. A quick run for Burks went for a couple of yards to set up a field goal. Spencer Shrader juuuuuust hit the 48 yarder to make it 3-3. Goodson brought the kick return across the 40, continuing to strengthen his hold on a roster spot. Nate Carter took the handoff a yard. Then Rush hit Nick Muse for nine yards, thanks to Muse fighting through multiple tackle attempts. Carter then took it up the middle again and got the needed yard. Shane Steichen challenged the spot for no apparent reason but the ruling was upheld. Then Goodson got loose and took it 49 yards for a touchdown on the single most impressive play of the preseason to this point. 10-3 Falcons , but there was a 15 yard penalty for unsportsmanlike conduct call after the play that made Folk work a little harder for the extra point. The return went back to about the 30. McGowan picked up two yards. The throw to Raymond Sharp was knocked away by CJ Henderson, but Henderson was called for pass interference and it was a first down. McGowan was stonewalled on first down, but Sydney Brown was called for unsportsmanslike conduct. Leonard then led his receiver too much and Darnay Holmes ensured it wasn’t complete by getting some contact at the very end of the play. The Falcons then sniffed out the screen to Burks, with Kendal Daniels getting the tackle for no real gain. The Falcons got pressure and almost took Leonard down, and he dirted his pass. Shrader hit the 53 yarder, though, to make it 10-6 Falcons. Vinny Anthony took it past the 30. Jack Velling reeled in the short catch and picked up four yards, fighting for yards. Then Nate Carter did a nice job of running it up the middle for a first down. Then Rush hit a diving Chris Blair over the middle for 18 yards, cancelling out two penalties on the Colts. Carter then got maybe a yard to end the quarter. 2nd Quarter Carter then stumbled his way for four yards, and looked sharper as a runner in this one than he did in the first preseason game. Then Rush hit Anthony over the middle and he kept running for 17 yards. Goodson was stopped after just a yard on first down. Rush then hit Goodson for six yards. Goodson then got the handoff and maybe got a yard despite evading a tackle attempt. The Falcons went for it on fourth down with a pass to Blair, but a flag on the Colts put the ball on the one yard line. Carter then tried to plunge it in from a yard out and didn’t quite get there. Rush’s sneak went nowhere on second down. Carter was almost stuffed, but fought through contact impressively to get into the end zone. Falcons 17, Colts 6. The Colts returned it to the 30. McGowan was swallowed up immediately by Natrone Brooks and company for a loss of two, with offsetting penalties. The blitz got home for Leonard and he threw it a little low and incomplete, with a hit from Cam Sample on the play. Leonard then hit the 3rd and 12 pass, but an illegal hands to the face on the offense backed them up 10 yards. The third down screen pass was low and fell incomplete. Punt, and a solid return of nine yards by Anthony. A flip to Goodson picked up six yards, but a holding call on Andrew Stueber brought it back. A quick pass to Anthony picked up a few yards, and then Rush hit Velling for a first down, but holding brought it back again. Stueber again, too. A draw to Nate Carter got about seven yards. Jake Bailey’s punt was downed at the three yard line by Darren Hall. A one yard run and then a three yard run paired up. Then Leonard missed on third down. Punt. Carter then picked up three yards, and Jack Strand was in at quarterback, but Carter was tackled for a loss on the next play. Strand then hit Velling for a first down. Strand then rolled out and hit Muse for another first down. Strand then fired one in to Blair for about 20 yards and another gain. Strand then scrambled for about six yards. Cash Jones then took the handoff for a couple of yards. A quick pass unde pressure from Strand to Jones went for six. 24-6 Falcons. Josh Woods then made the big tackle. A first down pass and then a seven yard pass ensued for the Colts. A long pass from Leonard was called back by an offensive pass interference. A quick dumpoff went for eight yards. Then Leonard was tipped on the next play. Punt, and that’s the half. 3rd Quarter Atlanta ball. Strand rolled out and found Josh Simon for a first down, with Simon picking up plenty of yards after the catch. Carter then picked up maybe a yard. Strand then threw one a little off balance but connected with Antwane Wells Jr. deep. Then he ran it in himself from 20 yards, showing off the wheels, and putting the Falcons up 31-6. Anthony Richardson connected on a first down ball, but a penalty brought it back. Richardson then missed on 1st and 20. Anderson Castle took it four yards on second down. Richardson then found a receiver for about 10 yards, but it wasn’t enough. Punt.…

summary: The Baltimore Ravens notched their second straight preseason victory under new head coach Jesse Minter on Saturday afternoon, besting the Minnesota Vikings by a score of 13-3. As with last week’s win over the Philadelphia Eagles, Baltimore’s stifling defense controlled the game, particularly in the second half when they forced turnovers on Minnesota’s last three […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Silas Walters #36 of the Baltimore Ravens celebrates after intercepting the ball against the Minnesota Vikings during the fourth quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens notched their second straight preseason victory under new head coach Jesse Minter on Saturday afternoon, besting the Minnesota Vikings by a score of 13-3. As with last week’s win over the Philadelphia Eagles, Baltimore’s stifling defense controlled the game, particularly in the second half when they forced turnovers on Minnesota’s last three drives of the game. The unit finished with five sacks, forced two turnovers, and held the Vikings offense to a combined 6-17 on third and fourth down. Practice paying off for Mike Green! For more highlights, visit https://t.co/ciLFizvHBw . pic.twitter.com/CN9q1kfB7P — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) August 22, 2026 The Ravens’ young defensive line were particularly impactful, both off the edge and on the interior. Outside linebackers Mike Green and Ethan Burke flashed on multiple plays, while defensive tackles Aeneas Peebles, C.J. Okoye, and David Olajiga all made their presence known in Minnesota’s backfield. Secondary coverage was somewhat shaky in the first half with safety Silas Walters allowing multiple explosive connections downfield. The undrafted rookie bounced back in the fourth quarter, making a perfect read to undercut a dig route for an interception. Other standout defensive backs include Keondre Jackson and Chandler Rivers, who not only secured roster spots but made cases for regular-season roles in Minter’s defense. INTERCEPTION! ANOTHER RAVENS TAKEAWAY! Tune in now on @wbaltv11 . pic.twitter.com/BWXApNBQSG — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) August 22, 2026 Baltimore’s offense got off to a slow start with three straight three-and-outs, but Tyler Huntley put together a nine-play, 70-yard drive to open the second quarter that resulted in a 49-yard Tyler Loop field goal. The second-year kicker was only called on twice more for an extra point and a 20-yard field goal, both of which split the uprights. In the second half, undrafted rookie quarterback Joe Fagnano put up his second stellar performance in a row, driving the offense down the field on multiple scoring drives with several strong passes with pressure in his face. He finished with 15 completions on 20 attempts for 123 yards, one touchdown, zero interceptions, and just one sack. The former UConn starter may be playing himself into 53-man roster consideration, as capable young quarterbacks often get poached off the practice squad once injuries start mounting during the regular season. TOUCHDOWN, @la_wester !! Tune in on WBAL! pic.twitter.com/KoqrjHjVMD — Baltimore Ravens (@Ravens) August 22, 2026 After watching the Ravens’ other three pass-catching draft picks excel last week, rookie tight end Josh Cuevas took his turn in the spotlight with a team-high 46 yards. Receivers Devontez Walker, LaJohntay Wester, and Dayton Wade all made multiple catches with Wester scoring his team’s only touchdown of the day on a eight-yard pass from Fagnano in the fourth quarter. Ja’Kobi Lane and Elijah Sarratt played surprisingly little, suggesting that offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has already seen all he needs to from the rookie wideouts to give them targets in the regular season. The Ravens did not get much clarity on their starting center competition on Saturday. Jovaughn Gwyn, who impressed against the Eagles and during joint practices with the Vikings, did not stand out, while veteran Ethan Pocic put forth a competent if unspectacular 31 snaps in his first extended work since last year’s Achilles tear. The Ravens are returning to Baltimore on Saturday with three training camp practices scheduled for this week, including a joint session with the Washington Commanders on Wednesday ahead of their preseason finale on Friday at M&T Bank Stadium.

summary: The Baltimore Ravens won their second preseason game against the Minnesota Vikings by a score of 13-3. Stock up OLB Ethan Burke Burke stuffed the stat sheet in Minnesota, finishing with two tackles, two passes defended, one sack, and one […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Joe Fagnano #12 of the Baltimore Ravens passes the ball against the Minnesota Vikings during the second quarter of the preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens won their second preseason game against the Minnesota Vikings by a score of 13-3. Here is an instant stock report from Baltimore Beatdown’s staff coming out of the victory. Stock up OLB Ethan Burke Burke stuffed the stat sheet in Minnesota, finishing with two tackles, two passes defended, one sack, and one forced fumble. His work on coverage was particularly impressive – he surged to the ball to strip the ball with Jay Higgins on one play and later had a PBU that could have easily been a pick six. The undrafted rookie out of Texas is making a strong roster case through two preseason games. – Nikhil Mehta QB Joe Fagnano For the second week in a row, the undrafted rookie quarterback looked like he belonged on an NFL field. Fagnano’s most impressive trait has been his ability to remain poised under pressure to deliver the pass on target. It seems unlikely that anything Fagnano could have done this preseason would have unseated Tyler Huntley as the backup quarterback, but he is making it difficult to keep him off the 53-man roster after back-to-back impressive showings. – Dustin Cox OLB Mike Green After a quiet outing against the Eagles, Green made his presence felt on the second drive against the Vikings with a sack followed by a pressure that resulted in a holding call on the next play. The 2025 second-round pick looks ready for a breakout sophomore campaign. – Kevin McNelis DT Aeneas Peebles Peebles showed some great burst on his first steps tracking down the ball-carrier. He was involved in several run-stuffing plays and was in the area for a drive-killing third down sack of Carson Wentz. He added a few more pressures in the pass rush and looks like a disruptive young piece for this Ravens defensive line. – Kevin McNelis P Ryan Eckley After shanking his first NFL punt last week, Eckley been awesome. His second pinned the Eagles at the 10-yard line and he launched bombs downfield all afternoon in Minnesota. He totaled 332 yards on six punts (55.3 yards per punt), including a field-flipper that forced the Vikings to start at their own 4. – Zach Canter TE Josh Cuevas Last week it was rookie fourth-round tight end Matthew Hibner showing off his receiving chops against the Eagles, but this week was fellow rookie fifth-round tight end Josh Cuevas’ chance to do so. Cuevas led the team with 46 receiving yards on three catches. The Ravens will need at least one of their two rookie tight ends to contribute on Sundays this season. – Dustin Cox Stock Down G Vega Ioane Ioane impressed in his NFL debut last week, but he struggled out of the gate in Minnesota. He missed a run block, committed a holding penalty, and allowed a pressure that Tyler Huntley narrowly kept from becoming a sack. Is it anything to worry about? Probably not, but it is a sign that Ioane’s All-Pro ceiling is just that: a ceiling. He’s still a rookie offensive lineman who will have to take his lumps in the NFL. – Nikhil Mehta OLB Adisa Isaac Isaac was quiet for a second game in a row. It’s great to see him healthy and on the field, but he still has to flash some NFL talent to make a competitive defensive roster. Ethan Burke looked more deserving of the fifth outside linebacker spot in Minnesota by a wide margin. Is Isaac’s 2024 third-round draft status enough to keep him around? – Nikhil Mehta

title: Ravens WR Rashod Bateman facing multiple criminal charges in Georgia
summary: Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman is facing three criminal charges in Walton County, Georgia, after allegedly smashing the windshield of a car occupied by his 3-month-old child and their mother, according to Jonas Shaffer of the Baltimore Banner. The incident, which was first reported by TMZ, took place on the morning of June 3. […]
full_text: BALTIMORE, MD - DECEMBER 07: Rashod Bateman #7 of the Baltimore Ravens looks on before the game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at M&T Bank Stadium on December 7, 2025 in Baltimore, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images Baltimore Ravens wide receiver Rashod Bateman is facing three criminal charges in Walton County, Georgia, after allegedly smashing the windshield of a car occupied by his 3-month-old child and their mother, according to Jonas Shaffer of the Baltimore Banner . The incident, which was first reported by TMZ , took place on the morning of June 3. Bateman, a Georgia native, turned himself in later that day. The 26-year-old was charged with one felony – first-degree criminal damage to property – and two misdemeanors – family violence battery and reckless conduct. The first charge carries up to a year of jail time. A Ravens spokesperson issued the following statement regarding Bateman’s arrest: “We are aware of the situation involving Rashod and have been in direct communication with him. We notified the league office and have been cooperating throughout the process. As this is a pending legal matter, we will not have further comment.” Bateman’s lawyer, Jordan Siev, also provided a statement to news outlets: “It is unfortunate that a personal family situation has been taken completely out of context for sensational reasons. We will let the court process play out, and the facts will come out at that time.” The matter is under review by the NFL and could result in a suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy, which mandates a six-game minimum suspension for any family-related violence. The presence of Bateman’s infant in the car could be considered an aggravating factor in levying a more severe punishment.

title: Buffalo Bills dominate Cleveland Browns in preseason action
summary: The Buffalo Bills and the Cleveland Browns faced off in Week Two of the 2026 NFL preseason, and after a lengthy lightning delay, the teams were able to complete a fairly competitive game. Buffalo’s first drive was put on hold after just 1:39 of game time thanks to strong storms that blew through the area, […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - AUGUST 22: Michael Coats Jr. #39 of the Cleveland Browns tackles Ray Davis #7 of the Buffalo Bills during the first quarter of a preseason game at Huntington Bank Field on August 22, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills and the Cleveland Browns faced off in Week Two of the 2026 NFL preseason, and after a lengthy lightning delay, the teams were able to complete a fairly competitive game. Buffalo’s first drive was put on hold after just 1:39 of game time thanks to strong storms that blew through the area, as the game began in heavy rains. After the delay, though, much better weather prevailed, and the teams were able to complete the exhibition. With both teams playing mostly backups, it was a good day to watch some depth pieces make their case for the 53-man roster. Buffalo’s depth showed out strongly, and they spearheaded the club to a blowout win. Here’s our stock report after the Bills’ second preseason game. Horns Up: Trent Sherfield Sr. With a battered receiving corps, the Bills needed players to eat snaps. These backup wideout had a chance to show their mettle, as well. Sherfield may not be a young pup, and he has plenty of NFL film to show what he is at this point in his career, but he showed himself to be a reliable target on Saturday. He was a frequent recipient of Kyle Allen passes in the first half, catching a few longer gains on the Bills’ rain-delayed opening drive, which ended with a touchdown. Sherfield also showed off as a gunner on special teams, combining with fellow reserve wideout Stephen Gosnell on a tackle after rookie punter Tommy Doman’s 50-yard punt on Buffalo’s second possession. I’ve long felt that Sherfield is the most likely WR6 in camp thanks to his ability on special teams, but he flashed some value on offense, as well. He helped his case for the 53-man roster today. Horns Up and Down: Mecole Hardman Jr As with Sherfield Sr., Hardman Jr. saw some extra reps on offense thanks to the injuries at receiver. Unlike Sherfield Sr., Hardman Jr. did not make the most of his opportunities. He dropped two passes, both of which came on third downs and would have given the Bills first-down yardage. Hardman Jr. did a nice job on a kickoff return after Cleveland scored a touchdown in the second quarter, gaining 30 yards to set the Bills up in solid field position. However, with running back Ray Davis as the reigning All-Pro kickoff returner while also looking to add the punt-return role to his resume, Hardman Jr. is going to need to be useful as a wideout in order to make the team. Hardman Jr. had a good two-minute drill at the end of the first half, making a first-down grab to start things off before capping the drive with a nine-yard catch and run on a wide receiver screen with just 15 seconds remaining in the first half. Hardman Jr. has the juice to help out in multiple roles, but he needs to show consistency in order to do so, something that has been hard for him throughout his career. Horns Up: Kyle Allen Josh Allen’s backup had himself another solid outing, looking, poised, decisive, and accurate in first-half action. Kyle Allen completed 10-of-12 passes for 128 yards and a touchdown. That included some long gainers to Sherfield Sr., as well as a big-time pass to Ja’Mori Maclin in the aforementioned two-minute drill, which set up Hardman Jr.‘s touchdown grab. Yes, it was only the preseason, and yes, it was against the Cleveland Browns’ backups. However, No. 11 did exactly what he was supposed to do given the scenario. Horns Down: Damar Hamlin Yes, he had an interception in the first half. That play was less a result of something Hamlin did than it was good fortune, as linebacker Joe Andreessen made the nice play to knock the ball into the air and Hamlin just happened to be in the right place at the right time. Otherwise, Hamlin was fooled multiple times by misdirection, and he allowed some big gains in coverage when he was just a step or two slow in trying to cover his assignment. The Bills are going to have some tough decisions to make in the defensive secondary, and while there is something to be said about keeping a heady veteran like Hamlin for depth, the Bills might be better off rolling the dice on the youth, athleticism, and versatility of players like Jordan Hancock and Jalon Kilgore. Horns Up: Footballers Who Use Their Feet Tyler Bass drilled a 52-yard field goal in the second half; he also hit on two extra points in the first half and two more in the second half. Rookie Tommy Doman Jr. landed two punts inside the 20-yard line, including a 50-yard boot, while averaging 43 yards per punt. Mitch Wishnowsky hit an absolute missile on his first punt, drilling a 59-yard boot that was only returned for one yard. Overall, Buffalo’s special teams group looked solid. It was nice to see Bass hit from range, and while punting is never fun, it was good to see the rookie perform in his first real action. Horns Down: Shane Buechele Sure, he’s the third-string guy, but Buechele showed once again that he has neither the arm strength nor the consistent accuracy to be an NFL quarterback. Buffalo would be wise to look for a younger player to develop for their practice squad, someone who might have some long-term viability as an NFL passer, sooner rather than later. Buechele still might make the practice squad for this season, and as he showed on the touchdown pass he threw to Ja’Mori Maclin, he can sneak one in on shorter routes. He also has enough mobility to give other third-stringers problems. However, the Bills should be looking to replace him as soon as they feel comfortable doing so. Horns Up: Depth Corners Last week, it was Kani Walker making a fabulous play to intercept a Carolina Panthers pass. This week, it was Te’Cory Couch going up and catching a ball that Jordan Dunbar deflected to intercept Deshaun Watson. Dunbar and Walker made some nice plays in the run game, as well, as they showed zero fear in sticking their head in to deliver some punishment around the line of scrimmage. Davison Igbinosun looked good in that regard, as well, totaling four tackles and one tackle for loss in his limited action. The Bills might lack name recognition in the defensive secondary, but it seems as if they have a strong young core of defensive backs to choose from heading into the regular season. Horns Down: Maxwell Hairston Maybe this is unfair, as the second-year man has been nursing an injury for much of the summer and he has yet to play this preseason. However, Hairston was injured for much of last season, as well, and his continued inability to suit up is only giving other players a chance to show that they can do his job. Igbinosun, in particular, has garnered lots of buzz this summer, and while someone like Walker or Dunbar might not be considered true threats to Hairston’s role on the team, they have done a nice job with their opportunities. Hairston might not be on the roster bubble, but the CB2 job appears to be very much up for grabs. Horns Up: Ja’Mori Maclin This guy can run a little bit! Maclin made two huge plays, catching a 71-yard touchdown pass in the second half where he took a simple shallow drag route and sprinted to paydirt. He also made a huge grab on Buffalo’s final scoring drive of the first half, hauling in a Kyle Allen lob for a 37-yard gain to put that scoring drive in business. Maclin played like a man who knew he had a big opportunity to prove himself, and while he might still fall short of the 53-man roster, he made the coaching staff’s job more difficult with his ability to find space and beat corners off the line. Horns Down: Frank Gore Jr. Gore Jr. fumbled on his lone kickoff return attempt, and while he recovered his own fumble, it’s still not a great look. He also dropped a pass on a screen attempt in the fourth quarter, as he looked to run before he secured the grab. Finally, he once again looked like the slower, less explosive option…

title: Buffalo Bills DT Ed Oliver’s young son has passed away
summary: The Buffalo Bills are mourning the loss of the young son of defensive tackle Ed Oliver. Rumors began circulating Friday night with the NFL Network reporting it Saturday morning. The Bills confirmed the tragedy Saturday afternoon. Ed Oliver’s 2-year-old son has tragically passed away. “On behalf of the entire Buffalo Bills organization, we want to […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - NOVEMBER 13: Ed Oliver #91 of the Buffalo Bills pressures Russell Wilson #3 of the Denver Broncos during the first quarter of the game at Highmark Stadium on November 13, 2023 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Bryan M. Bennett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills are mourning the loss of the young son of defensive tackle Ed Oliver. Rumors began circulating Friday night with the NFL Network reporting it Saturday morning. The Bills confirmed the tragedy Saturday afternoon. Ed Oliver’s 2-year-old son has tragically passed away. “On behalf of the entire Buffalo Bills organization, we want to publicly express our condolences to Ed Oliver and his family on the devastating loss of his son. It’s an unthinkable tragedy for any parent. We will continue to support Ed and his family as we all grieve this tragic loss,” said general manager Brandon Beane in a statement released by the team. The Bills and Oliver have not released any details at this time. The organization has known about the incident the entire time and honored Oliver’s wish to not disclose it publicly, according to ESPN’s Adam Schefter. The incident reportedly occurred in late June at Oliver’s suburban Houston home, where first responders were called for an unresponsive young male who had been pulled from a pool. Oliver was born and raised in Houston and played for the University of Houston. Oliver has been in attendance at the team’s training camp throughout July and August but missed this week’s joint practices in Cleveland with an injury. Some outlets have connected the absence to his son’s death but we have no indication that is the case. Our condolences go out to Oliver and his family.

(Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills are on the other end of Lake Erie this weekend, set to meet the Cleveland Browns for Week 2 of the 2026 NFL preseason. A week ago now, Buffalo smacked the Carolina Panthers 29-14 in the team’s preseason debut at the new Highmark Stadium. This weekend? They’re due west for a classic AFC rustbelt matchup. This is the Bills’ only road game of the preseason, though they did take advantage of the opportunity in leveraging a joint practice with the Browns earlier in the week. Head coach Joe Brady initially stated that how long starters played this weekend would depend on how things went in the joint practice. If they saw all that was needed, then it’s likely the bulk of starters give way to those on the roster battling to make an impression towards Buffalo’s roster depth. However, it’s clear that new defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard is working overtime to install his system, which sees the Bills shifting toward an attack-based 3-4 scheme. It’s anyone’s guess if that, alone, plays a role in who plays on defense, and for how long today in Cleveland. Of course everyone knows only one thing that matters at the end of the day, and it’s not the score. The Browns boast a stout defense led by a certain future first-ballot NFL Hall of Fame defensive end in Myles Garrett. That means Buffalo’s offense should tread lightly in a game meant to provide evaluation and practice. With that, here’s your open thread for today’s preseason game between the Bills and Browns! As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

title: Bills vs. Browns: Preseason game No. 2 gets questions answered
summary: The second preseason game is the tipping point of the summer for NFL teams. It’s when the fun, out-of-nowhere training camp stories, underdog-starring late July novelties that refuel fans for football season, either vanish into thin air or mature into serious narratives for the regular season and beyond. Will the fan-favorite journeyman actually work his […]
full_text: ORCHARD PARK, NEW YORK - AUGUST 15: Ian Wheeler #27 of the Buffalo Bills runs the ball in for a touchdown during the second half against the Carolina Panthers at Highmark Stadium on August 15, 2026 in Orchard Park, New York. (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The second preseason game is the tipping point of the summer for NFL teams. It’s when the fun, out-of-nowhere training camp stories, underdog-starring late July novelties that refuel fans for football season, either vanish into thin air or mature into serious narratives for the regular season and beyond. Will the fan-favorite journeyman actually work his way into the rotation when the games count? How about that Day 3 rookie? Or will they both fade to memory? The first preseason week is a feeling-out process. After weeks cracking helmets against teammates — relatively gently, of course — the opening exhibition game allows players to dip their toes into the competitive waters once again. Coaches shake off play-calling rust. Preseason game No. 2 is an entirely different animal. Teams are now close to being fully settled in. They’ve gotten into the game-week groove. For some teams, this has become the dress rehearsal for the regular season, when starters get extensive first-half work before backups fight mercilessly for final spots on the 53-man. Others sit all the starters. But the second preseason game tells us a lot. And getting this preseason game after a spirited, full-bore joint practice makes for ideal timing for roster-curation. That’s precisely what the Bills are getting today after practicing the Browns on Thursday. Can Ian Wheeler continue to steamroll the competition en route to chasing down Frank Gore Jr. for the primary practice squad runner or something more? As promised, here's #Bills RB Ian Wheeler lowering his shoulder today in the joint practice with the Browns. A thud loud enough that everyone could hear and one that got the entire Buffalo offense hyped up. Josh Allen said Wheeler is a "low runner" with a lot of power. @WGRZ https://t.co/sErOib16h2 pic.twitter.com/0NtIT8VBVU — Jonathan Acosta (@JAcostaTV) August 20, 2026 Who will seize the opportunity as WR5 or WR6 with a bevy of Buffalo receivers sidelined with injury? Does Skyler Bell see the field for his first NFL action after missing the opening preseasong game? Who seizes the starting left guard job? How about backup center? And what does Jim Leonhard do with three inside linebackers vying for two jobs at that position? How does safety shake out? Who’s named Buffalo’s main big nickel defender? How about the safeties behind CJ Gardner-Johnson and Cole Bishop? Heck, the Bills are suddenly loaded at tight end too — don’t forget about Keleki Latu and veteran Shane Zylstra, both of whom turned in quality performances against Carolina a week ago. A lot remains unanswered. For now. Regular-season decisions will be made based on the individual efforts given by Bills players today. That’s what makes preseason game No. 2 so darn important.

title: Buffalo Bills 2026 scouting report: running back James Cook III
summary: The Buffalo Bills were the top rushing team in the NFL last season, leading the league in total carries (547), rushing yards (2,714), and rushing touchdowns (30). They also tied for the league lead in total first downs rushing, notching 146 first downs to lead the league with the Baltimore Ravens. Buffalo also led the […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 12: James Cook #4 of the Buffalo Bills scores a touchdown against the Miami Dolphins during the first quarter in the game at Hard Rock Stadium on September 12, 2024 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Buffalo Bills were the top rushing team in the NFL last season, leading the league in total carries (547), rushing yards (2,714), and rushing touchdowns (30). They also tied for the league lead in total first downs rushing, notching 146 first downs to lead the league with the Baltimore Ravens. Buffalo also led the league in another, less positive category, as they fumbled 12 times on rushing plays. Their top running back had six of those fumbles, and while he was the NFL’s leading rusher, he also turned the ball over more than the team would have liked. Does that mean they should have given him the ball less? Absolutely not. However, it does point to an area where he can improve moving forward. In today’s edition of “91 players in 91 days,” we discuss the NFL’s leading rusher in 2025. _____________________________________________________________________________ Name: James Cook III Number: 4 Position: RB Height/Weight: 5’11” 190 lbs. Age: 26 (27 on 9/25/2026) Experience/Draft: 5; selected by Buffalo in the second round (No. 63 overall) of the 2022 NFL Draft) College: Georgia Acquired: Second-round draft choice Financial situation (per Spotrac): Cook III enters the first year of the four-year, $46 million extension he signed prior to last season. He carries a cap hit of $5.88 million this season. Buffalo would carry a dead cap charge of $22.83 million if he were to be released. 2025 Recap: After an offseason where Cook III expressed displeasure over his contract, he signed a new deal and immediately went out and showed that he was worth it. Cook became the first Buffalo player since O.J. Simpson in 1976 to lead the NFL in rushing, as he set career-highs in carries (309) and rushing yards (1,621). He hit double-figures in rushing touchdowns for the second straight year, scoring on 12 runs. And, while his passing game usage still felt like it could be a greater asset, he saw 40 targets on the season, catching 33 passes for 291 yards and two scores. Cook also played on a career-high 639 offensive snaps in the regular season, which represented a career-high total of 56% of the team’s total snaps. In the playoffs, Cook III remained outstanding, though he was much less efficient. He carried 39 times for 163 yards, averaging a full yard per carry less than he did in the regular season (4.2 yards per carry in the postseason as opposed to 5.2 yards per carry in the regular season). With that increase in touches, though, came an increase in fumbles. He fumbled a career-high seven times, including six fumbles in the regular season. He was named to the Pro Bowl Games for the third straight season, and he was Second-Team All-Pro for the first time in his career. Positional outlook: Cook III is one of five running backs on the current roster. Ray Davis, Ty Johnson, Frank Gore Jr., and Ian Wheeler are the others. Ben VanSumeran is the team’s only fullback. 2026 Offseason: Cook III is healthy and he has participated in both training camp practices and preseason action so far this summer. 2026 Season outlook: How will Cook’s body react after touching the football 385 times last season in Buffalo’s 19 games that counted? That’s really the only question that needs answering, as Cook III had been “babied” a bit in terms of his snap counts and his touches prior to last season, especially in comparison to the big jump in both categories that he took last season. He has earned every penny of his four-year, $46 million extension, and he’s arguably outperformed it already given the recent explosion of running back contracts in the NFL. That’s not to say that he should hold out, or that he will hold out, for a new deal, but it does show how prescient the move to sign him was when general manager Brandon Beane and Cook’s agents agreed to the deal. It also might be a little crazy given that this is technically the first year in which he’s playing under its terms, but I digress. Cook III had 299 touches between the regular season and postseason in 2024, and he had 325 total touches during the 2023 regular season and postseason combined. That’s a lot of punishment over a three-year span, and a nearly 100-touch jump year over year is quite a lot. Cook III has shown a penchant for avoiding big hits throughout his career, which bodes well for his continued durability, but I do wonder if he’ll see fewer carries this season in an attempt to manage the beating he takes just a bit. Head coach Joe Brady called him the league’s best running back , and has said that he expects Buffalo’s top rusher to take another step forward this season. Whether that step includes more usage in the passing game is yet to be seen, but we can assume that is where the step will be taken this year. Whatever the Bills do, though, they need to continue involving No. 4 in the offense. He is a dynamic runner no matter how the Bills put the ball in his hands. If he can clean up the fumbles that appeared last season, he can be even better than he was last year. Cook III is an elite running back, and a top-flight offensive weapon on a team that continues to be one of the league’s best scoring offenses. I expect that he’ll have lower total numbers this season, but hopefully the trade-off is that he remains just as efficient with a slight reduction in touches.

title: 2026 Season Opener Countdown: 22 Days Remaining
summary: Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to […]
full_text: CHARLOTTE, NORTH CAROLINA - JANUARY 10: Taylor Moton #72 of the Carolina Panthers runs onto the field prior to an NFL wild card playoff football game against the Los Angeles Rams at Bank of America Stadium on January 10, 2026 in Charlotte, North Carolina. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here at Cat Scratch Reader we have counted down the final 100 days leading up to the Carolina Panthers season opener by for at least the past ten years. We’ve always done this by highlighting the current player on the roster whose jersey number matches the day on the countdown. This year, we decided to change that up a bit by counting down our own list of the Top 100 Panthers of all time. This does not correspond to jersey number, does not need to be somebody who wore a jersey, and will in no way be controversial. #22. Taylor Moton At the moment, it looks like the Carolina Panthers are going to start the season without the services of Taylor Moton. It’s not a familiar spot for the Panthers to be. Moton has been one of the most reliable offensive linemen in the entire league, much less the Panthers, and he’s been doing it for a long time. The Panthers drafted Moton at the back end of the second round of the 2017 NFL Draft. He spent his entire rookie season as a reserve, playing sparingly on special teams and in spot duty as an extra tackle. He earned the starting nod at right tackle going into his second season, and he has yet to relinquish that spot. He played 6,787 consecutive snaps at right tackle across six-plus seasons. He finally missed his first snaps in the fifth game of the 2024 season after playing every snap of the six previous seasons. He would miss three games in 2024 and one in 2025. Other than that, he’s never come off the field when the offense is on it. Moton’s got more to his game than durability though. He’s been a very good if unheralded right tackle throughout his time in Carolina. He’s never earned any postseason accolades, but he’s always been a comfortably above average tackle. With how much any offensive line is ravaged by injury and roster turnover from year to year, having the ever reliable Moton at right tackle has provided some much needed security. Moton is currently on the non-football injury/illness list as he recovers from a blood clot in his lungs. That’s a scary prognosis, but Moton seems to be doing well and is expected to be back during the season. We obviously wish him a speedy recovery both for his own personal wellbeing and his ability to help the Panthers. His spot as a constant on the right side of the offensive line and the quality of play he’s brought to that spot has earned him spot number 22 on the list of the top 100 Panthers of all time.

summary: For the first time in the Ben Johnson era, the Chicago Bears lost a preseason game. Considering the Bears began the game with most of their starters while the Bengals played their twos, […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Chicago Bears quarterback Case Keenum (11) hands the ball off to running back Roschon Johnson (23) in the first half against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For the first time in the Ben Johnson era, the Chicago Bears lost a preseason game. The Cincinnati Bengals won handily, 27 to 9, and I have a feeling the film session with Johnson will not be fun. Considering the Bears began the game with most of their starters while the Bengals played their twos, the game didn’t start the way the Bears had hoped. The first-string offense stalled on their first and only drive and settled for a 45-yard field goal, while Cincinnati’s second offense drove down the field against the Bears’ defense fairly easily, eating up 7:01 in time of possession, before getting a field goal of their own. The Bears used a heavy dose of Roschon Johnson in the first half (12 runs, 42 yards), including on a 4th-and-a-foot from their own 15 that they converted right before the two-minute warning. But that drive only went three more plays before Tory Taylor punted it away. The teams had traded scores up to this point, but Cincinnati’s offense drove down and added a Josh Johnson-to-Tanner Hudson touchdown to take a 17-6 lead into the half. OR SO THEY THOUGHT! After a 16-yard run by Salvon Ahmed set the Bears up with a 1st and 10 from the Bengals 49, Case Keenum led the Bears into field goal range with a couple of completions. Cairo Santos hit his third to pull the score to 17-9. Cincy added another TD to open the third period, and the quarter just kind of petered out. The Bengals added a fourth-quarter field goal, and the game came to an end. Chicago was sloppy in all three phases, and their 11 penalties for 81 yards only made it worse. The Bears play the Tennessee Titans in a week to close out the preseason, and they do have a joint practice scheduled during the week. title: Erick All Jr. makes long-awaited return to the field after almost a year and a half
summary: The best story out of Saturday night in the Queen City was Erick All Jr. making his 2026 debut as the Cincinnati Bengals took on the Chicago Bears. All missed the final part of his 2024 rookie season after suffering a torn ACL in his right knee. After that, complications arose from a previous injury […]
full_text: The best story out of Saturday night in the Queen City was Erick All Jr. making his 2026 debut as the Cincinnati Bengals took on the Chicago Bears. All missed the final part of his 2024 rookie season after suffering a torn ACL in his right knee. After that, complications arose from a previous injury All sustained in college, leading to a second surgery on the knee the following offseason, forcing him to miss the entire 2025 season. The Bengals have been limiting him throughout camp, hoping to ramp him up to be fully healthy when the regular season starts on September 13th. All sat out during the first preseason game as part of that process. Thankfully, he dressed out and went through stretches with the team prior to the game. Despite logging several snaps, All did not see a target, but that’s not important. Not on this night. The real story was he was back in an NFL game for the first time in nearly a year and a half. All is a versatile player at the tight end position when he is healthy. He can line up all over the formation; he loves the physicality as a blocker, and he can make plays in the passing game. It is a welcome sight to see him out on the football field. And unless there’s some sort of setback, All is expected to make the 53-man roster and hopefully get back to the player we saw before his rookie season ended.

title: 7 winners and 3 losers from the Bengals’ 27-9 win vs. Bears
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals played their second of three preseason games—and their last one in front of a home crowd—on Saturday night. They put on a show for the home crowd, defeating the Bears by a final score of 27-9 and moving to a meaningless 2-0 to start the 2026 campaign. Even though the game didn’t […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Cincinnati, Ohio, USA; Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Josh Johnson (11) throws a pass against the Chicago Bears in the first half at Paycor Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Katie Stratman-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Cincinnati Bengals played their second of three preseason games—and their last one in front of a home crowd—on Saturday night. They put on a show for the home crowd, defeating the Bears by a final score of 27-9 and moving to a meaningless 2-0 to start the 2026 campaign. Even though the game didn’t matter, and even though the Bengals rested their starters, there was a lot to be excited about (and a couple of things that weren’t so exciting). Here are this year’s winners and losers. Winners Colbie Young The positions of WR1 and WR2 are set in stone, and so are WR3 and WR4 as well. It’s possible that WR5 and WR6 are up for grabs, though, and there are three people vying for those two last spots. Colbie Young may have sealed one of those two spots on Sunday. Trailing 6-3 late in the second quarter, Young beat his man deep down the right sideline and caught a pass from Josh Johnson in the end zone to give the Bengals a 10-6 lead. He finished with three receptions for 48 yards (which led the team) and a touchdown. Dohnte Meyers Meyers has been a camp favorite for many Bengals fans this offseason, and he was impressive during both preseason games so far. With Tee Higgins and Ja’Marr Chase sidelined for the team’s second preseason game, it was Young and Meyers leading the receiving room. He finished Saturday night’s game with five catches (which led the team) for 41 yards, as well as one run for nine yards. Josh Johnson The first half wasn’t super exciting offensively, but against the Bears’ starting defense, Johnson was able to move the ball down the field on a 14-play, 62-yard drive that ended in an Evan McPherson field goal. He later found Young in the end zone in the second quarter to take a four-point lead. He wrapped up his performance by leading the Bengals on another scoring drive, finding Tanner Hudson in the end zone with less than 30 seconds left in the half, giving the Bengals a 17-6 lead. Johnson may not play football in Cincinnati this year because of the Joe’s, but he showed he can still play. He played the entire first half and completed 15 of 23 passes for 156 yards and two touchdowns. Tanner Hudson Drew Sample and Mike Gesicki are on top of the depth chart, and Erick All Jr. is healthy. Jack Endries fell to the Bengals in the seventh round and has been impressive in the small amount of time we’ve seen him on the field. All of this means the pressure is on for Hudson. Hudson caught Johnson’s second touchdown pass in the second quarter from the six-yard line, giving the Bengals a two-score lead. I don’t think Hudson is on the outside looking in, but I don’t think his roster spot is set in stone either, so producing when he’s on the field is important. Landon Robinson Robinson is a seventh-round rookie on a team with a very deep defensive tackle rotation, thanks to the offseason additions of Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen, and others. With last year’s starters on the depth chart listed as backups, seeing Robinson knock down passes at the line of scrimmage in key moments and recording his first multiple-sack game gives me hope that the Bengals’ defensive line rotation will be outstanding in 2026. Al Golden The Bengals rested their starters on Saturday, which meant the Bengals’ defensive backups started the game against the Bears’ starting offense. It wouldn’t be that way for the whole game, as the Bears’ starters only played for a short period of time, but throughout the entire game, Golden’s defense was able to keep the Bears out of the end zone. The Bengals really only need a mediocre defense out of Golden’s crew, but he could piece together a top-10 unit with this roster. Evan McPherson Money Mac was two for two on field goals, including a 58-yarder, and made all three extra points. He’s been good from 56, 33, 41, 25, and 58 this preseason. Hopefully that continues into the regular season. Losers Any wide receiver not named Young, Meyers, or Tinsley Like I said above, the Bengals’ wide receiver position is loaded, and, at most, one or two spots are up for grabs. Those two spots are going to go to some combination of Young, Meyers, or Tinsley, which means anyone else on the team is going to be hoping for a practice squad position at best. Cody Ford Ford struggled badly on Saturday night against the Bears. He started the game at right guard and was called for two holding penalties and two false starts, all in the first half. It was Jalen Rivers who started at left tackle for the Bengals on Sunday, which means that Cody Ford, who was in consideration to be the team’s swing tackle, could be on the outs. The Bengals may need to think about adding depth along the offensive line before the season starts. Josh Newton Newton has struggled throughout camp this year and has reportedly been in the “doghouse.” With that said, it wasn’t a good time for Newton to get beat badly by Jahdae Walker down the left sideline for a 36-yard completion. That was the longest completion of the night for the Bears. Who was your biggest winner tonight? Sound off in the comments!

full_text: Cincinnati Bengals Joe Burrow answers questions from media during a press conference after practice at Paycor Stadium, Thursday, Aug. 20, 2026, in downtown Cincinnati. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co The Bengals, after years of half measures, seem to have finally pushed all their chips to the middle of the table. Now quarterback Joe Burrow feels the pressure, and he wants everyone in the building to feel it as well. “I’ve tried to instill an urgency in the room—a palpable pressure—because we have guys playing and coaching for their jobs this year,” he said to ESPN’s Marty Smith . “That’s how, you know, I’m looking at it. I’m playing for my job this year.” He went on to say he’s pushing for every player to attack every rep at every practice to get as much out of practice as possible. Entering his seventh season in the league, he knows what it takes to win, and he believes the Bengals have what they need. “We have the team to do it this year,” he said. “Now we have to take advantage of the opportunity.” The Bengals sent their No. 10 overall selection to the Giants in exchange for All-Pro nose tackle Dexter Lawrence II, signed Boye Mafe, Bryan Cook, Jonathan Allen and Kyle Dugger, completely reshaping the defense, and they kept the most loaded offense in the NFL together. On paper, they should be one of the most dominant teams in the league. For now, though, it’s all potential energy. Hopefully, they can turn it into something kinetic once the games actually matter.

title: Andrei Iosivas isn’t trying to prove himself anymore
summary: For most of Andrei Iosivas’ NFL career, there has been something to prove: Prove that a wide receiver from Princeton could play in the NFL; prove that a sixth-round draft pick belonged on the field with Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins; and prove that his rare combination of size and athleticism could translate into production […]
full_text: For most of Andrei Iosivas’ NFL career, there has been something to prove: Prove that a wide receiver from Princeton could play in the NFL; prove that a sixth-round draft pick belonged on the field with Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins; and prove that his rare combination of size and athleticism could translate into production against NFL defensive backs. Three years into his career with the Cincinnati Bengals, Iosivas doesn’t sound particularly interested in proving anything anymore. And that may be the best indication yet of how far he’s come. “I just feel like I am flowing and I am playing,” Iosivas said in a recent interview. “I’m happy about the way I approach the days. I’ve been focusing on how I walk into the building, how I get out to practice, and whatever happens, happens.” View this post on Instagram That’s quite a change from the player Cincinnati selected with the 206th overall pick in the 2023 NFL Draft. Iosivas arrived in Cincinnati as one of the more intriguing developmental prospects in that draft class. At 6-foot-3 and around 210 pounds, he had the physical traits, but he was making the jump from Ivy League football at Princeton to an offense featuring Joe Burrow, Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins. He has spent the past three seasons showing that he belongs. Iosivas played in 16 games as a rookie and caught 15 passes for 116 yards. Four of those 15 receptions went for touchdowns. His role grew substantially in 2024, when he caught 36 passes for 479 yards and six touchdowns. He followed that with 33 receptions for 435 yards and two scores in 2025. Add it all together, and Iosivas enters his fourth season with 84 receptions for 1,030 yards and 12 touchdowns. In short, he has become a regular part of Cincinnati’s offense, and his attitude appears to have evolved along with his game. “I feel like I’ve put out enough film and even in practice now,” Iosivas said. “I know who I am. I’m not excited to prove it to anybody else.” There is an important distinction there. Iosivas isn’t saying he has nothing left to accomplish. He’s saying he no longer needs outside validation to tell him whether he belongs. And that confidence could be particularly important this summer. While Chase and Higgins remain firmly entrenched at the top of Cincinnati’s receiver room, things are getting interesting behind them. Rookie fourth-round pick Colbie Young showed some of his potential in Cincinnati’s preseason opener against the Detroit Lions, catching two passes for 28 yards. Former CFL receiver Dohnte Meyers has also generated attention throughout training camp and continued to make his case against Detroit. Iosivas doesn’t sound like someone spending much time looking over his shoulder, though. Instead, he’s concentrating on himself. “I think a lot of guys in here, we just all make each other better, so it’s been really fun,” Iosivas said. “It’s a good group of guys, and you’ve just got to do you. Run your route, make the play, do whatever you need to do.” And that may be exactly what the Bengals need from him.

title: Former Browns RB Nick Chubb retires; Career stats include joining history
summary: Every Cleveland Browns fan can remember where they were when the Houston Texans announced that they had signed running back Nick Chubb. It was a sad day in Northeast Ohio. On Friday, Chubb announced his retirement from the NFL on an Instagram post. Chubb began the 2025 season as Houston’s lead running back, but his […]
full_text: CLEVELAND, OHIO - DECEMBER 15: Nick Chubb #24 of the Cleveland Browns carries the ball during the third quarter against the Kansas City Chiefs at Huntington Bank Field on December 15, 2024 in Cleveland, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Diamond Images via Getty Images) | Diamond Images/Getty Images Every Cleveland Browns fan can remember where they were when the Houston Texans announced that they had signed running back Nick Chubb. It was a sad day in Northeast Ohio. On Friday, Chubb announced his retirement from the NFL on an Instagram post. Chubb began the 2025 season as Houston’s lead running back, but his snaps became more limited as the season rolled along, and eventually fourth-round rookie Woody Marks surpassed him. Chubb concluded the season with just nine starts and 326 offensive snaps, or 32% of all offensive plays. RELATED: CAN WE TAKE A MINUTE TO APPRECIATE NICK CHUBB? Chubb follows the past greatness of exceptional running backs associated with the Browns such as Jim Brown, Kevin Mack , Marion Motley, Greg Pruitt , Leroy Kelly, Ernie Green, Earnest Byner, Dub Jones, and Bobby Mitchell. View this post on Instagram Chubb was a second-round selection in the 2018 NFL Draft and pick #35 out of Georgia. He started just nine games in his rookie season and then was the starting RB beginning in 2019. He has rushed for over 1,000 yards in four seasons, including the 1,525 he gained in 2022. Chubb has been named to the Pro Bowl four times and voted Second Team All-Pro in 2022. He suffered two gruesome knee injuries in his career, one with Georgia in 2015 and the other against the Pittsburgh Steelers in the early stages of the 2013 season. He had a broken foot in the Week 15 game against the Kansas City Chiefs in 2024. Chubb spent seven seasons with Cleveland before playing with Houston last year. His career totals are 100 games played with 87 starts, 1,462 attempts for 7,349 rushing yards, 340 first-down conversions, 54 rushing touchdowns, plus 141 receptions for 1,109 receiving yards and five additional scores. Impressively, Chubb was productive with his carries in a way that is unique among NFL running backs all time: Nick Chubb retires as just the fourth running back in NFL history with more than 1,000 carries and an average of more than 5 yards per carry. https://t.co/x2EpQjl9mP — ProFootballTalk (@ProFootballTalk) August 22, 2026 The Texans failed to re-sign Chubb to another one-year deal, and he became an unrestricted free agent. There was loose talk about a Cleveland return for 2026, but that never happened either. While with Cleveland, the home stands were littered with #95 (Myles Garrett) and #24 (Chubb) jerseys worn by Browns fans. Still are, still will be.

title: KC Concepcion has been killing it for the Browns, and there’s no sign of him stopping
summary: The Cleveland Browns appear poised to have their second strong draft class. After last week’s first preseason game, we asked fans which Browns rookie was the most impressive in the game. The three candidates we nominated were WR KC Concepcion, LT Spencer Fano, and CB Michael Coats. Even though all three players had strong performances […]
full_text: BEREA, OHIO - AUGUST 03: KC Concepcion #1 and Denzel Boston #12 of the Cleveland Browns walk off the field after the Cleveland Browns Training Camp at CrossCountry Mortgage Campus on August 03, 2026 in Berea, Ohio. (Photo by Nick Cammett/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns appear poised to have their second strong draft class. After last week’s first preseason game, we asked fans which Browns rookie was the most impressive in the game. The three candidates we nominated were WR KC Concepcion , LT Spencer Fano , and CB Michael Coats . Even though all three players had strong performances worthy of taking the top honor, Concepcion blew the others out of the water with 72% of the vote. Fano had 16%, while Coats had 12%. When Cleveland first selected Concepcion back in April, some fans were skeptical, and then relieved when the team followed that up with the selection of WR Denzel Boston in the second round. Boston himself has also had a great camp, but Concepcion has been killing it for the Browns each practice, and there’s no sign of stopping him. From the eye test early on, he has the makings of a player who makes you go, “Wow — this guy could dominate the league.” After the Bills-Browns joint practice this past Thursday, head coach Todd Monken was pleased with the team’s performance. As a result, he said that he doesn’t anticipate the veteran players seeing action (although QB Deshaun Watson is supposed to play in the third quarter still). Monken didn’t guarantee that Concepcion and Boston will play, but re-iterated that their younger players will see action: “I don’t anticipate seeing our older ones with that. I do see some of our younger players. I anticipate our younger players playing Saturday.” That means there’s a good chance that the likes of Concepcion, Fano, and Coats will have a chance to impress for a second straight week. Or will another rookie stand out amongst the crowd? The Browns are still heavy underdogs to make the postseason, at 61/1 compared to the other teams, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

title: Cowboys have done something for first time since 2007
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are 2-0 in the preseason. Alert the masses. Before we go any further, we all agree that wins and losses in the preseason do not ultimately matter. full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - NOVEMBER 29: Tony Romo #9 of the Dallas Cowboys looks on during warm-ups before a game against the Green Bay Packers on November 29, 2007 at Texas Stadium in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Sporting News via Getty Images via Getty Images) | Sporting News via Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are 2-0 in the preseason. Alert the masses. Before we go any further, we all agree that wins and losses in the preseason do not ultimately matter. You would certainly rather win these exhibition contests than lose them, but at the end of the day that particular detail does not matter as much as the roster growth and development you ideally experience within them. That being said, it has had been almost 20 years since the Cowboys could say that they were 2-0 in a given preseason. As we discussed this past week the last season where this was the case was 2007. Many around here believe that 2007 was the best team that the Cowboys have fielded throughout the entirety of The Drought™ so perhaps this is an indication that 2026 will be as successful as that one was, ideally without the exact same finish. Obviously we are just having fun with all of this, but it is pretty wild that the Cowboys had gone so long without getting to 2-0 in the preseason, isn’t it? Consider that the Cowboys got to 1-0 in the preseason last week for the first time since 2017. This offseason, and now preseason have felt so much like the Cowboys doing things they haven’t done in a long time, and that trend is certainly continuing.

It looked like they were going to score yet another touchdown, but things fizzled out and they had to settle for a casual Brandon Aubrey field goal from 50. SCORE: COWBOYS 24, CARDINALS 6 The Cardinals got in position for their kicker, Chad Ryland, to attempt a 62-yard field goal. It was about as far right as your opening tee shot when everyone from the clubhouse can still see you. The Cowboys were able to head to the locker room with all the reason in the world to feel great about themselves. Third Quarter As noted the Cardinals had been coming close on their last few possessions. It seemed as if some halftime talk and discussion helped them figure things out and they were finally able to get things across the goal line, figuratively and literally speaking. Corey Kiner was the man who punched it in for the first Arizona touchdown of the night and first touchdown at large that the Cowboys defense had allowed in the preseason since their first possession in Seattle. SCORE: COWBOYS 24, CARDINALS 13 The Cowboys went down the field at a much slower rhythm than earlier in the game. Maybe this was because of how late it was, joking obviously, but also the team had a big lead due to what happened in the first half. They were clearly aware of that and running the ball much more. The efforts finished shy of the endzone, but Brandon Aubrey was able to nail another three. SCORE: COWBOYS 27, CARDINALS 13 The quarter ended with Arizona holding the ball. Fourth Quarter Arizona wound up punting the ball back to the Cowboys early in the quarter, and Brian Schottenheimer let Sam Howell throw it a bit more this time around. Unfortunately he may have let Sam throw it a bit too much. After the Cowboys got within striking distance Howell threw a pretty inexcusable interception to turn the ball over. This happening after Milton set the game on fire certainly made the QB2 conversation pretty obvious. Thankfully the Cardinals were not able to do anything with the ball and stalled out at their own 38-yard line. Dallas took over on downs with five and a half minutes to go, and everything seemed pretty formal at that point. Formalities can change, though. Right when it seemed liked the Cowboys were going to just run things out… Phil Mafah had other plans! to the ➡️, to the ⬅️, to the endzone #DALvsAZ | @PhilMafah1 📺: #DALvsAZ on CBS11 📲: Stream on NFL+ https://t.co/7pAfvQ9tid pic.twitter.com/41A7X2M4GV — Dallas Cowboys (@dallascowboys) August 23, 2026 SCORE: COWBOYS 34, CARDINALS 13 The Cardinals basically ran the clock out and that was the ballgame! Cowboys win!
