title: Klint Kubiak calls out Raiders’ underperforming wide receivers
summary: When Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak was asked his opnions on his wide receiver room, he didn’t shy away from it. Klint’s keeping it real Kubiak addressed the question head-on and with candor, and for a man who doesn’t say much, that speaks volumes. He appears to be realizing he must find a […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TX - AUGUST 20: Wide receiver Malik Benson #19 of the Las Vegas Raiders leaps for a reception during the NFL preseason game between the Houston Texans and the Las Vegas Raiders on August 20, 2026, at Reliant Stadium in Houston, TX. (Photo by David Buono/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images When Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak was asked his opnions on his wide receiver room, he didn’t shy away from it. Klint’s keeping it real Kubiak addressed the question head-on and with candor, and for a man who doesn’t say much, that speaks volumes. He appears to be realizing he must find a guy who can distinguish themselves from the pack. As a whole, his entire receiving corps has taken a step backwards. Coach Kubiak responding to my question about the WR room and what he learned from the two days in Houston – “Learned a lot about the WR Room, they gotta get a lot better and fast, they took a step back, and are still looking for someone who is accountable and can help them on… — Your Boy Q (@YourboyQ254) August 21, 2026 Has Klint lost faith in his wide receivers? Not by a long shot, but he is a realist and the receivers need to get a whole lot better in the remaining three weeks before the season opener. Two weeks into the preseason, the team’s leading receivers, Shedrick Jackson and Brandon Johnson, are tied at 55 receiving yards, and UDFA EJ Williams has 47. Tre Tucker, Jalen Nailor and Jack Bech, all expected starters, have played about a series apiece with quarterbacks Kirk Cousins and Fernando Mendoza. If we are to take Kubiak at his word, none of them made an impact in the joint practice with the Texans before the preseason Week 2 game. Calling his guys out in the media usually goes one of two ways. Will coaches challenge be accepted Initially, hearing a coach call out his players for not achieving the standard is admirable and a desired quality. The first-year head coach is getting a crash course in just how good he had it with Jackson Smith-Njigba. Being able to scheme receivers open with an elite player who gets open on his own leads to triple crowns. Currently, every receiver on the Raiders depth chart has enjoyed success in a complementary role. Joint practice against the Texans defense left something to be desired. Keep in mind the ferocious pass rush of Will Anderson and Danielle Hunter cut down the time to get open to the break of the route. Technically, Kubiak didn’t single “anyone” out, say any names, or point any fingers. By all accounts, tight end Brock Bowers is Batman, Michael Mayer is the original Robin and the wide receivers are the rest of the Bat-family. The wide receivers have one job: run the correct route, get open and catch the football. Kubiak is not satisfied with having coasters in his offense.
author: Philip Robinson

title: Raiders’ penalties, tackling woes remain prime areas of opportunity
summary: While the Klint Kubiak era is indeed in its infancy, the Las Vegas Raiders are in mid-season form in one particular aspect: Penalties. After engaging in two of the three preseasons games, Kubiak’s desert marauders racked up 17 infractions to the tune of 158 yards. The Silver & Black’s most recent outing — a 22-20 […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 20: Woody Marks #4 of the Houston Texans rushes into the end zone for a touchdown during the first quarter of the game against the Las Vegas Raiders at NRG Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Kenneth Richmond/Getty Images) | Getty Images While the Klint Kubiak era is indeed in its infancy, the Las Vegas Raiders are in mid-season form in one particular aspect: Penalties. After engaging in two of the three preseasons games, Kubiak’s desert marauders racked up 17 infractions to the tune of 158 yards. The Silver & Black’s most recent outing — a 22-20 comeback win over the Houston Texans this past Thursday night — showcased nine penalties to the tune of 83 yards. And no part of the Raiders’ game was immune as early in the game, all three phases (offense, defense, and special teams) partook in mental lapses resulting in infractions. In Las Vegas’ first preseason tilt — against the Arizona Cardinals on Aug. 13 — the team committed eight penalties for 75 yards. And Kubiak is none to happy. A stickler for attention to detail, his football team’s habit of mental lapses isn’t ideal — even for a rookie head coach in his first season helming an NFL franchise. But Kubiak takes full onus of the situation noting that blame falls upon his shoulders in the immediate aftermath during the post-game press conference. And he expanded upon it during media availability Friday morning. #Raiders HC Klint Kubiak said he's "very concerned" about the number of penalties: "Two weeks in a row, and that's on me as a coach … That's on me to get that cleaned up. I said the same thing last week, so I'd better figure it out real quick." https://t.co/MyvlKcM2DG pic.twitter.com/PLPiIFUaqA — SleeperRaiders (@SleeperRaiders) August 21, 2026 “Holding guys accountable, working, drilling things that we didn’t do as well. For instance, a back block on Roman Hemby, educating guys better on the rules,” Kubiak explained when asked how does he intend to coach penalties out of his team. “We got D-Cam (cornerback Decamerion Richardson), made a costly error running out of bounds. I know that’s things that we coach them on every day, but we do have a lot of young guys that you can’t take anything for granted. So, we put it on ourselves as coaches number one, with how we educate them, what we’re practicing, what we’re drilling, and it’s on us, as coaches, to get it fixed.” Richardson’s gaffe, in particular, occurred on the Raiders’ second offensive drive (post Fernando Mendoza pick six), and negated a booming 64-yard punt by punter AJ Cole III which was downed deep in Texans’ territory inside the 10-yard line. Richardson ran out of bounds on the punt coverage and was the first to touch the ball resulting in Houston getting the ball on the 20-yard line. Eight plays and 48 yards later, the Texans drilled a 51-yard field goal to take a 17-0 lead in the opening quarter. “I don’t know if I’ve seen that many special teams penalties in a game, and you look at the guys that are committing these penalties, and these are some younger guys, and it’s not acceptable,” Kubiak said. “So, we have to get it fixed defensively. We get a stop on third down, we taunt a guy and let them stay on the field. Unacceptable. One was a face mask defensively. It’s two weeks in a row that, as a coaching staff, we’ve got substitution penalties. Unacceptable.” The taunting penalty arrived when promising 2026 draft fourth-round pick Jermod McCoy was flagged for doing a dual thumbs down as he stood above a Texan after an incompletion . We’ve heard plenty of previous Raiders coaching staffs lament on eliminating or reducing penalties and that job is on them as coaches. So it’ll be intriguing to see if Kubiak and his crew can course correct going forward. Woody Marks recorded a 23.0% forced missed tackle rate last season, the highest for a starting Texans running back under DeMeco Ryans LVvsHOU on ESPN Stream on #NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/A9ARriGZ7D — NFL+ (@NFLPlus) August 21, 2026 Tackle The Job Yes, the Raiders rested a vast swath of defensive starters against the Texans — cornerback Darien Porter was one of a handful of potential starters active and on the field in second preseason clash — but even accounting for that and the vanilla play calls used in exhibition tilts, tackling issues remain for the Silver & Black. As you can see from the post above from NFL Plus, Houston running back Woody Marks is already a tough tackle and the Raiders defenders had a rough time wrapping him up proper on the opening drive. Marks 20-yard touchdown on the Texans first possession was a prime example of Raiders getting to him — like safety Tristin McCollum and Porter — but Houston was not to be denied. Marks ended up carrying both Raiders safety Treydan Stukes and linebacker Tommy Eichenberg into the end zone with him. Las Vegas’ tackling ability did improve as Houston began to substitute in more second-, third-string players and the roster hopefuls. And it wasn’t all a lost cause as both McCollum and Stukes showcased strong tackling ability in the open field when presented opportunities. Stukes, in particular, used his instincts, speed, and explosion to diagnose and react to a play for a tackle behind the line of scrimmage. An encouraging sign of progress for the 2026 second-round pick who was slow to garner first-team defensive snaps in training camp practices. McCollum and 2026 fifth-round pick Dalton Johnson paced Las Vegas with seven total tackles each, while defensive end Patrick Johnson and defensive tackle Thomas Booker led the team with two stops for loss. A major portion of the comeback victory was takeaways by the Raiders defense as two strip sacks resulted in a pair of takeaways. “As a team, being plus one in the turnover margin, that’s how you win games. So, with (defensive coordinator) Rob (Leonard) taking it away, with our offense protecting the ball, that’s how you win,” Kubiak said. “You’ve obviously got to score, but you’ve got to you got to win the turnover battle. That was a huge part of the game.” Good job by Stukes rotating down, redirecting on PAP, playing the crosser to the flat, and finishing for a TFL pic.twitter.com/5BTM4SYlWO — Ted Nguyen (@FB_FilmAnalysis) August 21, 2026 Extra Points What an ugly outing for undrafted free agent Kansei Matsuzawa against the Texans. Going 1-for-3 on point after attempts is not the impression you want to make on a Raiders coaching staff during a kicker “competition”. The first miss by Matsuzawa sailed wide right but the second one — after Las Vegas went ahead 22-20 in the waning moments of the game — was hideous. It was shanked so bad, I messaged our Matt Holder: “That second miss looked like I kicked it.” Matt’s response: “I think you’d be hard pressed to find a kicker who has had a worse preseason in NFL history.” Veteran kicker Matt Gay drilled a second-quarter 52-yard field goal to put the Raiders on the board in the second quarter (17-3). And unless he gets hurt or has a bout of shanks, too, Gay will likely be the choice for special teams coordinator Joe DeCamillis with Matsuzawa 0-for-1 on field goal attempts and 1-for-3 on extra points. Quote of Note “Well, resilience. The resilience sticks out because we shot ourselves in the foot. We had nine penalties, five on special teams. The first half was atrocious. We started slow on both sides of the ball, and in the NFL, it’s all about winning the game. And so, we gutted it out and found a way to win, and that’s how this whole season’s going to be. All these games come down to the wire, and you get to learn a lot about players in practice, but you learn a whole lot more, and when the live bullets are flying in a game, and I learned a lot about guys in a good way last night.” —Las Vegas Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak on what stood out watching the second preseason game film

title: Raiders Mailbag: With several young, promising defensive backs, who gets left off 53-man roster on cutdown day?
summary: We’re about ready to put a bow on the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 training camp and preseason, which means the regular season is right around the corner! Get excited, but we also have one more preseason game and the NFL’s cutdown day coming next week. So, this week’s mailbag will have a heavy emphasis on […]
full_text: LAS VEGAS, NEVADA - DECEMBER 7: Decamerion Richardson #25 of the Las Vegas Raiders warms up prior to an NFL football game against the Denver Broncos at Allegiant Stadium on December 07, 2025 in Las Vegas, Nevada. (Photo by Brooke Sutton/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re about ready to put a bow on the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 training camp and preseason , which means the regular season is right around the corner! Get excited, but we also have one more preseason game and the NFL’s cutdown day coming next week. So, this week’s mailbag will have a heavy emphasis on the roster and guys who are on the bubble. Let’s get to it! Q: For cut-down day, Greedy Vance has practiced and played well. Hezekiah Masses and Decamerion Richardson have been about the same. Jermod McCoy is in recovery but not as good as those two yet. Which corners and safeties are among the 53? A: This is a tough one, and cornerback was one of the hardest decisions to make on my latest 53-man roster prediction , which was written and published before Thursday night’s game against the Texans. I had Vance, Masses and McCoy making the team while Richardson gets cut. But that was mainly because we hadn’t seen Richardson play in a while, and he had a good outing in Houston, giving up just one catch for three yards on two targets, per Pro Football Focus . This is a good problem to have, but the Raiders have a handful of young, talented corners where one of them likely isn’t going to be on the 53-man roster. I think the ideal situation is that Richardson continues to play well in the final preseason game and enough to catch another team’s eye, so John Spytek can flip him for a draft pick, another defensive tackle or wide receiver. Granted, a player-for-player swap doesn’t help get the roster down to 53 guys, but there’s plenty of fat to trim at those two positions. Then, it’s a matter of whether the coaching staff wants to keep five or six corners. It feels like Vance is the sixth, and as much as I’d like to see him make the team, the defense already has a handful of nickel options. Taron Johnson is the starter, Treydan Stukes can play there too, and Jeremy Chinn is the big nickel. Plus, Masses has gotten some run at covering the slot, and it wouldn’t be surprising to see McCoy get a shot there at some point, too. It comes down to whether the organization thinks Vance can clear waivers and is willing to re-sign on the practice squad or not. Other teams are watching the preseason too, so they could claim him if they need a nickel, and he might want to try his luck somewhere else if it’s not working out in Vegas. Maybe Vance could get put on the trade block too, but it’s hard to sell a former undrafted free agent who spent the majority of last season on the practice squad and isn’t going to make the 53-man this year. My last thought on this is admittedly a little bit out there. But if the Raiders don’t think McCoy will play very much this season anyway, then they could use his knee as an excuse to stash him on injured reserve for a “redshirt year”. I don’t like that option because it guarantees the fourth-round pick won’t see the field after missing all of last year, and I’d like to see him play at some point this fall. However, it is something the club could do to keep all of its young corners Q: If DJ Glaze continues to get beat on the edge, do you think Klint Kubiak would move Charles Grant to RT? Why waste him as a backup? Or is Trey Zuhn III really looking like the solution at RT? I just don’t think Glaze is the answer unless they camp out a tight end next to him. Do you? A: Glaze was in street clothes for the Texans game, so that’s a pretty good sign he’s going to be the starting right tackle to begin the season. I thought Grant would have a chance to compete for the job, but that never happened. I’m not sure why, but he’s stuck at left tackle throughout the summer. Maybe Grant wasn’t comfortable on the right edge, and he only played on the blind side in college. Some guys can make that switch seamlessly; others can’t get the footwork down after doing it in the opposite direction for so long. At this point, it seems like the 2025 third-rounder is the succession plan for Kolton Miller, or at least one of the options to be Miller’s long-term replacement, because Zuhn has been getting the reps at right tackle with the second-team offense. I’m skeptical of Glaze at tackle, but I have no choice but to give him the benefit of the doubt heading into the campaign. Clearly, Rick Dennison thinks he can get the job done or is the best option, and Dennison has forgotten more about offensive line play than I know. Hopefully, good coaching is all Glaze needs. Q: I thought Jordan Meredith looked terrible at center, per usual, against the Texans. Do you think Kubiak might try Trey Zuhn III there to be a backup? A: I definitely agree that Meredith had a bad game against the Cardinals, but I thought he played alright this week. For what it’s worth, PFF gave him a decent 67.3 grade overall and didn’t have him on the hook for any pressures on 22 snaps in pass protection. That being said, I recently mentioned that I don’t think Meredith will get traded to maintain some depth on the interior offensive line. However, that was before his rough outing against the Cardinals, and our Marcus Johnson recently got a scoop that Meredith is on the trade block. So, my read on that situation was clearly off, and keep your eyes peeled for a potential deal next week. If Meredith isn’t on the roster, then yes, Zuhn will likely be the backup center. He played there a bit at Texas A&M last year and has reportedly gotten some run at center (and just about every offensive line position, for that matter) during training camp. Quick break for an announcement from my friends at Homage . They’ve restocked their Raiders’ Starter pullover and satin jackets . Pictures are in the slider below and follow this link for the pullover and this one for the satin jacket . Q: Do you think Malcolm Koonce could get cut? He just disappears. I don’t know if No. 50 plays the same position, but he looks like he has some juice and tackles. The same with Jahfari Harvey. A: Koonce isn’t getting cut because he’d be a $10.5 million dead cap hit with only $510k in savings, per Over The Cap . If anything, he’ll get traded because that would slice the dead cap hit in half. But I also wouldn’t base this decision off of two preseason games. Keep in mind that Koonce has only played 27 snaps while Harvey has 44 against lower competition, which is why the latter is standing out more at this stage. Segun Olubi (No. 50) definitely had a good game in Houston, but he’s an off-ball linebacker and doesn’t play the same position as Koonce. Q: Is the 3/4 D the problem stopping the run or just the weakness of our tackles? A: No, it’s not a scheme issue; the defensive tackles are just getting their butts kicked. I pounded the table so hard for Kayden McDonald in the draft because the Raiders have a collection of defensive tackles who are good athletes to generate some pressure but leave a lot to be desired when it comes to stopping the run. That being said, I thought Foley Fatukasi provided some encouragement against the run versus the Texans. Ultimately, just like with wide receiver, I think John Spytek and Co. are going to see if any of the young defensive tackles can step up this season. And if no one rises to the occasion, the position will be one of the biggest needs in the offseason. Granted, the defense could probably still use another interior lineman if only one guy steps up this year. Someone else asked a similar question and what my thoughts are about addressing defensive tackle and wide receiver during a rebuilding year. I’m on board with taking the lumps for this season and seeing if anyone rises to the occasion. If another young player at either position comes available on the waiver wire after cutdown day, then I’d be up for adding them and seeing if they…

summary: Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza completed eight of 15 passes for 86 yards, no touchdowns and an interception against the Houston Texans in his second preseason game. While plenty of people have their opinions on Mendoza’s performance, the only one that really matters is head coach Klint Kubiak’s. After taking some time to […]
full_text: HOUSTON, TEXAS - AUGUST 20: Fernando Mendoza #15 of the Las Vegas Raiders talks with head coach Klint Kubiak on the way to the locker room after a preseason game against the Houston Texans at Reliant Stadium on August 20, 2026 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Tim Warner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Las Vegas Raiders rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza completed eight of 15 passes for 86 yards, no touchdowns and an interception against the Houston Texans in his second preseason game. While plenty of people have their opinions on Mendoza’s performance, the only one that really matters is head coach Klint Kubiak’s. After taking some time to review the film, Kubiak was asked about his quarterback’s outing during a press conference on Friday. “I think if you sat in our quarterback meeting the night before the game, listened to him go through his progressions and reads and adjustments, I was very impressed with how prepared he has made himself,” the coach said. “That whole quarterback room, led by [quarterbacks] Coach [Mike] Sullivan and [offensive coordinator] Andrew [Janocko], have done an excellent job of being prepared. “I was pleased with watching the tape. I really like what he did on third down. We were only one of five on third down in the first half. However, we did drop the ball twice, and we threw one short of the sticks on third and long. He had really good ball placement on the first third down of the game with a guy in his face. So, in the critical downs, I thought he was playing his best. There are things that we must get corrected that will be addressed ASAP.” Kubiak didn’t get into details about what “must get corrected”, but Mendoza’s pick-six is likely at the forefront of those conversations. The coach also mentioned that the quarterback’s cadence was the reason for the false start penalty on the second play of the game, which he “was not happy with”. Next week is the final week of training camp and the last chance for the No. 1 pick to beat out Kirk Cousins for the starting quarterback job ahead of the Week 1 matchup versus the Miami Dolphins, as the Raiders gear up for their final preseason game against the San Francisco 49ers on Thursday evening. In Other Raiders Links: Raiders-Texans winners and losers: “A lot was made about [Treydan] Stukes getting off to a slow start in training camp, and he was pretty quiet in the Raiders’ first preseason game, too,” via S&BP . “However, the second-round pick had a much-needed strong performance against the Texans.” Underrated Raiders: “Last season, Nailor caught just 29 passes on 49 targets for 444 yards and four touchdowns,” SB Nation’s Doug Farrar wrote, “but the ratio of big plays to catches should be a precursor to future possibilities — especially since J.J. McCarthy made every receiver on the roster (including and especially Justin Jefferson) struggle to match their usual productivity.” Coach calls out wide receivers: “I learned a lot, that we have to get a lot better very fast,” Kubiak replied when asked about his wide receivers, via Michael David Smith of Pro Football Talk . “We took a step backwards. That doesn’t mean we can’t go forward, but right now we are trying to find someone that is accountable and can help us on Sunday. Still looking.” Allegiant Stadium potential facelift: “The Las Vegas Stadium Authority is meeting on Thursday to vote on the Raiders’ request for $75 million to help fund a $158 million project that would create a new ‘front door’ to the stadium’s north entrance, according to a release,” via Bleacher Report’s Adam Wells . title: Giants vs. Dolphins: Final score, immediate reactions and trends
summary: The Miami Dolphins faced the New York Giants on Saturday afternoon as part of the second week of the 2026 NFL Preseason. Miami elected to sit most of the starters for the game, using the contest as a chance to see the depth players as roster decisions start being made. The players put a lot […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FLORIDA - AUGUST 22: Kevin Coleman #83 of the Miami Dolphins makes a catch ahead of Tyler Nubin #27 of the New York Giants during the first half of a pre season game at Hard Rock Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Miami Dolphins faced the New York Giants on Saturday afternoon as part of the second week of the 2026 NFL Preseason. Miami elected to sit most of the starters for the game, using the contest as a chance to see the depth players as roster decisions start being made. The players put a lot on film during the game, but few performances stood out for the right reasons. Today’s game was another instance of Miami looking outmatched and headed for a miserable regular season. Final Score Giants 26 – 3 Dolphins The Dolphins were never in this game. New York scored a touchdown on their first drive and they could have shut it down from there. Miami averaged just 2.8 yards per play on offense, gave up 4.9 yards per play on defense, and the special teams did nothing to help. It was another ugly performance from Miami who now have six days to figure out things before their preseason finale on Friday. Immediate Reactions Trending down: Injuries starting to pile up The injury bug hit Miami hard in the first half. During the first quarter, rookie linebacker Trey Moore left the game with a left leg injury. He was assisted off the field and was not putting any weight on his leg, relying on trainers to support him as he walked off the field. He was then taken to the locker room on a cart. Unfortunately, it did not stop there. In the second quarter, running back Ollie Gordon was tackled and remained down on the field. It appeared he was favoring his arm, but there was no clear indication of what the issue might have been. He was able to leave the field on his own, but he walked straight back to the locker room. The Dolphins are already hurting for depth, even before injuries start to take their toll. It seems like that toll is coming early this season. Trending up: Jackson Woodard continues upward trajectory An undrafted free agent last year who bounced between three teams and made four special teams appearances as a rookie, Jackson Woodard came into the summer as a camp body who was likely vying for a practice squad role. That may still be where he lands, but he is not going there without a fight. Last week he finished with a game-high seven tackles, and he came back this week firing around the field. Against the Giants, Woodard came to play. He recorded four tackles and recovered a fumble. He also made an impression on special teams, tallying two tackles in punt coverage (one officially negated by a holding penalty). Trending down: Depth offensive line struggles Maybe this does not need the qualifier of “offensive line” for this reaction, given the depth struggles all over the roster, but that is where we will focus. The line was bad today. They could not open running lanes. They could not protect quarterback Cam Miller in the first half, nor quarterback Mark Gronowski in the second half. The Dolphins did not reach 100 yards of offense until 8:46 remaining in the game. The best plays of the day came on quarterback scrambles as they ran for their lives away from pressure. Rookie guard Kadyn Proctor was the only starting lineman to play in the game, and he only played three snaps. The depth linemen were responsible for the day, and they did not step up. Interestingly, late in the fourth quarter, guard Josh Priebe was working as the center. Andrew Meyer, the primary backup center, has struggled while rookie Jim Bonifas may need time to develop. Could Priebe serve as the backup to starter Aaron Brewer and free up a roster spot somewhere else? Trending up: Rookie wide receivers This one is probably reaching for a positive, but the rookie wide receivers have made an impression two weeks in a row. After Caleb Douglas made a spectacular catch against the Commanders last week, Kevin Coleman, Jr., made sure he was noticed on Saturday. Coleman stood out during the joint practice on Thursday with the Giants, then backed it up with a leaping catch in traffic for a 30-yard gain during the game. He finished with two receptions for 32 yards – the only Dolphins player with multiple catches. Miami will face growing pains with multiple rookies on the field this season, especially at wide receiver, with three drafted players expected to contribute, but the flashes are showing in the preseason. Trending down: Special teams The special teams were trending down – and then wide receiver Tahj Washington lost a muffed punt just before the end of the game. The special teams are not good right now. Nothing seems to be working in sync, whether it is kick coverage, punt coverage, field goal attempts, kick returns, or punt returns. The entire special teams unit needs to be a focal point between now and the start of the regular season. Bonus trending down: Tutu Atwell continues to struggle I wanted to limit this to five immediate reactions, but Atwell needs to be brought up today. There should be no pathway for Atwell to make the roster. It is harsh, but he is not playing well enough to justify a roster spot when the Dolphins could let a rookie gain experience and likely get the same production. The former second-round pick of the Los Angeles Rams in 2021 has fallen off. He finished the game with no receptions on two targets, a rush for one yard, and one kick return for 27 yards. That should not be the production Miami is trying to keep on their roster this season.

full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - JUNE 03: Miami Dolphins linebacker Trey Moore (17) participates in drills during Miami Dolphins Minicamp on Wednesday, June 3, 2026 at Baptist Health Sports Center in Miami Gardens, FL (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Miami Dolphins rookie linebacker Trey Moore sustained a left leg injury in the first quarter of the team’s Preseason Week 2 game against the New York Giants. During New York’s first possession, Moore pressured quarterback Jameis Winston, jumping to try to block the pass at the last second. He landed awkwardly after the leap, immediately grabbing at his left leg as the crumpled to the turf. Trainers came out to look at Miami’s 2026 fourth-round pick, examining his lower left leg. They eventually assisted him off the field, but Moore was clearly still in pain and could not put any weight on the leg. Selected 130th overall, Moore spent two years at the University of Texas after starting his college career with a three-year stint at the University of Texas – San Antonio. He played in 57 games over five seasons, recording 104 tackles, a fumble, five forced fumbles, five fumble recoveries, and 30.5 sacks. This is a developing story and will be updated as more information becomes available.

Where are the biggest areas of concern for Dolphins fans when it comes to the team’s preparations for the season? Earlier this week, we asked you that question in our SB Nation Reacts survey. Nearly half of the responses zero in on one major area of concern: the secondary. Miami’s cornerbacks and safeties are battling for position and roster spots, but there are not a lot of players standing out as the best of the pack. Depth concerns, as well as inexperience, dominate both position groups and, if Miami’s edge rushers cannot get immediate pressure on opposing quarterbacks, the secondary may not be up to their coverage responsibilities. The backup quarterback position, where Quinn Ewers struggled last week against the Washington Commanders and is now injured, was second in the results, receiving 32 percent of the vote. Injuries already starting to hit the team was third with 15 percent, while punting received four percent of the vote. Miami heads into the game as a 3.5-point underdog , according to the FanDuel Sportsbook oddmakers, despite being at home. title: Dolphins preseason 2026: Predicting the 53-man roster ahead of Giants game in Preseason Week 2
summary: The Miami Dolphins hit the field on Saturday for the second time in 2026, playing their Preseason Week 2 contest against the New York Giants. The two teams met in a feisty joint practice on Thursday, one that featured multiple skirmishes, Dolphins right tackle Austin Jackson being removed from a large portion of practice, and […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - AUGUST 20: Miami Dolphins linebacker Jacob Rodriguez (10) and linebacker Chop Robinson (44) speak during a New York Giants and Miami Dolphins joint practice at the Miami Dolphins Training Camp on August 20 2026, at the Baptist Health Training Complex in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Doug Murray/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins hit the field on Saturday for the second time in 2026, playing their Preseason Week 2 contest against the New York Giants. The two teams met in a feisty joint practice on Thursday, one that featured multiple skirmishes, Dolphins right tackle Austin Jackson being removed from a large portion of practice, and the Giants manhandling Miami for much of the time. Before they meet in a game scenario, it is time to take a look at the Dolphins’ preseason roster and predict the regular season roster. Under NFL rules, teams can carry up to 90 players during training camp and the preseason (or 91 in Miami’s case due to a roster exemption for International Pathways Player tight end Seymour Traore), but have to drop to 53 players when the league’s roster limit changes on August 30. Here is the prediction of the Dolphins 53-man roster during Preseason Week 1: Miami Dolphins offense (22) Quarterback (2) Malik Willis Quinn Ewers Cut: Cam Miller, Mark Gronowski Willis is entrenched at the top of the depth chart. Ewers has not clinched the second position and is now injured, but no one behind him has really pushed him for the backup job. Miller could be a practice squad option. Gronowski is likely a camp arm who is released whenever Ewers returns from his injury. Running backs (3) De’Von Achane Jaylen Wright Ollie Gordon II Cut: Donovan Edwards, Carlos Washington, Jr. The running back group feels like the most secure position group on the roster. Miami’s offense will be built around Achane this year, with Wright serving as his primary backup. Gordon is more of a power back than the other two and will be given the short-yardage duty along with rotational play to keep Achane as fresh as possible throughout the year. Edwards could find himself on the practice squad. Washington has work to do if he wants to make it to the roster. Fullbacks (1) DJ Herman Cut: None Herman is not a lock to make the roster, but I think he has the potential to stick around. If he moves over to the practice squad, with tight end Ben Sims (listed as a fullback on the team’s unofficial depth chart) taking the primary fullback role, it would not be a surprise. Tight ends (3) Greg Dulcich Will Kacmarek Ben Sims Cut: Seydou Traore, Cole Turner, Jeremiah Franklin Herman making the roster as the fullback eats up a tight end spot, because Sims should make the roster as well. The bubble player here is Traore, who has the draft capital of a fifth-round pick, but he has had a quiet training camp and first preseason game. He could be a practice squad player, with Miami gaining the International Player Pathway roster exemption. If he makes an impression on Saturday, he could fight his way onto the roster, but he would cost Miami no roster or practice squad slots if he were to land on the practice squad. Offensive lineman (10) Tackles Patrick Paul Austin Jackson Caedan Wallace Charlie Heck Guards Kadyn Proctor Jonah Savaiinaea DJ Campbell Josh Priebe Centers Aaron Brewer Andrew Meyer Cut: Gottlieb Ayedze, Jim Bonifas, , Kevin Cline, Marques Cox, James Ester Paul, Proctor, Brewer, Savaiinaea, and Jackson should be the starting offensive line, left to right. Jamaree Salyer was likely in line to be the top swing tackle and would provide guard depth as well, but he landed on injured reserve this week. Meyer, as the backup center, is a concern; he struggled last week in the Commanders game. Bonifas could make the roster in Meyer’s place, or may be on the practice squad as a developmental lineman. Preibe and Heck need to step up if they want to ensure their roster spot; Miami could look to waiver claims to round out the bottom end of the depth chart. Wide receivers (6) Malik Washington Caleb Douglas Chris Bell Kevin Coleman, Jr. Jalen Tolbert Jalen Reagor Cut: Tutu Atwell, AJ Henning, Donaven McCulley, Terrace Marshall, Theo Wease, Jr., Tahj Washington The wide receiver group is a clash of roster locks (Malik Washington, Douglas, Bell) and a bunch of question marks (Tolbert, Reagor, Atwell, Marshall, Wease, Tahj Washington). Several players on the cut line are developmental players I would love to keep, but there is not enough roster room to keep everyone and hope they reach their potential. Reagor’s return ability has him jumping over players like Atwell and Tahj Washington. I am not convinced Tolbert is a roster lock, especially with Bell now off the non-football injury list; could Miami head into the season with three rookies and Malik Washington as their primary receiving corps? Join the conversation! Sign up for a user account and get: Fewer ads Create community posts Comment on articles, community posts Rec comments, community posts New, improved notifications system! Miami Dolphins defense (26) Defensive ends (5) Chop Robinson Josh Uche Robert Beal, Jr. David Ojabo Max Llewellyn Cut: Seth Coleman-Lyles, Clelin Ferrell, Cameron Goode, Rodney McGraw Ferrell on the cut line is not where I thought I would have him, but the numbers forced me into a cut I did not want to make. The locks are probably Robinson, Uche, and Beal. Ojabo’s stock is probably falling, and it could be a matter of Ferrell or Ojabo on the final roster. If the Dolphins think they can stash Llewellyn, a seventh-round pick this year, on the practice squad, that would free up a roster spot as well. I want to find a way to keep Goode, but right now, I do not have it. Today’s game could shake up this position group a lot. Defensive tackle (5) Zach Sieler Kenneth Grant Jordan Phillips Zeek Biggers Fatorma Mulbah Cut: Matthew Butler, Keith Cooper, Jr., Alex Huntley, Cam Rice I think the Dolphins could look to roll deep along the defensive line, and they have the players to do that at defensive tackle. Sieler is the top option, but he is getting to the point in his career where the coaching staff needs to rotate him out to keep him fresh to make an impact when it is most needed. Grant, Phillips, and Biggers are all 2025 draft picks and are showing up now. The bubble watch for the position comes down to Butler or Mulbah. Mulbah was impressive against the Commanders, so he moves onto the roster projection this week. Linebackers (6) Jordyn Brooks Jacob Rodriguez Trey Moore Tyrel Dodson Kyle Louis Ronnie Harrison, Jr. Cut: Stephen Dix, Jr., Willie Gay, Jr., Cam Riley, Jackson Woodard Harrison and Gay are in a position battle to claim the final spot among the linebackers. I will give the nod to Harrison right now, because it feels like he has had a better overall performance this summer, but Gay was all over the field last week against the Commanders and another performance like that today could flip those two spots. Moore will moonlight as an edge rusher and Louis will play in a big nickel/hybrid safety role as well. Dodson is in an odd position of seeming like both a starter and someone who might not be on the roster when the season starts, albeit as a potential trade candidate. Cornerbacks (6) Chris Johnson JuJu Brents Jason Marshall, Jr. Ethan Bonner A.J. Green III Marco Wilson Physically Unable to Perform list: Darrell Baker, Jr., Storm Duck Cuts: Alex Austin, Miles Battle, Ahmari Harvey, Nick McCloud (Released pre-game on Saturday) Johnson, Brents, and Marshall seem like they are locked into the top three positions on the depth chart. After those three, you could spin a wheel to pick the remaining cornerbacks. title: Vikings Post Ravens 53-Man Roster Projection
summary: Now that the Minnesota Vikings have completed joint practices and their preseason game with the Baltimore Ravens, rather than do a stock market report, with the bulk of the opportunities for players to impress their virtues on the coaching staff have come and gone, and with only one preseason game and a few more practices […]
full_text: EAGAN, MN. - JULY 2026: Vikings GM Nolan Teasley left, and head coach Kevin O'Connell speaks to members of the Media at TCO Performance Center in Eagan, Minn., on Tuesday, July 28, 2026. (Photo by Jerry Holt/The Minnesota Star Tribune via Getty Images) Now that the Minnesota Vikings have completed joint practices and their preseason game with the Baltimore Ravens, rather than do a stock market report, with the bulk of the opportunities for players to impress their virtues on the coaching staff have come and gone, and with only one preseason game and a few more practices remaining before roster cuts must be made, I thought I’d simply do another 53-man roster projection. There are still some tough calls, but here is my best effort at projecting who the Vikings will include on their initial 53-man roster later this month. Quarterback (3) The Vikings have kept three quarterbacks on the roster for emergency purposes on games days given the rule that a third quarterback can be added to the active list. QB1: Kyler Murray QB2: Carson Wentz QB3: J.J. McCarthy Practice Squad (PS): Max Brosmer Wentz has shown more consistency and ability to run the offense effectively than McCarthy in preseason action. I suspect KOC trusts Wentz more as well. I expect the Vikings will be listening to any trade offers for McCarthy and I won’t be surprised to see him traded. He hasn’t shown any improvement in training camp or preseason and the Vikings hope/patience with his development may be at an end. Running Back/Full Back (4) The Vikings kept three running backs and a fullback last year and I expect the same again this year. RB1: Aaron Jones RB1a: Jordan Mason RB2: Demond Claiborne FB1: Max Bredeson PS: Zavier Scott Notes: Jordan Mason may be the RB1 at some point this season, whether or not Jones is healthy. I have him as RB1a right now, but I wouldn’t be surprised if he ends up with more snaps this year than Jones. I could see Claiborne earning up to a couple hundred snaps as well over the course of the season as he becomes the replacement for Jones next year. Claiborne has shown he can do a decent job as a pass protector so far, which helps his chances to see the field. Max Bredeson is a lock at fullback and looks to be an upgrade over C.J. Ham. Zavier Scott is worthwhile keeping on the practice squad and could be called up in the event of injury. Wide Receiver (5) The Vikings kept five wide receivers on the roster last year and expect the same again this year. WR1: Justin Jefferson WR2: Jordan Addison WR3: Jauan Jennings WR4: Tai Felton WR5: Myles Price PS: Dillon Bell, Jeshaun Jones and/or Dontae Fleming Notes: These roster spots are pretty much locked up either contractually or based on training camp/preseason action. Both Felton and Price have stepped up and there hasn’t been much from the rest. Dillon Bell and Jeshaun Jones or possibly Dontae Fleming are good practice squad candidates. Tight End (3) The Vikings kept three tight ends on the roster last year and I expect the same again this year. TE1: T.J. Hockenson TE2: Josh Oliver TE3: Gavin Bartholomew PS: Ben Yurosek Hockenson and Oliver are locks and I think with Max Bredeson able to function as a blocking tight-end/H-back, Bartholomew’s receiving ability may be more attractive than Yurosek’s blocking ability. That would give the offense two receiving and two blocking tight ends. Offensive Line (10) Keeping ten offensive linemen is likely to be the new normal for the Vikings as they’ve dealt with injuries across the offensive line the past few seasons. LT1: Christian Darrisaw LT2: Ryan Van Demark LG1: Donovan Jackson LG2: Joe Huber C1: Blake Brandel C2: Michael Jurgens RG1: Will Fries RG2: Walter Rouse RT1: Brian O’Neill RT2: Caleb Tiernan PS: Henry Byrd, Tomas Rimac, Gavin Gerhardt, Triston Leigh, Delby Lemieux Caleb Tiernan did not play well in his first preseason game and I wouldn’t be surprised if he starts on the PUP list given his ankle injury and limited value at this point, in which case Henry Byrd may make the roster initially. Joe Huber has been okay in training camp and preseason, rather than great, but he has a track record that helps him keep a roster spot. Walter Rouse has looked good at guard- he’s played both guard spots well- in two preseason games and I think that, along with his ability to play tackle in a pinch, will allow him to keep a roster spot as well. There doesn’t appear to be any serious challenge to Michael Jurgens at backup center. Henry Byrd is on the bubble and offers more value right now than Tiernan, but on the other hand hasn’t been as solid as Rouse. Defensive Interior Line (6) The Vikings kept six defensive tackles last year and I expect the same this year. Jalen Redmond Levi Drake-Rodriquez Tyrion Ingram-Dawkins Caleb Banks Domonique Orange Elijah Williams PS: Isaiahh Loudermilk, Taki Taimani, Jahvaree Ritzie The first five spots are locks and Elijah Williams has been the best of the rest and I’m not sure it’s been that close. The Vikings will need Williams to handle rotational reps as Banks and Orange ramp up this season. Outside Linebacker (4) The Vikings kept five outside linebackers last year and that could be the case this year, but it may come down to whether they want a fifth OLB or ILB, but there is a lot of overlap with Eric Wilson and Jake Golday taking snaps off the edge and Chaz Chambliss taking snaps at inside linebacker against the Ravens. I’m guessing they’ll go with a fifth ILB. One of Bo Richter, Chaz Chambliss, or Tyler Batty I have being cut and hopefully placed on the practice squad. I’m picking Bo Richter to lose his roster spot, but it’s very close. Andrew Van Ginkel Dallas Turner Tyler Batty Chaz Chambliss PS: Bo Richter Inside Linebacker (5) The Vikings kept five inside linebackers on their initial roster last year and that may be the same this year as well. Blake Cashman Eric Wilson Jake Golday Ivan Pace Jr. Jacob Roberts Notes: Cashman, Wilson, and Golday are roster locks. It was looking like Ivan Pace may be the odd man out but after special teams coordinator Matt Daniels talked about Pace as being a leader this year on special teams, that indicated his roster spot may be safe. His violent play style can be a tone setter, however, even if he’s usually good for a play per game where he’s caught out of position that proves costly. He might not be needed as much defensively as the season goes on and Jake Golday ramps up, however. Wilson and Golday, potentially, could take snaps off the edge this season which is why I have five inside linebackers and four edge rushers. Jacob Roberts had a great yet under-the-radar preseason so far. In 53 snaps, he’s had 8 tackles and an assist, including six for stops. In 21 coverage snaps he was targeted four times, with an interception and 3 receptions allowed for 30 yards and a touchdown. He’s also played 20 snaps on special teams and has a tackle but one penalty. Overall, he is the fifth-highest PFF graded linebacker in preseason so far. He’s been instinctive and frequently around the ball as a run defender. He was also a good core special teamer in the CFL last year. Cornerback (4) The Vikings kept four cornerbacks last season and I expect the same this season. Byron Murphy Jr. Isaiah Rodgers James Pierre Charles Demmings PS: Dwight McGlothern, Zemaiah Vaughn Murphy, Rodgers, and Pierre are roster locks and Demmings has clearly outperformed the rest in training camp and preseason so far. Zemaiah Vaughn has done well throughout training camp and preseason overall and has overtaken McGlothern at this point. But that’s not enough for a roster spot over Demmings. Safety (6) The Vikings kept five safeties last season but how this group has developed and is able to contribute warrants keeping six this year. Josh Metellus Theo Jackson Jay Ward Jacob Thomas Tavierre Thomas Jakobe Thomas Notes: Jakobe Thomas has really played or participated much in training camp or preseason, apparently due to lower back tightness…

title: Baltimore Ravens 13, Minnesota Vikings 3: A Game Definitely Was Played
summary: On Saturday afternoon at U.S. Bank Stadium, the Minnesota Vikings’ defense, even the second-string, looked like it was in midseason form. Given what the offense looked like for most of the day, they’d better hope that carries over to the regular season. The Minnesota offense, which played three different quarterbacks on the afternoon, managed just […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - AUGUST 22: Tai Felton #13 of the Minnesota Vikings catches a pass over Silas Walters #36 of the Baltimore Ravens in the first quarter of a preseason game at U.S. Bank Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by David Berding/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Saturday afternoon at U.S. Bank Stadium, the Minnesota Vikings’ defense, even the second-string, looked like it was in midseason form. Given what the offense looked like for most of the day, they’d better hope that carries over to the regular season. The Minnesota offense, which played three different quarterbacks on the afternoon, managed just three points and turned the ball over twice in a 13-3 loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Minneapolis in Week 2 of the 2026 preseason. The Vikings got the football first, with J.J. McCarthy leading the offense onto the field. McCarthy completed three of his four pass attempts on the drive, but the drive ended in a punt for the Minnesota offense. The Ravens’ offense, led by Tyler Huntley, then went three-and-out, with a fair catch interference penalty on Baltimore giving the Vikings the ball in solid field position. On the second play of the drive, McCarthy eluded the rush and launched one deep to Tai Felton along the right sideline for 50 yards to set up a first-and-goal. J.J. McCarthy goes DEEP to Tai Felton! Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cvO0UUGoCb — NFL (@NFL) August 22, 2026 The Vikings eventually worked the ball to a fourth-and-goal from the 1-yard line, and McCarthy’s pass for Myles Price was too high and fell incomplete to leave the game scoreless midway through the first quarter. Another three-and-out from the Baltimore offense gave the Vikings the ball with good field position again, this time near midfield. After a sack and a holding penalty that negated a first down, the Vikings punted it away, and Baltimore responded with a third consecutive three-and-out. A nice return from Trayvon Rudolph gave the Vikings the ball near midfield again, but the Vikings couldn’t move the ball, and another punt ensued to start the second quarter. Baltimore’s offense then finally found some rhythm as they moved the ball inside the Minnesota 40-yard line. The drive stalled out, and Tyler Loop connected on a 49-yard field goal attempt to give the visiting team a 3-0 lead with around nine and a half minutes remaining before halftime. Carson Wentz took over at quarterback for Minnesota on the following series, and the Vikings pushed into Baltimore territory, but a third-down blitz from the Ravens resulted in a sack, and the Vikings punted it away once again. The Ravens then made a quarterback change of their own, with Joe Fagnano replacing Tyler Huntley at quarterback. His first drive resulted in yet another three-and-out, and they punted it away just after the two-minute warning to give Wentz and the Vikings another opportunity. Wentz then hit a long pass of his own, finding Jeshaun Jones for a 35-yard pass to get the Vikings into Baltimore territory with just under 40 seconds left in the half. Carson Wentz throws it up to Jeshaun Jones who hauls in the tough 36-yard reception 👀 Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/GdocS8a5jq — NFL (@NFL) August 22, 2026 A screen pass to tight end Gavin Bartholomew then moved the Vikings to the Baltimore 29-yard line. A couple of plays later, Wentz was sacked again, and the Vikings burned their last timeout of the half before calling on Will Reichard for a 52-yard field goal attempt. He drilled it, and we went into the locker room at halftime tied at 3-3. The Ravens got the ball to start the second half and immediately. . .you guessed it. . .went three-and-out. Max Brosmer then took over at quarterback for the Vikings. His first drive led to another punt for the Vikings in what was not exactly a riveting offensive display. Baltimore’s next drive pushed into Minnesota territory, aided in part by a personal foul penalty on Bangally Kamara that negated a third-down stop. Fagnano then pushed the Ravens into the Minnesota red zone on a pass to Devontez Walker, and they eventually got into the end zone courtesy of an 8-yard pass from Fagnano to LaJohntay Wester to make it 10-3 with just under six minutes remaining in the third quarter. Minnesota’s next drive got off to a solid start, as Brosmer completed consecutive passes to Jeshaun Jones and Dillon Bell to pick up a first down, and a completion to Dontae Fleming moved the Vikings into Baltimore territory. Ultimately, the Vikings found themselves with a 4th-and-3 from the Baltimore 44-yard line and elected to go for it. Brosmer’s pass fell incomplete, and the Vikings turned it over on downs. To start the fourth quarter, the Vikings were driving again, and Brosmer completed a pass to Jones to convert a first down. Jones then fumbled the ball, with former Detroit Lion Amani Oruwariye recovering for the Ravens at the Minnesota 43 to end the drive. The Ravens took advantage of the turnover, as they added to their lead on a 20-yard field goal from Loop to make it 13-3 with just under nine minutes left in regulation. The Vikings took over and cobbled together one of their longer drives of the day, pushing the ball down to the Baltimore 24-yard line. However, Brosmer’s pass intended for Terrill Davis was intercepted by Silas Walters inside the 20-yard line to end the drive and, effectively, end any chances at a Minnesota victory in the second preseason game. Jesse Minter’s squad ran out the clock from there, and they left town with a ten-point win. The Vikings will close out the preseason this coming Friday night, as they’ll head to the Mile High City to take on long-time nemesis Sean Payton and the Denver Broncos. The Minnesota Vikings fall to the Baltimore Ravens in Week 2 of the 2026 preseason by a final score of 13-3 in a relatively unexciting contest. Thank you to everyone who got their coverage of this week’s game right here at The Daily Norseman!

title: Baltimore Ravens at Minnesota Vikings: Preseason Game 2 Discussion
summary: We are just about ready to kick off the second game of the 2026 preseason for our Minnesota Vikings, as they prepare to host the Baltimore Ravens in their lone home preparatory contest of the season. Let’s get you caught up on all the information you need to be ready for this one. Date and […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - AUGUST 15: Myles Price #4 of the Minnesota Vikings catches a third quarter touchdown against the New York Giants during a pre-season game at MetLife Stadium on August 15, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. Minnesota Vikings defeated the New York Giants 13-10. (Photo by Mike Stobe/Getty Images) | Getty Images We are just about ready to kick off the second game of the 2026 preseason for our Minnesota Vikings, as they prepare to host the Baltimore Ravens in their lone home preparatory contest of the season. Let’s get you caught up on all the information you need to be ready for this one. Date and Time : Saturday, 22 August 2026, noon Central time Location : U.S. Bank Stadium, Minneapolis, Minnesota Weather : There’s no weather. . .game’s inside. Television Coverage : FOX 9 in the Twin Cities, various local affiliates in several markets around the Midwest (and Alaska, apparently), NFL+ or ESPN Unlimited for out-of-market viewers Radio Coverage : Vikings Radio Network , SiriusXM Channel 227, SiriusXM App Channel 820 Bonus : KFAN (which, again, is doing a simulcast for both radio and TV this season) has promised that new Vikings’ general manager Nolan Teasley will be joining the broadcast for the entirety of the third quarter of today’s game. Should be interesting to hear from the new guy in charge. Line : Seriously, don’t bet on preseason games. Chris’ Prediction : Yeah, still not making predictions on preseason games. Three Keys 1) No injuries – Well, the Vikings couldn’t check this box last week. . .stupid MetLife Stadium turf. Here’s hoping that both teams can make it through today’s game without suffering any significant injuries. 2) Backup quarterback battle – Kyler Murray isn’t going to play today, so the Vikings are going to get a chance to sort out their backup quarterback situation. J.J. McCarthy will likely start, and he didn’t put up great numbers against the Giants last week. . .but he didn’t get a whole lot of help, either. Carson Wentz got some extended run thanks, in part, to the Max Brosmer injury, and he could potentially make a run at the #2 spot. We’ll be keeping an eye on how things shake out. 3) Special teams issues – Last week, much like we saw last season, it seemed like there was a flag on pretty much every special teams play, particularly on punt returns. The Vikings even managed to get a punt return on a fair catch, which was impressive in a sad way. Even though a lot of those were from players who are fighting for spots at the bottom of the roster, those are the sorts of things that need to be cleaned up. Hopefully we’ll see less of those sorts of things today. Know the Foe : Baltimore Beatdown Twitter/X/Whatever we’re calling it today : @DailyNorseman FaceBook : https://www.facebook.com/thedailynorseman That should be everything you need, folks! Remember, we’ll be keeping everything for today’s game right here. We’ll also be putting any highlights that get posted on social media over in the Feed, so keep your eyes over there as well. Here’s hoping for a good, solid afternoon of football that ends with nobody on either team getting hurt. SKOLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL VIKINGS!!!!

title: 10 things we learned from Patriots vs. Eagles preseason game
summary: The New England Patriots played their second preseason game of the summer on Saturday night at Gillette Stadium, and, once again, decided not to use their starters. Naturally, with the backups in the game, the roster competition was the main event against the Philadelphia Eagles. Let’s find out what we learned about them, and the general state […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Casey Rogers #65 of the New England Patriots celebrates after a fumble recovery with Karon Prunty #21 and Namdi Obiazor #48 during the fourth quarter of a preseason game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots played their second preseason game of the summer on Saturday night at Gillette Stadium, and, once again, decided not to use their starters. Naturally, with the backups in the game, the roster competition was the main event against the Philadelphia Eagles. Let’s find out what we learned about them, and the general state of the roster, during the Patriots’ 24-21 victory . Behren Morton does it all Rookie Behren Morton had a solid night at quarterback for the Patriots and led the team to two touchdown drives to turn a 14-10 halftime deficit into a 24-21 victory. The first of those drives started late in the third quarter, and the second one proved to be the game-winning rally late in the fourth. Morton himself was poised, and looked confident throwing the ball. If that had been his entire night, it would have been a really good one. Of course, it wasn’t, because he also had three punts with at average 44.3 yards per kick. Bryce Baringer apparently wasn’t feeling great after his second punt in the second period, so they sent Morton in to punt instead, something he hadn’t done since he was in high school (Baringer, meanwhile, remained as the team’s holder). It makes sense for the Patriots to only keep two quarterbacks with the roster looking the way it does, but I could see a world where they decide to keep Morton as their emergency QB3. He looked decent last week, and looked solid this week, even though he didn’t get a single joint practice rep against the Colts or Eagles. I therefore still think it’s a long shot for him to be on the roster on cut down day. A tough receiver decision awaits Mike Vrabel has made it pretty clear that Kyle Williams is going to be a big part of their plans this year. He showed why late in the first half, when he caught a 69-yard touchdown pass from Tommy DeVito. Simply put, if you run man press on him without safety help over the top, he’s a good candidate to take any pass to the house. Having a guy with his releases who possesses natural speed and ball tracking abilities is invaluable to an offense. Sure, he only does one thing, but he does it very well and there’s now enough talent on the roster that he can do that one thing because of the guys ahead of him. Efton Chism, meanwhile, was a demon underneath and caught all four of his targets for 45 yards. He looked slippery with the ball in his hands, and that’s the exact type of thing that Patriots fans hope he can bring to the roster. He might not be a Pro Bowl-caliber player, but he’s proven himself to be a legitimate NFL talent. The Patriots are going to have to make tough decisions on roster cutdown day with the receiver position. I’m starting to think that they end up keeping all seven of their wide receiver and maybe only keep two tight ends, knowing that C.J. Dippre or Tanner Arkin are likely to clear waivers and end up on the practice squad as potential elevation candidates on game day. Nick DeGennaro bursts onto the scene Speaking of looking slippery with the ball in his hands, Nick DeGennaro, the rookie from James Madison, had a great night on Saturday. He caught four passes for 61 yards, and had a 37-yard touchdown to win the game, when he got behind former Patriot Isaiah Bolden for the score. With the receiver room as packed as it is, I can’t imagine he makes the active roster, but he might have secured himself a spot on the practice squad with his performance on Saturday. His ability to work out of the slot and also play on the outside was impressive, and that’s something the team might want to keep around. Cameron Dorner, who finished with two catches and also drew two flags when he beat his guy fairly decisively, also looks like a practice squad option with the way he’s performed all camp. No running room for the offense The Patriots had a tough time running the football on Saturday night. If you take away their longest runs of 20 and 10 yard, respectively, Jam Miller had 10 carries for 16 yards and Lan Larison had eight for 23. I thought they both ran hard but there was nowhere to go most of the night. The offensive line consisted exclusively of backups, yes, but the Eagles didn’t have any starters out there either, so you’d like to think you could have some level of success. That was not the case, unfortunately. RB3 battle is heating up Running back is one of the most intriguing positions on the roster right now because there are four guys vying for what appears to be a single roster spot, and all of them have looked good at times. On Saturday night, Lan Larison looked the best of the bunch. He ran hard between the tackles, including on a 4th-and-1 where he was hit in the backfield but kept the legs churning to bounce off a would-be tackler and move forward for the conversion. Larison looked good catching the ball out of the backfield as well, with his best plays a 28-yard screen pass in the first quarter that saw him dance down the sideline and a really nice pickup on 3rd-and-6 where he had to fight for the last few yards. Jam Miller ran hard as well, even though there wasn’t much available to him. He’s not super explosive, but he has good vision, and gets what is given to him. He’s similar to Terrell Jennings, who looked like the frontrunner for the RB3 spot before he was placed on injured reserve and subsequently released off of it. Hassan Haskins didn’t receive nearly the amount of snaps that the first two got, while JaMichael Hasty looked good catching the ball and pass-protecting, but a fumble in the second half might prevent him from making the roster. Hasty has been on and off the team the last few years, so even if he doesn’t make the 53-man roster or even the practice squad, the Patriots have shown a willingness to bring him back before to help in a pinch. Overall, it feels like Larison might have taken a small lead on Saturday night. We will see how it plays out, but his willingness and ability to run between the tackles and contribute in the passing game could have him on the inside track right now. James Hudson had a bad night Tackle-turned guard James Hudson did not have his best day at the office on Saturday. The veteran offseason signing had multiple holding penalties, and was beat on multiple occasions both in the run and the pass game. The Patriots brought in Greg Van Roten, who seems to be in a good position to make the roster , but the depth on the inside still isn’t great. Hudson might have flexibility to play both tackle and guard, but he doesn’t do either particularly well, so you have to assume that he is not going to make the roster. Chad Muma is not the answer at linebacker The Patriots have been in need of quality linebacker depth for multiple years, which prompted them to bring in a good amount of veteran players to try to address the issue. Chad Muma was one of those players; he arrived in New England as a practice squad pickup from the Colts last December. While he offers an intriguing athletic skillset and vast special teams experience, he hasn’t looked impressive in training camp so far. On Saturday, meanwhile, he had a forgettable night and found himself out-positioned on multiple plays. He then left the game in the late fourth quarter with an injury. Not great. Kindle Vildor makes a bid for a roster spot The Patriots need cornerback depth, and it appears that Kindle Vildor and Karon Prunty are right in the mix for the backup spots. Prunty had a consistent game against the Eagles; He wasn’t flashy, but did a decent job in coverage and in the run game. Vildor, on the other hand, had one of the best drives you will see a corner have. The offseason signing beat the receiver to…

title: 8 winners and losers from Patriots’ preseason win over the Eagles
summary: The New England Patriots continued their preseason Saturday night at Gillette Stadium with a 24-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles. Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Patriots’ preseason opener. Winners QB Behren Morton: Things looked much more comfortable for New England’s rookie quarterback in preseason game No. 2. […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Behren Morton #15 of the New England Patriots looks to pass during the fourth quarter against the Philadelphia Eagles of a preseason game at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images The New England Patriots continued their preseason Saturday night at Gillette Stadium with a 24-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles . Here is who caught our eye for better or worse upon live-viewing the Patriots’ preseason opener. Winners QB Behren Morton: Things looked much more comfortable for New England’s rookie quarterback in preseason game No. 2. Morton completed 13-of-17 passes for 129 yards and a touchdown as he led the offense down the field to score the game winning 37-yard touchdown by finding Nick DeGennaro down the right sideline. With punter Bryce Baringer also not feeling great after his first two punts, Morton, a former high school punter, handled those duties. WRs Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams: New England’s second-year wide receiver duo showed their potential as they played throughout the first half. As usual, Chism remained a reliable target underneath and over the middle of the field hauling in all four of his targets for 45 yards — including a 24-yard completion on third-down on a Josh McDaniels staple. Williams’ night was more volatile as he caught just 2-of-6 targets and potentially could have fought harder over the middle of the field. But the speedster made his mark, as he beat Ambry Thomas off the line of scrimmage on a go ball to haul in a 69-yard touchdown. TOMMY DEVITO TO KYLE WILLIAMS FOR 69 YARDS PHIvsNE on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/QvyMDDZYlC — NFL (@NFL) August 23, 2026 DBs Kindle Vildor and John Saunders Jr.: The Patriots continue to look for cornerback depth behind Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis. With Charles Woods sitting with the regulars, Kindle Vildor made his mark Saturday night. The veteran had an interception called back due to a roughing the passer penalty but rebounded by forcing an incompletion then driving downfield to break up a third-down pass. As for Saunders, the safety continued his strong summer. Saunders was on scene to shut down several of Philadelphia’s play-action bootleg concepts and recorded a pass breakup in coverage on second-round rookie tight end Eli Stowers. Saunders play style fits nicely into this defense and the 24-year old is seriously pushing for a roster spot. RB Lan Larison: As the battle for a third running behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson continues, Lan Larison made sure to keep his name in the mix with a strong performance. Larison totaled 33 yards on nine carries while finding the end zone and also added 41 yards on three catches. “I felt like Lan certainly had a good performance, a gritty, tough performance tonight, and did some really good things,” Vrabel said. Losers OG James Hudson III: The Patriots backup offensive line continued to struggle Saturday night. That was led by another tough performance by James Hudson, who recently moved inside to guard, as he allowed a sack and additional pressure while generating two holding penalties on the opening drive. LB Chad Muma: After a rough preseason opener, Muma’s struggles continued on Saturday as the linebacker missed a pair of tackles in the first half. Muma, who suffered an injury last week, later spent time in the blue medical tent before going on to play the whole second half until needing to leave the field again due to injury in the final minute. Linebacker depth is a concern right now as the Patriots also lost Khalil Jacobs Saturday night. Honorable mentions Tommy DeVito had some accuracy issues again but delivered a beautiful touchdown ball to Kyle Williams and made several plays with his legs. UDFA Nick DeGennaro hauled in the game-winning touchdown in the final minute. Making the roster at wide receiver is a no-win situation, but DeGennaro looks primed for a practice squad spot. JaMycal Hasty lost a fumble. Preseason game No. 2 seemed to draw better results for Caleb Lomu in live action. Lomu played 57 snaps at left tackle and gave up one sack failing to pickup a stunt. He seemed to struggle at times in the run game, but the athletic ability is seen in 1-on-1 pass pro situations. Gabe Jacas registered a QB hit as an unblocked rusher off the edge on a zero blitz. He did get flagged for a roughing the passer penalty on a similar play that negated a potential interception. Strong rush and strip sack to ice the game by rookie pass rusher Q Hutchins. Namdi Obiazor recorded an impressive pass breakup on fourth-down in the end zone playing the hands of an Eagles’ pass catcher. Andy Borregales rebounded after a poor preseason debut by making all four of his kicks (one field goal, 41 yards, three extra points). Borregales’ bounce-back came with Julian Ashby back at long snapper. Ashby, who missed last week with an injury, also logged two tackles on kick coverage.
