title: Patriots react to Ja’Quinden Jackson injury in Eagles preseason game
summary: The New England Patriots’ preseason game against the Philadelphia Eagles started in the worst possible fashion. On the game’s opening kickoff that was run back by New England’s Lan Larison, Eagles running back Ja’Quinden Jackson remained on the ground after a collision. It was clear immediately that his injury was significant, prompting a quick reaction […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MA - AUGUST 22: vhc checks on an injured Ja'Quinden Jackson #45 of the Philadelphia Eagles during a preseason game between the New England Patriots and the Philadelphia Eagles on August 22, 2026, at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Fred Kfoury III/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The New England Patriots’ preseason game against the Philadelphia Eagles started in the worst possible fashion. On the game’s opening kickoff that was run back by New England’s Lan Larison, Eagles running back Ja’Quinden Jackson remained on the ground after a collision. It was clear immediately that his injury was significant, prompting a quick reaction from the medical staff. Jackson eventually was put on a stretcher and left the field in an ambulance. His team later shared that he has “strength and movement in all extremities” and was being taken to a hospital for further evaluation. His agent, Damien Butler, released a statement afterwards that his client was “awake, has full movement and use of all four limbs, and his CT scan came back negative.” The scene nonetheless was a scary one. Afterwards, the Patriots expressed their well-wishes for the 24-year-old. “I would just like to send our thoughts and prayers out for Ja’Quinden Jackson,” said New England head coach Mike Vrabel during his postgame presser . “You never like to see that. Obviously, I hope everything’s okay there. That’s not how you want to start any game or see anybody out there on the field like that.” “Our thoughts and prayers are with Ja’Quinden and his family,” added quarterback Tommy DeVito. “Not something you would like to see on the field. Obviously, it’s a physical game. Definitely not the way you want the game to start out. I hear he’s doing a better, though.So, thoughts and prayers with him and his family.” A second-year running back who started his career as an undrafted rookie with the Jaguars, Jackson joined the Eagles earlier this month. He played 19 snaps between offense and special teams in Philadelphia’s preseason opener, catching an 11-yard pass. Further Patriots to comment on the injury include Kyle Williams, Behren Morton, Nick DeGennaro and Efton Chism. They appeared on the podium after Vrabel and DeVito, and also opened their pressers by making sure to shout out Jackson. “Just want to give my thoughts and prayers out to Mr. Jackson and his family, and everything they’re going through,” Chism said. “That’s a very tough situation. I hope everything is going well for them and that they’re in good spirts.” Jackson’s injury brought back memories of former New England cornerback Isaiah Bolden remaining on the ground in a preseason game against the Packers in 2023. Back then, with 10:29 remaining in the fourth quarter, the contest was suspended. No such thing happened on Saturday, with the game resuming a handful of minutes after Jackson’s departure. The home team Patriots ended up winning with a final score of 24-21 .
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Instant analysis from Patriots’ 24-21 preseason win over Eagles
summary: After two joint practices, there were more reps to be taken under the Gillette Stadium lights. The New England Patriots turned those reps into a 24-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Saturday night in Foxborough. Here’s a glance back on the 7 p.m. ET kickoff before sights set on the preseason finale and the […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 22: Tommy DeVito #16 of the New England Patriots hands the ball of to Lan Larison #34 during the first quarter of a preseason game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Gillette Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) | Getty Images After two joint practices, there were more reps to be taken under the Gillette Stadium lights. The New England Patriots turned those reps into a 24-21 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Saturday night in Foxborough. Here’s a glance back on the 7 p.m. ET kickoff before sights set on the preseason finale and the NFL’s 53-man roster deadline. DeVito, Williams connect for second preseason TD After starting the preseason opener, Tommy DeVito handled a similar workload on Saturday night. New England’s No. 2 quarterback went 8-of-15 passing for 151 yards against Philadelphia. He again found one touchdown and no turnovers before calling it an outing. Six drives had been logged on the odometer by then. DeVito moved the chains on third-and-3 and first-and-10 scrambles. The waiver claim from the NFL’s 2025 cutdown deadline finished with 44 yards rushing as All-Pro captain Drake Maye looked on from the sideline, led by a 36-yard sprint. In “21” personnel with C.J. Dippre at tight end and Tanner Arkin at fullback, Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams served as the perimeter starters for the Patriots’ offense. The wide receivers from Eastern Washington and Washington State combined for six catches for 119 yards, including a 69-yard go route down the right sideline by the latter target for his second touchdown in as many weeks. The third snap of that drive gave the Patriots a 10-7 lead as Eagles cornerback Ambry Thomas chased the deep speed in coverage. It’d be Behren Morton’s turn under center for New England by the 10:23 mark in the third quarter. The Texas Tech alum, selected No. 234 overall in the 2026 NFL draft, doubled as a specialist during his second relief appearance. A 48-yard punt into the end zone for a touchback was followed by a 43-yard effort and then a 42-yard effort. The rookie QB went on to complete 13-of-17 passes for 129 yards a touchdown of his own. A third-and-8 shot to the end zone down 21-17 got lost in the lights. But a 38-yarder to undrafted wideout Nick DeGennaro did not, capping off an 11-play, 73-yard drive with a touchdown and a 24-21 victory. Reshuffled O-line takes another hit Attrition struck the interior of the offensive line during what became a 13-13 tie with the Indianapolis Colts last week. In the absence of proven backup Ben Brown as well as Andrew Rupcich, who recently reached an injury settlement , there was a new arrangement on deck. Saturday night’s starting five included rookie Caleb Lomu at left tackle. The No. 28 overall pick out of Utah let up a sack late in the first half and was flanked by Mehki Butler at left guard, Jacob Rizy at center and James Hudson III, who was flagged for two holding penalties on the initial drive, at right guard. And at right tackle, Marcus Bryant exited five offensive snaps in after getting his left ankle rolled up. The sophomore bookend was quickly ruled out and replaced by rookie sixth-rounder Dametrious Crownover from Texas A&M en route to a false start. The Eagles hit home for four sacks by game’s end. RB3 race tightens as Larison finds end zone Behind the tandem of Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson, the Patriots remain in search of a third running back. Versus the Eagles, that search went forward with Lan Larison in the starting spot. The redshirt from UC Davis took the game’s opening kickoff and proceeded to handle nine carries for 33 yards, three catches for 41 yards, plus a touchdown in the final quarter. A long of 28 as well as second efforts to convert on fourth-and-1 and third-and-6 were there, too. Rookie Jam Miller spelled into the backfield to the tune of 36 rushing yards across a team-high 11 handoffs. The No. 245 overall pick out of Alabama broke free for a long of 20 after pacing the position in the preseason opener. New England’s depth chart was rounded out by veteran August additions . Hassan Haskins rushed for 16 yards, while JaMycal Hasty lost a fumble on his way out of bounds in the fourth quarter and finished with 21 yards from scrimmage. Two sacks off the edges New England’s edge depth has been under the microscope. That held true on Saturday evening. Gabe Jacas was flagged for roughing the passer, but the No. 55 overall pick from Illinois tacked on three tackles to go with a quarterback hit. March signing Jesse Luketa got the start across from the rookie outside linebacker. And rotating in for the Patriots’ first sack of the night was a disciplined, gaming Amari Gainer to end the first half. Back-to-back turnovers on downs and a punt were how things got out of intermission for the defense. Yet with 3:39 to play, an unaccounted-for swing pass to Carson Steele in the right flat saw the visitors retake the lead after fellow Eagles running back Will Shipley previously got on the board. Then the final selection in New England’s 2026 draft got on the board, too. Boston College product Quintayvious Hutchins strip-sacked quarterback Cole Payton and defensive tackle Casey Rogers was there to recover the fumble as time expired. Looking for off-ball depth Khalil Jacobs got the call off the ball for the Patriots on Saturday. The undrafted free agent by way of South Alabama and Missouri logged a pair of tackles between defense and special teams, including a stop in the open field on third-and-10 to send the punt unit on. Veteran Chad Muma, who was beaten on a bootleg and missed a tackle before the first quarter concluded, also drew the start at inside linebacker. But two chunk plays on screen passes helped the Eagles retake the lead at 14-10 shortly before intermission. With tackling hard to rely on early, Eagles QB Tanner McKee hit receiver Britain Covey for a 14-yard touchdown as rookie linebacker Riley Wilson slipped by his intended target in traffic. The results would be different next time Philadelphia stepped into the red zone, however. A fourth-and-3 pass was met by close coverage from sixth-rounder Namdi Obiazor via TCU to halt the possession. Vildor, Saunders continue to have a hand On the heels of intercepting two passes last week, New England’s secondary remained active. The Patriots’ starting cornerbacks included Karon Prunty, Marcellas Dial Jr. and a previous pick collector in Kindle Vildor. The journeyman among them nearly got his second of the preseason and soon deflected two more on the same series to force a punt. A strong case continued on Saturday. The starting nickel package also featureed Dell Pettus and another August ballhawk in John Saunders Jr., who broke up a pass in the second quarter and added a strong stop in space in the third quarter. A penalty for unnecessary roughness arrived in between against third safety Mike Brown. Back through the uprights In the summer opener, Andy Borregales missed three attempts wide left. But the lone kicker on New England’s roster kept things through the uprights in his follow-up. The reigning PFWA All-Rookie selection did so by converting on his lone field goal and going 3-of-3 on extra points against Philadelphia. As part of the operation, the Patriots had fellow 2025 draft choice Julian Ashby back at long snapper on Saturday night after the waiving of backup Niko Lalos. And from there came a 41-yarder in the second quarter with punter Bryce Baringer holding.

title: Mike Vrabel makes concerning statement about Patriots’ depth after Eagles game
summary: The New England Patriots celebrated their first win of this year’s preseason on Saturday night, beating the Philadelphia Eagles with a final score of 24-21. And yet, Mike Vrabel was not particularly enthusiastic when appearing at the podium after the game. One are in particular he seems to be concerned about is his team’s depth. […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel looks on in the first half against the Philadelphia Eagles at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Edward Finan-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New England Patriots celebrated their first win of this year’s preseason on Saturday night, beating the Philadelphia Eagles with a final score of 24-21 . And yet, Mike Vrabel was not particularly enthusiastic when appearing at the podium after the game. One are in particular he seems to be concerned about is his team’s depth. He didn’t sugar-coat his feelings either. “I don’t think we have a very deep team,” Vrabel said when asked about personnel usage in the upcoming preseason finale versus the Brown. “We have to make sure that we’re preparing our football team and that we’re doing everything that we can that we keep our best players available. If that means playing Thursday as part of preparation, then that’s what we’ll do. I have not made that decision yet, but I would say that that’s something that I’m confident in with where we’re set up currently.” The Patriots’ starters around quarterback Drake Maye have been held out of preseason action in the two games so far, playing no snaps against either the Colts last week or the Eagles on Saturday. In place of game action, the top-level group did get plenty of reps in three combined joint practices against those teams. With no such sessions coming up next week, the plans might ultimately change. Vrabel’s statements after the Philadelphia game, however, indicate that Maye and company should again be expected to see minimal action, if that. There are, after all, various areas that have been tested from a depth perspective. Most prominent among those is the offensive line, which lost another top backup on Saturday when offensive tackle Marcus Bryant injured his ankle on the opening drive . While the severity of Bryant’s injury is not yet known, he joins a growing list of banged-up O-lineman that also includes top interior option Ben Brown and since-released Andrew Rupcich. The Patriots are scheduled to return to the practice fields on Monday and Tuesday before a final preseason contest in Cleveland on Thursday night.
author: Bernd Buchmasser

title: Patriots vs. Eagles final score, stats, game recap from NFL preseason
summary: The New England Patriots continued their preseason on Saturday night, defeating the Philadelphia Eagles 24-21 at Gillette Stadium following two joint practices on Wednesday and Thursday. As Drake Maye and the rest of the starters rested, New England turned to backup Tommy DeVito to lead the offense. DeVito’s offense trailed at halftime as Philadelphia drove […]
full_text: Aug 22, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots wide receiver Nick DeGennaro (23) in the first half against the Philadelphia Eagles at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Edward Finan-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New England Patriots continued their preseason on Saturday night, defeating the Philadelphia Eagles 24-21 at Gillette Stadium following two joint practices on Wednesday and Thursday. As Drake Maye and the rest of the starters rested, New England turned to backup Tommy DeVito to lead the offense. DeVito’s offense trailed at halftime as Philadelphia drove 62 yards downfield in under two minutes to reclaim a 14-10 lead. Both teams traded touchdowns in the fourth quarter, but it was Behren Morton’s deep touchdown pass to wide receiver Nick DeGennaro that swapped the outcome and sealed New England’s victory. Final score: Patriots 24 : 21 Eagles Saturday, Aug. 22, 7 p.m. ET | Gillette Stadium, Foxboro, MA | Broadcast information | Game day roster First Quarter The Patriots started at their own 20-yard line after a holding call on James Hudson III on first down. A Lan Larison screen with an open field ahead advanced New England 28 yards near midfield. However, on the following third down, Tommy DeVito’s late throw toward the right sideline was placed too far out of bounds for Kyle Williams to reach. A Bryce Baringer punt then placed the Eagles at their own 22. Running back Will Shipley broke loose for an 18-yard gain, but Philadelphia’s drive shortly ended following two Andy Dalton incompletions. Braden Mann’s 39-yard punt sets the Patriots up at their own 16 halfway through the first quarter. On New England’s following drive, a DeVito seven-yard scramble and a pair of short completions to Efton Chism III and Kyle Williams sparked two new sets of downs for the offense. That said, Eagles linebacker Jeremiah Trotter Jr. had other plans, breaking into the backfield and sacking the Patriots’ quarterback. Bryce Baringer pinned Philadelphia at its own two with a 61-yard punt, but Britain Covey returned the kick 21 yards to give the opposing offense room to operate. Two extended completions to wide receiver Darius Cooper totaling 38 yards helped the Eagles break into Patriots territory, and a string of efficient Shipley runs has their offense with a new set of downs at the home team’s five-yard line. Second Quarter Opening a new frame of play, Shipley finishes the job, breaking into the end zone on a rush up the middle to put Philadelphia ahead before a successful Jake Elliott extra-point attempt. [Patriots 0 : Eagles 7] New England, beginning its next drive at its own 18, broke into Eagles territory with DeVito scrambling 36 yards to Philadelphia’s 37. That said, two incompletions and a four-yard JaMycal Hasty carry feel short of the first-down markers. Kicker Andy Borregales delivered a 41-yard field goal to put the Patriots on the board. [Patriots 3 : Eagles 7] Then, the Patriots’ defense made a stand, forcing the Eagles’ offense to a three-and-out. Second-round rookie Gabe Jacas quickly pressured Dalton off the edge on second down, and two Kindle Vildor pass breakups on first and third put the offense in a difficult spot. The cornerback nearly returned an interception to the end zone on the first play of the drive, but a Jacas roughing-the-passer call eliminated the turnover. DeVito’s offense, taking over at their own 23, passed midfield after the signal-caller connected with Chism over the middle and more for a 24-yard gain. That said, Philadelphia defensive tackle Ty Robinson blew by center Jacob Rizy to sack DeVito and force a punt. And unexpectedly, quarterback Behren Morton is called upon to deliver a kick that falls into the end zone for a touchback with just under seven minutes remaining in the opening half. Following a short-lived Eagles drive, second-year wide receiver Kyle Williams quickly won his matchup, releasing off the line of scrimmage and hauling in a 69-yard touchdown pass from DeVito to claim New England’s first lead of the night. [Patriots 10 : Eagles 7] Philadelphia, operating under a short clock with just three minutes remaining, found the end zone for a score. From the Patriots’ 14-yard line, Covey caught a short pass, navigating the middle of the field after the catch. A pair of Carson Steele dump-offs totaled 30 yards, with an unnecessary roughness call on Mike Brown adding to the bleeding. [Patriots 10 : Eagles 14] With just over one minute on the clock, New England had a chance to regain their lead, but another Robinson sack ended their drive prematurely. The Eagles fielded a punt shortly after, yet outside linebacker Amari Gainer closed the pocket and recorded a sack on quarterback Tanner McKee to close out the first half. Third Quarter A Borregales kickoff touchback placed Philadelphia at its own 35-yard line to begin the second half. The opposing offense marched all the way down to the Patriots’ 12-yard line but was stopped on third down. Deciding to go for a fourth-down try, McKee floated a pass to tight end E.J. Jenkins in the back left corner of the end zone. In coverage, rookie linebacker Namdi Obiazor broke up the pass to force a turnover on downs. Taking over on offense inside the 10, Behren Morton’s opening drive was short-lived after a split-sack on third down between Eagles outside linebackers Joshua Weru and Jose Ramirez. Morton converted an early third-down snap, finding a wide-open Hasty in the flat for a nine-yard gain, but couldn’t recover from a Tejhaun Palmer offensive pass interference call. Philadelphia soon took over at New England’s 49-yard line halfway through the third frame; however, the Patriots’ pass rush heavily disrupted the Eagles’ offense. On third-and-one, defensive tackle Eric Gregory wrapped up Steele behind the line of scrimmage before Leonard Taylor III forced a quick pressure and tipped McKee’s pass on fourth down. Morton, with another chance, led New England’s offense downfield during a steady drive. On third and long, the Texas Tech product converted, firing a pass to Palmer, who corralled the ball through physical coverage on a slant. Then, rookie running back Jam Miller slipped free for 20 yards after cutting back inside, rushing into the red zone as the clock ran out. Fourth Quarter At the start of the final quarter, Larison closed out the drive, punching the ball in at the goal line after a 10-yard rush. Borregales split the uprights on the extra-point attempt. [Patriots 17 : Eagles 14] That touchdown series extended the defense’s intense energy into the fourth as the unit forced a second consecutive three-and-out Philadelphia drive. The Patriots, beginning their next drive at their own 23-yard line with 12:25 remaining, were knocking on the door of Eagles territory, preparing to run the ball from their 49. Hasty, turning toward the left sideline, lost the ball as familiar face Shaun Wade knocked it loose. With favorable field positioning at midfield, Philadelphia marched downfield 52 yards in nine plays to reclaim its lead with 3:39 set on the clock. On a pivotal third down, McKee connected with Steele in the flat, who sprinted toward the front right pylon and leapt over safety Eric Butler to secure the touchdown. [Patriots 17 : Eagles 21] Under pressure from the clock, Morton threw two third-down conversions en route to a 37-yard DeGennaro score down the right sideline. Borregales then split the uprights on the extra point, capping off an 11-play, 73-yard game-winning drive. [Patriots 24 : Eagles 21] And as the Eagles lined up for one last drive, seventh-round Quintayvious Hutchins sealed the game with a strip-sack on Cole Payton.

title: Patriots lose another O-lineman to injury against Eagles in preseason
summary: After already suffering some losses in last week’s preseason opener, the New England Patriots offensive line took another hit against the Philadelphia Eagles on Saturday. On the game’s first drive, right tackle Marcus Bryant remained down following a short run play. Bryant walked off the field under his own power, but had to be supported […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 13: Marcus Bryant #52 of the New England Patriots lines up during an NFL preseason football game against the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images After already suffering some losses in last week’s preseason opener, the New England Patriots offensive line took another hit against the Philadelphia Eagles on Saturday. On the game’s first drive, right tackle Marcus Bryant remained down following a short run play. Bryant walked off the field under his own power, but had to be supported by members of the Patriots’ training staff. He went straight to the blue medical tent on the sidelines and shortly thereafter had to be helped to the locker room. The Patriots have since announced that he won’t return to the game because of an ankle injury. Bryant, 24, originally arrived in New England as the 220th overall selection in the seventh round of the NFL Draft. Serving as a backup at right tackle, he appeared in 12 games as a rookie. He saw offensive action in just three of them, however, and was a regular on the inactives list as a healthy scratch from December on. Despite his uneventful rookie season, Bryant played a prominent role along the Patriots’ O-line this summer. Together with first-round rookie Caleb Lomu, he served as one of the two primary backups at the tackle position behind starters Will Campbell and Morgan Moses. With him out, the team inserted rookie Dametrious Crownover into its lineup. Last week against the Colts, the Patriots saw their top two interior backups — Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich — leave with injuries. Brown is expected to miss multiple weeks , whereas Rupcich was placed on injured reserve and since waived with an injury settlement .

title: Fans most worried about this position ahead of the season
summary: The regular season is right around the corner as the New England Patriots will wrap up their preseason and cut the roster down to 53 players next week. As the wins and losses will soon count for real, it again highlights the strengths and weaknesses on the current Patriots roster. While the team made sure […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 13: Elijah Ponder #91 of the New England Patriots looks on following an NFL preseason football game against the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The regular season is right around the corner as the New England Patriots will wrap up their preseason and cut the roster down to 53 players next week. As the wins and losses will soon count for real, it again highlights the strengths and weaknesses on the current Patriots roster. While the team made sure to upgrade positions such as wide receiver with A.J. Brown and Romeo Doubs this offseason, the roster still has some areas of concerns. Even after signing Dre’Mont Jones in free agency and drafting Gabe Jacas in the second round, the edge spot continues to have questions. In the results of the latest SB Nation Reacts survey, 47% of participants said that spot is the biggest area of concern on the roster. The comment section largely agreed: PatsFanFromNH I have to go with the pass rush. We have solid RBs & CBs, we have a good starting O-Line, and I’m not as concerned with depth as I am with starting effectiveness & force, and we’re lacking the ability to get to the QB. Bajer i was edge concerned until the recent injuries to the injuries to the guards/c — van roten is a good emergency signing, but can a guy hold upiin there who is 36 and has taken a pounding for 14 years? VaEagle85 I’m going LB followed by Edge. I have some faith that a couple of the young guys will be pleasant surprises on the Edge, so maybe some okay depth there. Not feeling the same about LB. I remember being a little shocked when Chaisson signed with the Commanders and the amount he signed for, wondering why the Pats had not offered at least that much. Losing him was pretty big and seems like an unforced error frankly. Leoa888 Edge. Harold Landry isn’t doing anything right now. Say on top of Jones and Ponder, Hutchins, Swinson, and Jacas all turn out to be better long term than Landry. When it’s time to bring Landry back, we’re going to have to give up a good young player just to justify Harold “Culture Guy” Landry. Felkey At this very moment, I’ll stick with oline. We know AVT is basically a ticking time bomb (and Wilson and Campbell both got hurt last year – granted one time is not a pattern, could just be bad luck) so this depth is more important than at other positions imo. Assuming Ben Brown comes back early season and Roten gets up to speed quickly, I’d shift to edge which is a very close second for me. All in all, this week’s survey results look as follows: Following the edge, concerns continue about the offensive line depth after losing Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich to injuries in the preseason opener. The unit received 24% of the votes as the team then signed veteran Greg Van Roten to fill a role. Depth on defense then rounded out the voting as linebacker depth received 21% of the votes and cornerback depth received 5%. Behind Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss is Chad Muma, who struggled in the preseason opener, K.J. Britt and rookies Namdi Obiazor and Khalil Jacobs. The cornerback depth has then been highlighted this summer as both Christian Gonzalez and Carlton Davis have missed time. The Patriots are hoping they can overcome the weaknesses on the roster to get back to the Super Bowl. They currently have the eighth-highest odds on FanDuel Sportsbook to do so — which marks the sixth-highest odds in the AFC.

title: 8 Patriots to watch in preseason game vs. Eagles
summary: Following a pair of joint practices, the New England Patriots and Philadelphia Eagles will take things inside Gillette Stadium for preseason game No. 2. After Drake Maye and the Patriots top offense received 61 competitive full-team snaps over two days of practice with the Eagles, the starters are not expected to play Saturday night. As […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - AUGUST 13: Gabe Jacas #50 of the New England Patriots lines up during an NFL preseason football game against the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium on August 13, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following a pair of joint practices, the New England Patriots and Philadelphia Eagles will take things inside Gillette Stadium for preseason game No. 2. After Drake Maye and the Patriots top offense received 61 competitive full-team snaps over two days of practice with the Eagles, the starters are not expected to play Saturday night. As for who we will be watching closely with just eight days until roster cutdown day, here are eight players on our radar. Running back: Hassan Haskins Injuries in their backfield caused the Patriots to sign Haskins a day before last week’s preseason opener. Thrown right into the fire, Haskins had some impressive moments on the ground and continued that into last week at practice. The former Mike Vrabel draft pick in Tennessee has good size (6-2, 228 lbs.) for a third running back and has contributed early on on special teams. He currently looks like the favorite to earn a spot behind Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. Wide receiver: Kayshon Boutte Despite Drake Maye and New England’s regulars not suiting up in the preseason opener, Kayshon Boutte went on to play their first three drives (16). He finished without a target. As the 24-year old’s future in New England remains unclear, Boutte’s usage Saturday night will again be of note with Maye and Co. not expected to play. Tight end: Tanner Arkin After building momentum early in camp, Arkin has slowed down in recent weeks. That included some struggles in the preseason debut as the undrafted free agent was on scene for three runs stuffs as a blocker. With that being Arkin’s strength and path to the roster, that will need to be cleaned up against the Eagles. Offensive line: Caleb Lomu and the depth options Lomu played all 39 snaps at right tackle in his debut last week. While he allowed just two hurries, the first-round pick had his fair share of ups and downs, even as New England didn’t ask him to pass protect on many traditional drop backs. Lomu has continued to play both left and right tackle in practice of late, and will look to take a step forward in game action Saturday night. Next to Lomu, the Patriots have seen plenty of turnover after losing top interior backups Ben Brown and Andrew Rupcich to injuries last week. That, combined with struggles from depth guards James Hudson and Mehki Butler, led them to sign veteran Greg Van Roten this week. The group will look for a bounce-back performance against a deep and talented Eagles defensive line. Edge rusher: Gabe Jacas and Co. Second-round pick Gabe Jacas has progressed nicely as the summer has gone on. Jacas’ size and physicality immediately stand out on the field but the rookie has expected room to grow when it comes to his awareness and play recognition — an area he struggled with last week vs. the Colts. Fellow rookie Quintayvious Hutchins drew the start opposite of Jacas in the preseason opener but the speed rusher was relatively quiet with just one hurry. Hutchins will look to make more of an impact this week, while second-year pro Bradyn Swinson will also look to build off his strong preseason opener where he logged three pressure and a QB hit in the second-half. Linebacker: Namdi Obiazor The Patriots’ linebacker group saw some rotational changes after the first preseason game, as Chad Muma struggled and suffered an injury that left him limited this week. Veteran K.J. Britt, who impressed last Thursday night, saw time with the first-team defense in addition to rookie Namdi Obiazor. The sixth-round pick will get plenty of run Saturday night on defense and special teams, where he remains on the top punt protection unit, as he looks to make his case for even more snaps moving forward. Cornerback: Charles Woods and Kindle Vildor With Christian Gonzalez sidelined, Charles Woods has remained the top cornerback opposite of Carlton Davis. But, Woods has struggled this past week returning from an injury of his own which led the team to turn to veteran Kindle Vildor at the end of Thursday’s joint practice. While Vildor logged an interception on Wednesday, he allowed two catches on Thursday — including a touchdown — during the Eagles end-of-game red zone drive. New England will hope one of the veterans will bounce back to end the summer and confidently fill the CB4 spot. Kicker: Andy Borregales After missing three field goals in the preseason opener, Andy Borregales kicked well this past week on the skinny field goal posts and then on Wednesday in the joint practice — where he ended the day connecting on a 57-yard field goal to end a two-minute drive. Now returning to a game setting, all eyes will be on if Borregales, who will be back working with long snapper Julian Ashby, can bounce back.

summary: Entering their preseason game against the Philadelphia Eagles fresh off a pair of joint practices, the New England Patriots are expected to give their starters some rest. Quarterback Drake Maye and the other core players on offense and defense are “unlikely” to take the field during the Patriots-Eagles exhibition contest on Saturday night, as first […]
full_text: Aug 13, 2026; Foxborough, Massachusetts, USA; New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye (10) has a laugh with quarterback Tommy DeVito (16) before a game against the Indianapolis Colts at Gillette Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Eric Canha-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Entering their preseason game against the Philadelphia Eagles fresh off a pair of joint practices, the New England Patriots are expected to give their starters some rest. Quarterback Drake Maye and the other core players on offense and defense are “unlikely” to take the field during the Patriots-Eagles exhibition contest on Saturday night, as first reported by Mike Reiss of ESPN. This means that Maye and company will not have seen any game action through two postseason games. The Patriots’ approach nonetheless comes as no surprise considering the quantity of reps over the two joint sessions with the Eagles on Wednesday and Thursday. Maye, for example, attempted a combined 36 passes during full-team drills alone. “I think we had a lot of great work,” the 23-year-old said on Thursday. “The biggest thing is that is a good football team over there, and I think just not riding the rollercoaster. I feel like we had some good periods that we were attacking them and had some good plays. Then we had some periods where we got to continue the competitive stamina, and that is the thing about this game: it can’t just be one play here, one play there. You got to string some plays together in a row, and I felt like we did that more [Wednesday] than we did [Thursday].” With Maye not expected to take the field on Saturday, backup Tommy DeVito is again expected to start at quarterback. In last week’s preseason opener against the Colts, DeVito went 13-for-22 for 138 yards and a touchdown. The game ended in a 13-13 tie. Kickoff for the Patriots’ second preseason game against the Eagles is scheduled for 7 p.m. ET at Gillette Stadium.

title: Game Recap: Saints v. Rams Preseason week 2
summary: Following a busy week full of practices, scuffles, and injuries, the New Orleans Saints trudged into their second preseason game on Saturday when they squared off against the Los Angeles Rams. In a lopsided blowout, the Rams demolished New Orleans by a final score of 34-0. Let’s recap. First Quarter New Orleans booted the opening […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - AUGUST 22: Zach Wilson #4 of the New Orleans Saints passes during the first half in a preseason game between the New Orleans Saints and the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium on August 22, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Following a busy week full of practices, scuffles, and injuries, the New Orleans Saints trudged into their second preseason game on Saturday when they squared off against the Los Angeles Rams. In a lopsided blowout, the Rams demolished New Orleans by a final score of 34-0. Let’s recap. First Quarter New Orleans booted the opening kickoff to Los Angeles, and both sides would exchange punts on their opening possessions. However, the Rams would then methodically down the field with a 14-play drive resulting in the game’s first points, a field goal. LA was setup with a first-and-goal inside of the Saints’ ten-yard line, but a false start penalty would back the Rams up, forcing them to eventually settle for the red zone FGM. 3-0, LAR. Second Quarter The Saints’ ensuing drive would leak into the start of the second quarter- barely. On the first play in the next period, New Orleans quarterback Zach Wilson attempted to hook up with wide receiver Bub Means but instead threw an interception to Rams’ cornerback Al’zillion Hamilton. Stetson Bennett and the Rams would take advantage of the turnover as he scampered into the endzone on a play action rollout. New Orleans would turn the ball over on downs during their next series leading to another Bennett TD run. A Saints’ drive that took less than two minutes off of the clock ending in a punt would give the Rams another opportunity to score before halftime which they converted into another FGM as time expired. 20-0, Rams. Third Quarter Zach Wilson, out. Spencer Ratter, in. Result? Just about the same. New Orleans looked like it was driving with a new QB at the helm to begin the second half, but after reaching a goal-to-go distance, Rattler threw an unwarranted pass into near triple coverage resulting in a 100-yard pick-six by LA’s Alex Cook. Suddenly, 27-0. Both teams would then exchange three-and-out drives before the Saints’ third turnover of the game. On a 32-yard catch and run connection from Rattler to running back CJ Donaldson, New Orleans would retain possession after a fumble at the end of the play bounced harmlessly out of bounds. Just two plays later, Saints’ RB Ty Chandler would fumble inside of the Los Angeles five-yard-line to end the scoring threat. Fourth Quarter Los Angeles’ Ty Simpson took over QB duties in the second half of the contest and led the Rams down near the red zone in the fourth quarter before a turnover on downs of their own. New Orleans would go three-and-out once more before Rams’ RB Jarquez Hunter put the cherry on top of LA’s dominant victory, a 12-yard TD run. Penalties, sloppy play, mental mistakes, and likely some exhaustion all factored into the poor performance from the New Orleans Saints in this one, but when it’s raining, it’s pouring and anything that could go wrong did. On the Saints’ final possession of the game, Rattler took the Saints down the field on a 12-play drive setting New Orleans up with a chance to escape the shutout bid. However, K Tanner Brown sailed a 39-yard FGA wide right as New Orleans finally lost 34-0 and if anything, realized there is still not a reliable kicking option on the roster.

summary: After falling to the Jacksonville Jaguars last weekend 24-20, the New Orleans Saints turn their attention to the second preseason game opponent, Los Angeles Rams. The NFC West foe, in contrast, is coming off of a 20-12 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs. The Rams’ passing attack ranked 8th in the league during week one’s […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - AUGUST 15: Michael Heldman #63 of the New Orleans Saints runs on the field prior to a preseason game against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Caesars Superdome on August 15, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images After falling to the Jacksonville Jaguars last weekend 24-20, the New Orleans Saints turn their attention to the second preseason game opponent, Los Angeles Rams. The NFC West foe, in contrast, is coming off of a 20-12 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs. The Rams’ passing attack ranked 8th in the league during week one’s slate of games after their quarterbacks put up a combined 228 yards through the air. Meanwhile, New Orleans gave up 157 yards to Jacksonville’s QBs. On the ground, Los Angeles managed 93 yards, good for 21st overall. The Saints were not so fortunate after the Jags literally ran the tables in the second half as the defense allowed 118 rushing yards. Following a joint practice with Los Angeles gave another opportunity for the Saints to see their 1’s get valuable reps, it is expected that many starters will once more not hit the field for New Orleans during this Saturday’s preseason contest. It is likely that this weekend’s players and snap counts will look similar to a week ago as teams continue to whittle down their rosters and give those vying for depth chart moves increased opportunities to show off their skillsets. The Rams made it to the NFC Championship game last season before falling to the eventual Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Regardless of the outcome on Saturday, a matchup against another 2025 postseason squad will only prove to be beneficial for a Saints team that continues its rebuilding efforts.

title: Giants-Dolphins winners and losers: Which players helped themselves, and which did not
summary: The New York Giants had an easy time manhandling the Miami Dolphins on Saturday, winning 26-3. Let’s review the game in our traditional ‘Kudos & Wet Willies’ style. Kudos to … Darius Slayton — Recovering from double sports hernia surgery, Slayton has had a quiet summer. He had a loud first half, with four catches […]
full_text: Devin Singletary runs for a touchdown Saturday against the Miami Dolphins. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants had an easy time manhandling the Miami Dolphins on Saturday, winning 26-3. Let’s review the game in our traditional ‘Kudos & Wet Willies’ style. Kudos to … Darius Slayton — Recovering from double sports hernia surgery, Slayton has had a quiet summer. He had a loud first half, with four catches for 58 yards. He set up the Giants’ first touchdown with a 29-yard catch-and-run on a third-and-5. Jameis Winston — The Giants’ backup quarterback played the entire first half. He went 15 of 21 for 150 yards, ran for an 11-yard score, and led a nice two-minute drive for a field goal. Good work! Devin Singletary — The eighth-year running back doesn’t get anywhere in a hurry. He isn’t exactly a burner. He does, though, keep on making plays and being dependable. John Harbaugh will like both of those things. Singletary made a terrific cutback on his 13-yard touchdown run, and finished with 40 yards rushing on eight carries. Devin Singletary bounces it outside and takes it in for the @Giants TD! NYGvsMIA on @nflnetwork Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/cNcRnNMKwo — NFL (@NFL) August 22, 2026 The secondary — I made this a blanket ‘Kudos’ for many of the guys who played in the first half. Greg Newsome had a pass defensed and was aggressive in run support. Deonte Banks was excellent. He was sticky in coverage, and had two passes defensed. He also made an an excellent, aggressive run stop. That would not have happened a year ago. Tyler Nubin missed a tackle on the opening kickoff, but was solid defensively. He had a pass defensed, continuing his tendency this summer of getting his hands on the ball more often. Early Pro Football Focus grades gave him an elite 90.4 grade. Dru Phillips gave up a 30-yard catch (and committed pass interference on the play), but responded with run stops and forced fumbles on his next two plays. I can’t point to a specific play, but Paulson Adebo started and also appeared to play well. Bobby Jamison-Travis — The rookie sixth-round pick needed a game in which he made a couple of plays, and he delivered one on Saturday. He got a sack, and even showed us that there is a new No. 97 sack dance in town: New celly alert 🍽️ pic.twitter.com/26uh4LXgfp — New York Giants (@Giants) August 22, 2026 J.C. Davis — The rookie sixth-round pick went the distance at left tackle in a performance that probably solidified a spot for him on the 53-man roster. In early grades from PFF, Davis scored an 86.6, best among offensive players. Davis played 53 total snaps. In 33 pass-blocking snaps, PFF had him with just one pressure allowed. Offensive line overall — Giants’ quarterbacks were sacked only once, and there were holes for all of the backs to run through. Well, except for poor Damon Bankston and his seven carries for 5 yards at the end of the game. Dare I say that there may actually be depth on the line. The Giants must think so, since they traded Daniel Faalele a few days ago. Dalen Cambre — The second-year wide receiver/special teamer did not enter the game until the second half. When he got on the field, he made the most of it. Cambre made the tackle on the opening kickoff of the second half, and had three catches in three targets for 26 yards. More importantly, all three of Cambre’s catches resulted in first downs. On third-and-7, he caught an 8-yard pass from Brandon Allen. On third-and-8, Cambre caught a 9-yard pass from Allen. On yet another third-and-8, Cambre caught a 9-yard pass from Jake Haener. Calvin Austin — Austin had a 21-yard rush, two receptions for 24 yards, and two punt returns for 29 yards. He will help the Giants in 2026. Related coverage What did we learn from the Giants’ 26-3 win over the Miami Dolphins? Giants-Dolphins instant grades: Lopsided victory leads to high marks Giants dominate Miami Dolphins in 26-3 victory Wet Willies to … Tyrone Tracy — Two preseason games, two major gaffes for Tracy. In Week 1 against the Minensota Vikings, he missed a blitz pickup resulting in a huge hit on quarterback Jaxson Dart. On Saturday, after runs of 11 and 12 yards, an untouched Tracy fumbled away a scoring opportunity. Tracy probably also fumbled away playing time with Najee Harris on the roster, and Singletary looking spry. Did he fumble away a roster spot? The miscues are unfortunate, because Tracy can be a plus in both the run and pass games. This, though, is a new coaching staff and they will go by what they are seeing with their own eyes. Darius Alexander — The second-year defensive tackle had a quarterback hit, but his overall play left a lot to be desired. His early 33.8 PFF grade was the lowest of any Giants’ defender. Alexander has been in both preseason games in the third quarter, and it is mostly because the Giants need better run defense from the 2025 third-round pick. There is a reason why Chauncey Golston has been starting on the defensive line. Maybe I was also influenced by the number of times Carl Banks spoke during the broadcast about Alexander needing to give the Giants more. Kwillies to … Odell Beckham Jr. — While fans, and even Harbaugh, are rooting for Beckham, his chance of making the season-opening 53-man roster remains murky. Yes, he can still get open. Yes, he had a 12-yard catch. Two catches for 17 yards and a dropped touchdown pass aren’t going to cut it, though. Not when the wide receiver room is as deep as it is, and other guys are making plays. You just can’t miss chances to make impact plays when you are fighting for a roster spot.

title: What did we learn from the Giants’ 26-3 win over the Miami Dolphins?
summary: We’re all just happy to be watching football again, but we can’t help but try to parse the results of the New York Giants’ preseason games for what they mean for the upcoming regular season. Here are Pro Football Focus’ top seven NFL teams after the three 2025 preseason games: Yes, your 3-0 New York […]
full_text: Devin Singletary carries the ball on Saturday. | Getty Images We’re all just happy to be watching football again, but we can’t help but try to parse the results of the New York Giants’ preseason games for what they mean for the upcoming regular season. Here are Pro Football Focus’ top seven NFL teams after the three 2025 preseason games: Yes, your 3-0 New York Football Giants were PFF’s top-ranked team in the 2025 preseason. It made sense based on a victory on the road over Super Bowl contender Buffalo, plus a blowout 31-12 win over the Jets and an an even bigger 42-10 stomping of the woeful Patriots, who did little in Drake Maye’s rookie season. Russell Wilson, Jameis Winston, and Jaxson Dart gave the Giants their best quarterback room in ages, and No. 3 draft pick Abdul Carter was going to make an already strong Giants pass rush even stronger. The regular season didn’t quite turn out that way for the Giants. Not for the Patriots, either. The preseason performance rankings did have some merit otherwise – Super Bowl Champion Seattle and NFL Championship Game losers Denver and Los Angeles were right there in the top seven as well, as was Chicago, who took a big step forward in Caleb Williams’ sophomore season and gave the Rams all they could handle. John Harbaugh’s perennial playoff Ravens team was no surprise in the No. 2 preseason spot, but things didn’t turn out so well for Harbaugh’s team once the games counted. So there’s not really a lot we can tell from preseason games other than which players’ stock might be rising or falling as cutdowns loom in the fairly near future. Many of the Giants’ starters did not play in tonight’s rain-soaked game against the Miami Dolphins. On top of that, the Dolphins are undergoing a major rebuild, and their few recognizable starters played little or not at all either. As a result the Giants dominated this game from start to finish, but without making any of their roster decisions any clearer. Let’s try to read the tea leaves to the extent we can, though. The running back depth chart is interesting Cam Skattebo, who was in a rotation with Tyrone Tracy last year before getting hurt, is pretty clearly the lead running back now. The question is what the depth chart is behind him. Skattebo did not play against Miami. Tracy did, and he promptly coughed up the ball untouched when he tried to switch it to his other hand before hitting the line. In isolation that wouldn’t matter much, but Tracy has developed a reputation for fumbling when hit, so an unforced error like this is magnified. On the other hand, Devin Singletary, who seemed to become No. 3 on the depth chart last year after the emergence of Skattebo, gained 40 yards on eight carries, including one from the Miami 13 in which he hit the right side of the line, saw no hole, and bounced it outside, and he was quick enough to get around the corner and take it in for a TD. In the second half, the usually forgotten 2023 draft pick Eric Gray tried the same thing, but he did not have the quickness to get upfield. (Gray did have 37 receiving yards on 6 catches.) Singletary was a prime cut candidate entering 2026 but he agreed to take a cut from $6.5M to $2.845M, some of that in incentives. Especially with Najee Harris (who did not play) now in the fold, it will be interesting to see whether Harbaugh and Greg Roman prefer the more explosive but more erratic Tracy to the more reliable but less spectacular Singletary, and whether the more powerful Harris can displace any of them when final cuts are made. The defense up front is better…I guess With exciting running back De’Von Achane, one of Miami’s few remaining blue chip players, not playing, starting quarterback Malik Willis sitting as well, and Jayden Waddle gone, the Dolphins’ offense posed little threat to the Giants’ defense. That said, other than a couple of 9-yard sprints up the middle by starting quarterback Cam Miller to escape the pass rush, the Dolphins’ run game did little, accumulating only 32 yards on 16 rushes. There were few holes in the middle of the line for them to run through. The most notable players in the interior were Zacch Pickens (2 tackles for -6 yards) and draftee Bobby Jamison-Travis (1 tackle for -3 yards), each of whom had a sack as well. Are 2024 Dru Phillips and Tyler Nubin back? In 2023 rookie first-round pick Deonte Banks showed some promise as a man cover cornerback who would contest catches. That Banks disappeared in 2024 and 2025, but he was active again today contesting catches. The even bigger mystery was 2024 third round pick Dru Phillips, who impressed as a rookie when playing close to the line but who clearly regressed in his second season as opponents started to expose him in the passing game. Second round 2024 pick Tyler Nubin was less impressive as a rookie but was awful in 2025. Both played better Saturday, with three tackles apiece. Phillips was beaten on one pass play but he was actually in good position, and he forced two fumbles. OBJ’s future is still up in the air Quarterback Jameis Winston tried to get the ball to Odell Beckham Jr. when he entered the game, targeting him four times. One one play OBJ made the catch and then put a nice move on the defensive back to get more yards and a first down. That play had the look of a player you want on the team. Then a little later, Winston found OBJ in the back of the end zone for a leaping catch and a TD … except that Beckham let the ball go through his hands. At this point, I think it’s fair to say that Beckham can still get open against NFL defensive backs. There was another play on which he went downfield and seemed to beat his man but was not thrown to. Whether this will be enough to get him a place on the 53 remains to be seen. Of note is that Darius Slayton, who’d been invisible last week, caught four balls in six targets for 58 yards, leading the Giants. Calvin Austin had two catches in two targets for 24 yards. How the wide receiver depth chart is going to play out after Malik Nabers and Malachi Fields is anyone’s guess at this point.
author: Anthony Del Genio

title: Giants-Dolphins instant grades: Lopsided victory leads to high marks
summary: The New York Giants beat up on the Miami Dolphins on Saturday in a one-sided 26-3 victory. It was clear from the joint practice that the Giants were a superior roster; reports from practice suggested that the Giants’ defense destroyed the first-team Miami offense — a first-team Miami offense that mostly rested in this preseason […]
full_text: Miami running back Ollie Gordon is tackled by two Giants defenders. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Giants beat up on the Miami Dolphins on Saturday in a one-sided 26-3 victory. It was clear from the joint practice that the Giants were a superior roster; reports from practice suggested that the Giants’ defense destroyed the first-team Miami offense — a first-team Miami offense that mostly rested in this preseason game. New York rested most of their players, other than some presumed starters who did not play in preseason Week 1: Greg Newsome II, Paulson Adebo, Dru Phillips, and John Michael Schmitz. The Giants defense smothered Miami’s offense, which was led by quarterbacks Cam Miller and Mark Gronowski. Miami barely eclipsed 100 total yards, as the Giants controlled the air and ground. But of course, Miami’s roster is devoid of proven talent, and they rested their starters. Still, it was nice to see New York have a dominating win for a change — it’s an uncommon experience of late for the Giants. New York had 393 total yards, as both of their trenches dominated. These grades will be positive — let’s hope that energy is maintained when the regular season rolls around. Quarterback Jameis Winston is a pro’s pro and comported himself well. He finished 15 of 21 for 150 yards with an 11-yard rushing touchdown. Brandon Allen relieved Winston in the second-half; he converted a first down but quickly suffered a sack that resulted in an eventual punt. Allen missed a pair of open receivers, and was fairly conservative. He did complete 13 of 18 passes for 101 yards. Overall, Allen played better than he did last week, but he still missed plays. Jake Haener, whom the Giants signed earlier this week, played the final seven minutes of the game and mostly handed the ball to Eric Gray. Grade: B+ Running Back Tyrone Tracy Jr. started the game behind Devin Singletary, but the third-year back quickly found his rhythm. He ripped off two runs of 10-plus yards and helped the Giants move into the red zone. Unfortunately, wet conditions contributed to a fumble by Tracy Jr., giving the ball away deep in enemy territory with a chance to extend the lead to two scores — a mistake that will never sit well with the coaching staff. Still, it’s worth noting that Tracy was running effectively before the turnover. Tracy had a positive blitz pickup, but also whiffed on one with 32 seconds left in the first half. Singletary ran decisively and found holes on under center runs. He looked good and capped off a drive with a 13-yard touchdown run: The #Giants are owning the point of attack against the Dolphins. Devin Singletary capitalized by bouncing the run outside for the 13 yard touchdown scamper. pic.twitter.com/O5SQxmHf0k — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) August 22, 2026 Singletary finished with eight carries for 40 yards with a touchdown and one catch for four yards. Tracy Jr. had six carries for 26 yards ( 4.3 YPC ) with three catches for 22 yards. Eric Gray and Damon Bankston took most of the second-half snaps at the running back position. Gray did have 10 carries for 33 yards with six catches for 37 yards. Grade: B + Wide Receiver Odell Beckham Jr. had a 12-yard comeback and also drew a pass interference with the Giants driving down the field in the final minute of the first half. Beckham had a drop in the end zone at the end of the first half that left four points on the board after Dominic Zvada’s field goal. It wasn’t the easiest play, but one that Beckham should have made. Calvin Austin III was quick and effective underneath. He caught a quick pass and took it 20 yards, and he also had another catch for four yards, while adding 21 yards on a jet sweep that easily gained the edge. Darius Slayton caught four of his six targets for 58 yards and was routinely getting open over the middle of the field. Dalen Cambre caught a few passes from Allen and Haener late in the game, as he continues to fight for a roster spot, primarily as a special teamer. Overall, the wide receivers didn’t have a massive impact, but it was great to see Slayton be effective, and it was evident that Austin III will have a role in the offensive 11 personnel package. Grade: B- Tight End The tight ends weren’t super involved in the passing attack. Chris Manhertz had a 22 personnel play-action shot designed toward him in the red zone, but it went incomplete. Theo Johnson caught a pass for 12 yards from Winston. Tanner Conner dropped a third-down pass but did secure one pass for 7 yards. Thomas Fidone II had four catches for 29 yards. Grade: B- Offensive Line The Giants owned the point of attack and kept Winston clean throughout the first half. Marcus Mbow continued to impress at tackle, and Josh Ezeudu, as well as Evan Neal, did well run blocking. The first-, second-, and third- team offenses generated good push up front. The Giants rushed for 135 yards in the game. The “ Greg Roman Effect” is creating a physical atmosphere, as players from the previous regime seem to be dictating more on the line of scrimmage, but AGAIN, this is a Miami Dolphins roster that is thin. Grade: A Defensive Line Bobby Jamison-Travis earned a sack in the first quarter of the game to force a second-and-13. Zacch Pickens also earned a sack and had his name called a few times for holding the point of attack and playing well in the run game. Darius Alexander played into the second half, once again, and he almost came away with a safety early in the third quarter. His power-rushing ability is impressive. Marlon Davidson continued his strong preseason with a pass deflection in the third quarter, as Pickens pushed the pocket. The depth on the defensive line played well against Miami. Grade: A- Edge Brian Burns, Abdul Carter, and Kayvon Thibodeaux did not dress in this game, leaving Chauncy Gholston as the number one edge defender. His presence was felt; his long arms were in passing lanes and he made one tackle near the line of scrimmage. Trace Ford displayed heavy hands and made a few impressive plays at the line of scrimmage against the run. Ford also earned a sack on a muffed snap by Miami. Grade: B+ Linebacker Arvell Reese was on the field early in the game, but left after the second series. He blew up a fullback on an iso run that was consistent with many of his physical plays from preseason Week 1. It was Micah McFadden who took many of the early snaps. McFadden played well, earning an early half-sack, and he recovered Phillips’ forced fumble in the first quarter. Zaire Barnes sniffed out a second-and-15 screen. Both Caleb Murphy and Jack Kelly flashed. Both are in direct competition with Darius Muasau to make the roster, and Muasau didn’t see the field until the threes buckled their helmets. Murphy finished with three tackles and looked physical. Grade: A+ Cornerback Greg Newsome II did not dress in preseason Week 1, but his presence was felt early on Saturday against the Dolphins. Newsome II made an impressive run stop at the line of scrimmage on the Dolphins’ first drive, and then knocked a crossing route down on the subsequent play. Newsome II also did an excellent job blowing up an end-around; he kept leverage to the outside and hit the back out of bounds. Dru Phillips did not fare so well initially; he took a defensive pass interference penalty while surrendering the catch to Kevin Coleman Jr. Phillips, however, did bounce back strong with two physical plays, including a forced fumble. I love how Dru Phillips responded to the slot-fade he surrendered. Phillips with back-to-back impact plays to shut down the Dolphins offense. Phillips' physical nature is one thing that can't be denied. pic.twitter.com/cgUPWZmk9E — Nick Falato (@nickfalato) August 22, 2026 Starter Paulson Adebo saw action and kept his positive trajectory from his performance in the joint practice. Overall, the Giants’ cornerbacks were sticky in coverage and surrendered little space. The defense, in general, dominated Miami’s offense. Grade: A+ Safety…

title: Survey results: Giants fans split on the status of Malik Nabers
summary: One of the biggest stories hanging over the New York Giants off-season has been the status of wide receiver Malik Nabers. Nabers tore his ACL early in the Giants’ victory over the Los Angeles Chargers, also suffering meniscus damage in the process. Nabers tore his ACL on September 28th, but wasn’t able to have surgery […]
full_text: Malik Nabers | Getty Images One of the biggest stories hanging over the New York Giants off-season has been the status of wide receiver Malik Nabers. Nabers tore his ACL early in the Giants’ victory over the Los Angeles Chargers, also suffering meniscus damage in the process. Nabers tore his ACL on September 28th, but wasn’t able to have surgery until a month later on October 28th. Concerns were raised again in the off-season when it was reported that he had a second “clean-up” procedure, with fans and the media wondering if he would be available to start the season. So it was a bit of a surprise when Nabers not only avoided the PUP list to start training camp, but started taking part in individual drills on the first day. He was a regular participant in individual drills for the first two weeks of camp, with those in attendance consistently reporting that he looked good doing so. Nabers graduated to taking part in team drills — albeit in a red “no contact” jersey — this past week. In light of his progress, we wanted to ask fans if Nabers taking part in team periods made fans more confident that he would be available for Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys. Most fans think he will be, but the fanbase as a whole doesn’t exactly seem to be brimming with confidence. We’ve had nothing but positive reviews of Nabers in practice and he has been a regular participant. His intensity has ramped up, and his body seems to have responded well, so it’s a bit of a surprise that a third of the fanbase still doesn’t expect him to be ready for Week 1 against the Dallas Cowboys. Granted, there’s a difference between running routes on air, practicing one-on-one against your teammates, or participating in team periods while the defense can’t (or at least shouldn’t) touch you. As head coach John Harbaugh said about Nabers, “He won’t go through the rest of the summer in a red jersey,” Harbaugh said. “No, he’ll be out of a red jersey before he plays in a game. He’s going to have to get bumped around and hit and fronted up so he knows how to, you just have to feel that and know how to deal with it to protect yourself.” Nabers’ progress thus far has to be encouraging, and the Giants have to hope that he’ll be available for Week 1 against the Cowboys. Jaxson Dart has quickly forged a connection with Isaiah Likely, while Calvin Austin III and Malachi Fields have performed well. Likewise, the Giants’ running game is intriguing with the addition of Najee Harris as well as Sisi Mauigoa playing well at right guard. But much like the Giants’ teams of a decade ago: The offense is significantly scarier with the star receiver from LSU than without him. The Giants are currently 2.5-point underdogs in Week 1 against the Cowboys (per FanDuel ), and their best chance of an upset comes with Nabers on the field.

title: Baltimore Ravens players take swipe at NY Giants coach John Harbaugh
summary: Two veteran Baltimore Ravens players recently took obvious swipes at former head coach John Harbaugh, now with the New York Giants, while praising first-year coach Jesse Minter. Wide receiver Rashod Bateman and offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley never mentioned Harbaugh by name, but ti was clear they believe more in what they are getting Minter and […]
full_text: John Harbaugh | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Two veteran Baltimore Ravens players recently took obvious swipes at former head coach John Harbaugh , now with the New York Giants, while praising first-year coach Jesse Minter. Wide receiver Rashod Bateman and offensive tackle Ronnie Stanley never mentioned Harbaugh by name, but ti was clear they believe more in what they are getting Minter and his coach staff than what got from Harbaugh. “From head coach to OC to receivers coach, everybody really harps on the details and the small things, and that’s just not what we were in our past,” Bateman said. “I think, right now, we’re learning how to play fast, smart football. Trusting the training, trusting the call, trusting our teammates. That’s the difference right now, honestly.” Bateman described the Ravens’ coaching staff as very “communicative, talkative and informative,” and “that’s what we never had here.” Stanley agreed, adding that Minter “just values details and the finer details a little bit more. I think that is something that is very much harped on, and he is also a very positive overall guy. He realizes we are chasing perfection, but that is something that is going to come with a lot of bad plays (and) bad days, and he is aware of that.” Really? Perhaps this is simply an example of how a message, no matter how well delivered, can simply grow stale after 18 years. Several former Ravens — fullback Patrick Ricard, tight end Isaiah Likely, defensive back Ar’Darius Washington, punter Jordan Stout, defensive tackle Josh Tupou — followed Harbaugh from Baltimore. Ricard’s admiration for Harbaugh was obvious when he was introduced to media after signing with the Giants. “I’m just very grateful for Coach Harbaugh,” Ricard said. “I mean, he’s been in my corner my whole career. He’s believed in me. And as soon as I saw he got the job here, I was definitely interested. I even told him, like, look, if you were coaching a Pop Warner football team, I’m interested. I’m there doing something. I don’t even know if I’m like the water boy, you know what I’m saying?” The Giants, who have practiced as long and hard as the rules allow since the spring, would probably beg to differ on the idea that Harbaugh doesn’t communicate or harp on the details and the smaller things. After Thursday’s joint practice with the Miami Dolphins in the intense Florida heat, Giants edge defender Brian Burns said the way the Giants have practiced allowed them to hold up in the searingly hot conditions. “I ain’t gonna lie, if we didn’t practice as hard as we do, I don’t know if we would have made it through this heat,” Burns said. “And the level of competition that we practiced with today. But I feel like us practicing as hard as we do, definitely prepared us for all of this.” From what media has been able to see, Harbaugh is a stickler for the details and the smaller things. Players have also praised his openness, messaging, and communication skills. Remember Kayvon Thibodeaux calling Harbaugh “a maniac”? “Coach Harbaugh – I think he’s a maniac, he’s obsessed. I love it,” Thibodeaux said. “He’s so great at explaining things that of course he looks at a guy like me like how could you ask so many questions, you know. But we always talk about like someone who questions, it’s not like they’re challenging, we just want to make sure we have the best understanding of how to execute at the highest level. I think, man, this is the best I’ve felt coming into a new year.” Maybe the simple reality is that, at least for some players who had been around Harbaugh for a long time, change was the best thing. Maybe for Harbaugh, as well.
author: Ed Valentine

title: New York Giants mailbag: Jaxson Dart, Najee Harris’s role, Odell’s number, more
summary: Peter Duhamel asks: In your post-game analysis you opined that removing Dart for a blue tent evaluation “was the right call,” noting that he “lay on the field for several nerve-wracking seconds before getting to his feet. Checking him was the right decision.” As I understand it, mid-game medical evaluations are mandated for potential concussion […]
full_text: Peter Duhamel asks: In your post-game analysis you opined that removing Dart for a blue tent evaluation “was the right call,” noting that he “lay on the field for several nerve-wracking seconds before getting to his feet. Checking him was the right decision.” As I understand it, mid-game medical evaluations are mandated for potential concussion or orthopedic injuries. Dart, however, was hit in the mid-section and as he himself explained, he got the wind knocked out of him. Even Coach Harbaugh on the sidelines was not concerned. I don’t understand your characterization of his recovery as being “nerve wracking” nor your conclusion that removing him from the game was “the right decision.” Please explain so I can better understand. Thank you. Ed says: Peter, let’s first clarify that that John Harbaugh said that he was not concerned about sending Dart back into the game AFTER he was checked for a concussion, and after checking with the player. I will always say erring on the side of caution by checking a player for a concussion if upstairs spotters or on field officials have any concern is the right thing to do. It was 100% the right decision. Player health and safety should be paramount. In this case, Dart took a massive hit and laid motionless on the field for a few seconds before rolling over and getting up. Could anyone be sure whether he did or did not slam his head to the turf when he went down? No. Of course it was “nerve wracking.” The starting quarterback, the future of the franchise, was laying on the ground after taking a huge hit in the firist quarter of the first preseason game. Concussion? Broken ribs? I would be surprised if most Giants fans didn’t think “oh, bleep” when they saw Dart on the ground. I don’t know how anyone could not have been concerned. Ray Kochert asks: Do you think that the signing of Najee Harris is because John Harbaugh is not sure of the current running backs being able to pass block or pick up blitzers? Especially on 3rd down. Ed says: No, Ray, I don’t think that is the reason. I understand the belief because it comes on the heels of the Tyrone Tracy missed block in the preseason game against the Minnesota Vikings, but that’s not it. I saw Ryan Dunleavy of the New York Post say on ‘X’ that he believes John Harbaugh and the Giants “liked’ their running back room, but did not ”love” it. I think that is 100% accurate. Remember, the Giants seriously investigated the price tag for Kenneth Walker in free agency. The Giants looked hard at the possibility of drafting Jeremiyah Love. Many well-placed analysts believe they would have if Love had been available to them at No. 5. As much as Harbaugh loves the running game, I don’t believe that was just smoke. Cam Skattebo is insanely popular, but his talent and production don’t match the hype. He can get tough yards, but he isn’t going to make big, explosive, chunk plays. Tracy is a good, but not close to great, back. Devin Singletary is dependable, but he isn’t a guy who you want to build a ground game around. I believe the Giants have been looking for a way to upgrade the play-making ability at that position. Harris has four 1,000-yard seasons, and was hurt the only year he didn’t reach that mark. He is the most accomplished back the Giants have. Skattebo fans are going to want to crucify me for this, but if he is healthy and is the same player he was pre-injury, Harris will be the Giants’ best back by season’s end. That is why the Giants added Harris. Brayden Martell asks: Will Odell Beckham Jr. get his number 13 back? Ed says: Brayden, the better, more important question is whether or not Beckham will make the team. Right now, I think that’s a 50-50 proposition. I might even trend toward saying I think it could be difficult for him to make the 53-man roster. If everyone is healthy Malik Nabers, Malachi Fields, Darnell Mooney, Darius Slayton, Calvin Austin, and Braxton Berrios are making the team. That’s six guys. NFL teams often keep only six wide receivers. If the Giants keep a seventh wide receiver, there is an argument to be made that Dalen Cambre might have more value on game days than Beckham because he can be a core special teams player. So, before you worry about Beckham’s jersey number, worry about whether or not he is going to get a jersey at all. Michael Schack asks: With kicker issues we have had under Daboll, I am left wondering what is the plan for a backup kicker for the Giants? Harbaugh seems like someone who has a plan for everything. I looked back at Giants history and the last non-kicker day-game active on roster player who backed up as kicker (other than Feagles and Gillan, and Gillan was highly questionable, while my memory of Feagles was he was much better than Gillan) was Brad Van Pelt (a personal favorite player of mine), and before that Frank Gifford. Yes, we could try to sneak Sauls to practice squad, but that does not address the emergency game day situation. Is there anyone on the Giants potential 53 (or certain to be active game day) capable of being the emergency kicker? Does Harbaugh have a plan? And while I am at it, same question for long snapper, because we know the intricacies of placekicking includes a competent long snapper. Ed says: Michael, as much as teams might want to they simply cannot cover every possibility when it comes to roster management. This isn’t college, where teams can have a roster of 105 players. They get 53. On game days, if you elevate two practice squad players, the most you can dress is 48. Teams don’t carry extra punters or placekickers on their active rosters. It just isn’t practical on a weekly basis because it leaves you short elesewhere. In emergency in-game situations, the punters and placekickers generally cover for each other. I know that punter Jordan Stout has experience kicking off. What happened with the Giants and Graham Gano the last few seasons was unusual. The mistake really wasn’t in roster construction, it was a couple of times when they knew Gano wasn’t 100% and they left themselves unprotected on game days. It is the same with a long snapper. Nobody can carry a second “dedicated” long snapper. I honestly don’t know who the emergency snapper would be. I would think Harbaugh does. Bob Donnelly asks: During the third quarter of the preseason game vs Minnesota Joe Schoen visited the broadcast booth. He discussed roster refinement as an ongoing process and that he was in contact with other GMs discussing the surplus of talent at some positions and desire to upgrade at others. The Faalele trade was no doubt the product of those discussions. This leads me to the question: Do you think that there will be another trade like Faalele‘s before the cutdown, and if so will the Giants be buyers or sellers. Ed says: Bob, I think a deal or deals “could” happen. I also think the Giants could be on either end, buying or selling. I keep saying this, but I won’t say deals are “likely”. There will be almost 1,200 players cut after the third preseason game. Teams will be able to help their rosters at that point without giving up assets, which lessens the trade market. Still, desperation to fill a specific need can lead to deals. Could the Giants trade a wide receiver like Darnell Mooney to open a spot for, say, Odell Beckham Jr.? Maybe. Could they target, say, an interior defensive lineman and send back a late-round pick? Perhaps. Could they swing big at cornerback and make offers to the Pittsburgh Steelers for Joey Porter Jr. or the New England Patriots for Christian Gonzalez? I don’t see it happening, but it doesn’t hurt to ask. Donald Poucher asks: Ed, just looking for your opinion…we often see suggestions that we trade middle to bottle tier roster players for day 3 picks, e.g Slayton for a 6. Every team has these players. Why don’t we see trades of players with value where we have depth, to teams who have a similar situation at a different position? As an example I heard Patty T point out the Seahawks have an…
